item.name: Getting started
Access and authentication

request.description:
## OAuth Token Request

This endpoint is used to obtain an access token for authentication purposes. It accepts a POST request to the URL `{{authRoute}}/oauth/token` with the necessary credentials provided in the request body.

#### Token lifespan

Access tokens are valid for up to 2 hours. To ensure efficient use of resources and maintain optimal system performance, we kindly ask that firms reuse the access token during its validity period rather than requesting a new token for each API call.

### Request Method

- **POST**
    

### Request Parameters

The request must include the following parameters in the `x-www-form-urlencoded` format:

- **grant_type** (text): The type of grant being requested (e.g., authorization_code, password).
    
- **client_id** (text): The unique identifier for the client making the request.
    
- **client_secret** (text): The secret key associated with the client ID.
    
- **audience** (text): The intended audience for the token, usually the API that the client wants to access.
    

### Expected Response Format

Upon successful authentication, the server responds with a JSON object containing the following fields:

- **access_token**: The token that can be used to authenticate subsequent requests.
    
- **scope**: The scope of access granted by the token.
    
- **expires_in**: The duration in seconds for which the token is valid.
    
- **token_type**: The type of token issued (typically "Bearer").
    

Make sure to handle the response appropriately to utilise the access token in your application.

This flow returns an API token that should be used in all subsequent calls to Seccl's API in the `api-token` header field.

API tokens generated by `Machine` users will expire after two hours of inactivity. API tokens generated by `User` users expire after ten minutes of inactivity and should only be used for the users accessing Seccl's services via the off-the-shelf user interfaces.

#### Parameters

---

`firmId` string **Required**

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`id` string **Required**

The unique identifier of your user or the email address of your user

---

`password` string **Required**

The secret password

---

This action creates a new password using the access token.

item.description:
#### Logging into Seccl's API

_**We're upgrading our Authentication to utilise**_ [Okta/Auth0](https://desktop.postman.com/?desktopVersion=10.15.0&webVersion=10.15.9-ui-230717-0642&userId=6135008&teamId=604381)_**, read more below...**_

Here at Seccl, we take the security of our API seriously. Here's how you can gain access...

Firstly, we will use an API token (a small, device-specific piece of code otherwise known as an access token) to authenticate requests and grant you access to our API.

Your API login details carry many privileges, so be sure to keep them safe! Do not share your login details in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code.

All API requests must be made over Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure ([HTTPS](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_Secure)), which is typically used for secure communication over a computer network. Calls made over plain HTTP will fail. API requests without authentication will also fail.

We will provide the details to allow you to set your password.

**Please note: We do not provide authentication services to end clients – this should be managed by your application.**

This flow will allow you to generate a token to:

- Log into the API
    
- Set your password
    
- Reset your password
    
- Change your password
    

**Authentication Upgrade**

You can continue to use our existing `/authenticate` endpoint within your `{{apiRoute}}`.

However, we're deprecating this in favour of an [OAuth 2.0](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/protocols/oauth) endpoint within your `{{authRoute}}`. This `authRoute` represents the specific Okta/Auth0 instance for your firm/environment combination. For example `https://seccl-staging-{{firmId}}.uk.auth0.com`.

As you onboard with our new authentication pattern, we'll provision:

- Okta/Auth0 Instance - providing the `authRoute`
    
- Machine to Machine Client - providing the `clientId` and `clientSecret`
    

These are then used within the new `/oauth/token` endpoint.

item.name: Errors
item.description:
#### HTTP errors

Seccl uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request.

You can see a full summary of the status codes below, but as a general rule:

- Codes in the `2xx` range mean a successful API request
- Codes in the `4xx` range indicate an error that failed due to the information provided
- Codes in the `5xx` range indicate an error with Seccl's server (these are rare!)
- Some `4xx` errors can be handled through programming – for example, an error code that briefly explains the error reported
    

| **Status code** | **Summary** |
| --- | --- |
| `200` - OK | Everything worked as expected |
| `400` - Bad request | The request could not be accepted |
| `403` - Forbidden | The API key doesn't have the permissions to perform the request |
| `404` - Not found | The requested resource doesn't exist |
| `409` - Conflict | The request cannot be processed because of an idempotency conflict |
| `419` - Session expired | The API key has expired due to inactivity |
| `500` - Internal server error | Something went wrong on our end |

#### Asynchronous exceptions

Asynchronous (async) exceptions are errors caused by the function or events beyond the control of the API instruction.

These errors have occurred in the system and require intervention to investigate and action.

In general, async exceptions relate to information that was entered incorrectly or issues with requests that were sent to a processing queue and therefore not immediately rejected.

You can find further information on viewing and managing async exceptions in the **Notifications** section.

item.name: Idempotency

request.description: Using this command, you can create an idempotency key.

item.description:
## Overview

To ensure **safe retry mechanisms** and **prevent duplicate operations**, our API supports **idempotency keys**. This allows clients to safely retry requests without accidentally performing the same action multiple times.

## When to Use Idempotency

Use idempotency keys for **any request that creates or modifies data**, such as:

- **Payment transactions**
    
- **Account creations**
    
- **Order processing**
    

Idempotency is **not required** for **GET requests** since they do not modify data.

## How It Works

1. **Include an** **`idempotency-key`** **in the request headers.**
    
2. **Send the request as usual.**
    
3. **If the request completes successfully,** the response is cached.
    
4. **If the same request is sent again with the same key:**
    
    1. if the requesst has completed, the original status code and response are returned.
        
    2. if the request has not yet completed, a `202 Processing` response is returned
        
5. **If the request fails before completion (e.g., network issue),** you can retry with the same key.
    
6. **If the request body changes but the key remains the same,** a `422 Unprocessable Entity` error is returned.
    

### Important Notes

- **The** **`idempotency-key`** **must be unique, regardless of action.** Once a key has been used, it cannot be reused for any request within 72 hours.
    
- **Idempotency keys apply to all API paths.** A `POST /client` request with key `123` is treated the same as a `POST /portfoliotransactiongroup` request with the same key.
    
- **Idempotency keys expire** afte 72 hours, after which a new request with the same key will be processed as new.
    
- **Changing the request body** for the same key results in a `422 Unprocessable Entity` error.
    
- If a request returns a 4xx error, the request can be retried with the same idempotency key as long as the body remains unchanged.
    

## Handling Errors

- **422 Unprocessable Entity**: If the request body changes but the idempotency key remains the same, this error is returned.
    

## Best Practices

✅ **UUIDv4 is recommended** for idempotency keys to ensure uniqueness.

✅ **Store keys on the client-side** to retry failed requests when necessary.

✅ **Generate a new key** for every unique request that modifies data.

## Summary

- **Idempotency keys** prevent duplicate operations by caching successful responses.
    
- **Clients must provide a unique** `idempotency-key` in the request header.
    
- **Retries with the same key return the original status code and response instead of processing the request again**.
    
- **Changing the request body for the same key will result in a** **`422 Unprocessable Entity`** **error.**
    
- **Idempotency keys must be unique, regardless of action.**
    

By following these guidelines, you can ensure safe and predictable interactions with our API.

item.name: Pagination
item.description:
All API resources support bulk fetches via "list" API methods. For example, you can list clients, investment accounts, assets and transactions.

When the list of returned items gets too long, Seccl's API provides **pagination** to retrieve the items in batches.

You can use the metadata at the bottom of the response to retrieve the number of items available for that API request. For example:

``` json
"meta": {
        "count": 200
    }

```

#### Query parameters

* * *

`page` integer

The page number of the call

* * *

`pageSize` integer

The number of items per page. We recommend setting the maximum to 100

* * *

#### Welcome to Seccl's API reference

Hello and welcome! 👋

In this section, we'll cover:

- Access and authentication
    
- Errors
    
- Idempotency
    
- Pagination
    
- Release notes
    

Before getting started, you'll need access to your sandbox environment. This will authenticate your firm's user account and allow you to generate an authentication token (so you can log in!).

##### First, a couple of things you need to know...

Our API is organised around REST (Representational State Transfer), which is a particular software architectural style. You can read [more about REST here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer).

Our API uses predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts form-encoded request bodies and returns JSON-encoded responses. It also uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication and verbs.

You can use the Seccl API in test mode, which doesn't affect your live data or interact with other partners. The API route you use determines whether the request is in live mode or test mode.

##### A note on the docs structure

The structure of the API docs aims to mirror the flow of a new investor signing-up to the investment platform – from creating a client account, to investing money and viewing the portfolio balance.

- Platform management: Setting up your platform, including operational users, assets, fees and exception monitoring
    
- Client onboarding: Creating a new client on your platform
    
- Investment accounts: Creating a new investment account for your client (e.g. an ISA, GIA, or pension, etc.)
    
- Investment strategies: Assigning how the investor's money is invested (e.g. selecting a model portfolio or individual asset)
    
- Payment methods: Collecting money from the investor's account and allocating it to their investment account
    
- Balances and valuations: Retrieving a summary of investor's holdings on the platform
    
- Transfers: Instructing a product transfer of cash or assets from one platform to your platform
    
- Withdrawals: Instructing a withdrawal (single or regular) from the investor's investment account
    
- Internal cash movements: Moving cash from one investment account to another investment account within the investor's portfolio
    
- Client reporting: Retrieving important regulatory platform documents for your investor
    

##### Just getting started?

If you're new to APIs (or need a brief re-introduction), you can check out our **Quickstart** development guide in the next section.

item.name: Transfers
Create a payUK transfer in

request.description:
### Search for Pay.UK-supported ceding providers

The query parameter `supportsPayUk` can be used to retrieve a list of ceding providers that support Pay.UK or vice versa.

| supportsPayUk value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `True` | Returns only masterparties where at least one transfer provider wrapper has `supportsPayUk` set to true. |
| `False` | Returns masterparties where `supportsPayUk` is false or not defined on any transfer provider wrapper. |
| _(omitted)_ | Returns all masterparties matching the rest of the query, regardless of Pay.UK support. |

---

#### Pay.UK-specific Attributes

`transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.supportsPayUk` boolean

Indicates whether the ceding provider supports Pay.UK transfers for the given wrapper type (e.g. ISA). When true, the provider can accept Pay.UK transfer-in instructions.

**Note**: The supportsPayUK field is located within each wrapper type object under transferProviders, alongside existing fields such as cashSupported and inSpecieSupported. For example:

``` json
            "transferProviders": [
                {
                    "transferProviderName": "ATG",
                    "providerReference": "PAYUK01",
                    "ISA": {
                        "cashSupported": true,
                        "inSpecieSupported": false,
                        "supportsPayUk": true
                    },
                    "JISA": {
                        "cashSupported": true,
                        "inSpecieSupported": false,
                        "supportsPayUk": false
                    }
                }
            ],

 ```

---

`transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.accountReferenceHint` string

This is used to indicate what the accountDesignation should look like

---

## Portfolio Transaction Group API - Submit a cash ISA transfer-in request via Pay.UK. The request must include a `payUkDetails` object containing the account identification details for the ceding provider. - The `previousProvider` must reference a masterparty that supports Pay.UK (i.e. `supportsPayUk: true` on the relevant wrapper type). Submitting `payUkDetails` against a non-Pay.UK masterparty will result in a validation error. - **Important:** The `earlyClosureWaiver` field is always required. It indicates whether the client consents to potential early closure charges applied by the ceding provider. ### HTTP Method `POST` ### Endpoint `{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransactiongroup` ### Request Body The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters: - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction. - accountId (string): The identifier for the account related to the transaction. - transactions (array): An array of transaction objects, each containing: - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm related to the transaction. - transactionType (string): The type of transaction (e.g., "Product Transfer"). - transactionSubType (string): The subtype of the transaction (e.g., "Cash"). - movementType (string): Indicates the direction of the transaction (e.g., "In"). - accountId (string): The identifier for the account involved in the transaction. - transferAccountAddress (object): An object containing the address details for the transfer account: - flatNumber (string): The flat number of the address. - buildingNumber (string): The building number of the address. - address1 (string): The first line of the address. - address2 (string): The second line of the address. - country (string): The country code (e.g., "GB"). - postCode (string): The postal code. - **previousProvider** (string): The identifier for the previous provider — the masterparty _**which supports Pay.UK**_. - **previousProviderRef** (string): A reference for the transfer, used for your own record-keeping and identification purposes. This value is stored on the transaction but is _**not used in the processing of the transfer**_. Our recommendation is to set this to the same value as accountDesignation, or a concatenation of sortCode and accountIdentification, to make it easier to identify the transfer at a glance. - **previousProviderAccountType** (string): Indicates the ceding (sending) account type. Only valid for ISA/JISA transfers. Defaults to `Stocks and Shares` if omitted for an ISA/JISA transfer. - **payUkDetails** (object): Required object for Pay.UK transfer instruction: - **earlyClosureWaiver** (boolean): Indicates whether the client consents to potential early closure charges. Must always be provided. | earlyClosureWaiver value | Description | | --- | --- | | `true` | Client consents to potential early closure charges. | | `false` | Client does not consent to potential early closure charges. | - **sortCode** (string): The ceding provider's sort code. Must be provided together with `accountIdentification`. - **accountIdentification** (string): The ceding provider's account number. Must be provided together with `sortCode`. - **accountDesignation** (string): An alternative account reference (e.g. building society roll number). Must be basic latin characters. Must not be combined with `sortCode` or `accountIdentification`. #### Validation Rules - `earlyClosureWaiver` is always required. Omitting it will result in a validation error. - You must provide either `sortCode` + `accountIdentification` OR `accountDesignation` — never both, never neither. - Providing `sortCode` without `accountIdentification` (or vice versa) will result in a validation error. - Providing all three fields ( `sortCode`, `accountIdentification`, and `accountDesignation`) will result in a validation error. - The `previousProvider` must reference a Pay.UK-supported masterparty. Submitting `payUkDetails` against a non-Pay.UK provider will result in a validation error. ### Expected Response The API will return a JSON response including the transaction group ID.

Create a Pay.UK transfer in (Sort Code + Account Identification)

item.description:
## Pay.UK Transfer In

This section explains how to use the Seccl API to instruct a cash ISA transfer in via the Pay.UK payment scheme. Pay.UK provides an electronic route for transfers that would otherwise need to be handled manually — removing the need for physical documentation and manual processing.

### What is a Pay.UK Transfer?

A Pay.UK transfer is an electronic cash ISA transfer that uses the UK's Pay.UK payment infrastructure to move funds between providers.  
Whether a ceding provider supports Pay.UK transfers is determined by the **masterparty** — Seccl's concept of a ceding scheme. Only masterparties with Pay.UK support enabled on the relevant wrapper type can be used for this transfer method.

---

### Account Identification Formats

Pay.UK supports two _**mutually exclusive**_ methods for identifying the ceding provider's account. You must use one or the other.

#### 1\. Sort Code & Account Identification

Use this format when the ceding provider's account is identified by a UK sort code and account number.

- **Sort Code** — a 6-digit code formatted as `00-00-00`
    
- **Account Identification** — an 8 to 11 digit account number
    

#### 2\. Account Designation

Use this format when the ceding provider's account is identified by a reference such as a building society roll number.

- **Account Designation** — a 4 to 18 character alphanumeric reference
    

**Important:** You must provide either Sort Code & Account Identification **or** Account Designation. Requests containing an invalid combination will be rejected with a validation error.

---

## API Workflow: Pay.UK Transfer In - high level

To instruct a Pay.UK transfer via API, follow these steps:

### 1\. `GET` Pay.UK-supported ceding providers

- Search for masterparties that support Pay.UK transfers using the `supportsPayUk` search parameter.
    

---

### 2.`POST` to `portfoliotransactiongroup` to Create Transfer

- Submit the transfer-in request, including the `payUkDetails` object with the appropriate account identification format.

item.name: Create a partial transfer in for ISA, GIA and ATG Pension
Create a Partial transfer in - GIA

request.description:
## Create a partial transfer in for a GIA

- Submit a cash GIA partial transfer-in request.
    
- The request must include `partialTransfer: true` to indicate that the transfer is a partial transfer.
    
- The request must include `amountToTake`, which is the cash amount to transfer from the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform.
    
- The `previousProvider` must reference a masterparty that supports GIA partial cash transfers. To check this, the masterparty must have:
    
    - `transferProviders[].GIA.partialCash` set to `true`
        
    - **Use a masterparty that supports GIA partial cash transfers.** Submitting partialTransfer: true against a masterparty where transferProviders\[\].GIA.partialCash is not true will result in a validation error.
        
- **Partial in specie transfers are not supported.** Seccl currently supports partial cash transfers only.
    

### HTTP Method

`POST`

### Endpoint

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransactiongroup`

### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters:

- firmId (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction.
    
- accountId (string): The identifier for the account related to the transaction.
    
- transactions (array): An array of transaction objects, each containing:
    
    - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm related to the transaction.
        
    - transactionType (string): The type of transaction (e.g. "Product Transfer").
        
    - transactionSubType (string): The subtype of the transaction (e.g. "Cash").
        
    - movementType (string): Indicates the direction of the transaction (e.g. "In").
        
    - accountId (string): The identifier for the account involved in the transaction.
        
    - **partialTransfer (boolean)**: Set this to true to indicate that the transfer is a partial transfer.
        
    - **amountToTake (number)**: The cash amount to transfer from the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform.
        
    - transferAccountAddress (object): An object containing the address details for the transfer account:
        
        - flatNumber (string): The flat number of the address.
            
        - buildingNumber (string): The building number of the address.
            
        - address1 (string): The first line of the address.
            
        - address2 (string): The second line of the address.
            
        - country (string): The country code (e.g. "GB").
            
        - postCode (string): The postcode.
            
    - previousProvider (string): The identifier for the previous provider. This must reference a masterparty where transferProviders\[\].GIA.partialCash is true.
        

### Expected Response

The API will return a JSON response including the transaction group ID.

item.name: Create a Partial transfer in - ISA PayUK

request.description: ## Create a PayUK partial transfer in for an ISA - Submit a cash ISA partial transfer-in request through PayUK. - The request must include `partialTransfer: true` to indicate that the transfer is a partial transfer. - The request must include `amountToTake`, which is the cash amount to transfer from the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform. - The request must include `subscriptionAppliesTo`, which indicates whether the ISA transfer relates to current tax year subscriptions or previous tax year subscriptions. - The `previousProvider` must reference a masterparty that supports both ISA partial cash transfers and PayUK. To check this, the masterparty must have: - `transferProviders[].ISA.partialCash` set to `true` - `transferProviders[].ISA.supportsPayUk` set to `true` - **Use a masterparty that supports both PayUK and ISA partial cash transfers.** Submitting `partialTransfer: true` against a masterparty where either `transferProviders[].ISA.partialCash` or `transferProviders[].ISA.supportsPayUk` is not true will result in a validation error. - **Partial in specie transfers are not supported.** Seccl currently supports partial cash transfers only. ### HTTP Method `POST` ### Endpoint `{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransactiongroup` ### Request Body The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters: - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction. - accountId (string): The identifier for the account related to the transaction. - transactions (array): An array of transaction objects, each containing: - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm related to the transaction. - transactionType (string): The type of transaction (e.g. "Product Transfer"). - transactionSubType (string): The subtype of the transaction (e.g. "Cash"). - movementType (string): Indicates the direction of the transaction (e.g. "In"). - accountId (string): The identifier for the account involved in the transaction. - **partialTransfer (boolean)**: Set this to true to indicate that the transfer is a partial transfer. - **amountToTake (number)**: The cash amount to transfer from the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform. - transferAccountAddress (object): An object containing the address details for the transfer account: - flatNumber (string): The flat number of the address. - buildingNumber (string): The building number of the address. - address1 (string): The first line of the address. - address2 (string): The second line of the address. - country (string): The country code (e.g. "GB"). - postCode (string): The postcode. - previousProvider (string): The identifier for the previous provider. This must reference a masterparty where transferProviders\[\].ISA.partialCash is true and transferProviders\[\].ISA.supportsPayUk is true. - **subscriptionAppliesTo (string)**: Indicates whether the ISA transfer relates to current tax year subscriptions or previous tax year subscriptions. Can be either "Current Year" or "Previous Year". - previousProviderRef (string): A reference for the transfer, used for your own record-keeping and identification purposes. This value is stored on the transaction but is not used in the processing of the transfer. Must always be provided. | earlyClosureWaiver value | Description | | --- | --- | | `true` | Client consents to potential early closure charges. | | `false` | Client does not consent to potential early closure charges. | - sortCode (string): The ceding provider's sort code. Must be provided together with `accountIdentification`. - accountIdentification (string): The ceding provider's account number. Must be provided together with `sortCode`. - accountDesignation (string): An alternative account reference (e.g. building society roll number). Must be basic latin characters. request.description:
## Create a partial transfer in for an ISA

- Submit a cash ISA partial transfer-in request through TeX.
    
- The request must include `partialTransfer: true` to indicate that the transfer is a partial transfer.
    
- The request must include `amountToTake`, which is the cash amount to transfer from the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform.
    
- The request must include `subscriptionAppliesTo`, which indicates whether the ISA transfer relates to current tax year subscriptions or previous tax year subscriptions.
    
- The `previousProvider` must reference a masterparty that supports ISA partial cash transfers. To check this, the masterparty must have:
    
    - `transferProviders[].ISA.partialCash` set to `true`
        
    - **Use a masterparty that supports ISA partial cash transfers.** Submitting `partialTransfer: true` against a masterparty where `transferProviders[].ISA.partialCash` is not true will result in a validation error.
        
- **Partial in specie transfers are not supported.** Seccl currently supports partial cash transfers only.
    

### HTTP Method

`POST`

### Endpoint

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransactiongroup`

### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters:

- firmId (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction.
    
- accountId (string): The identifier for the account related to the transaction.
    
- transactions (array): An array of transaction objects, each containing:
    
    - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm related to the transaction.
        
    - transactionType (string): The type of transaction (e.g. "Product Transfer").
        
    - transactionSubType (string): The subtype of the transaction (e.g. "Cash").
        
    - movementType (string): Indicates the direction of the transaction (e.g. "In").
        
    - accountId (string): The identifier for the account involved in the transaction.
        
    - **partialTransfer (boolean)**: Set this to true to indicate that the transfer is a partial transfer.
        
    - **amountToTake (number)**: The cash amount to transfer from the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform.
        
    - transferAccountAddress (object): An object containing the address details for the transfer account:
        
        - flatNumber (string): The flat number of the address.
            
        - buildingNumber (string): The building number of the address.
            
        - address1 (string): The first line of the address.
            
        - address2 (string): The second line of the address.
            
        - country (string): The country code (e.g. "GB").
            
        - postCode (string): The postcode.
            
    - previousProvider (string): The identifier for the previous provider. This must reference a masterparty where transferProviders\[\].ISA.partialCash is true
        
    - **subscriptionAppliesTo (string)**: Indicates whether the ISA transfer relates to current tax year subscriptions or previous tax year subscriptions. Can be either "Current Year" or "Previous Year".
        
    - previousProviderRef (string): A reference for the transfer, used for your own record-keeping and identification purposes. This value is stored on the transaction but is not used in the processing of the transfer.
        

### Expected Response

The API will return a JSON response including the transaction group ID.

item.description:
## Partial Transfer In

This section explains how to use the Seccl API to instruct a partial cash transfer in through ATG for ISA, GIA and pension wrappers.

A partial transfer lets you transfer part of the value held with the ceding provider onto the Seccl platform, rather than transferring the full account value.

### What has changed

Seccl previously supported partial transfers for pension accounts through Origo only.

This release extends partial transfer support to ATG for ISA, GIA and pension wrappers. This means more partial transfers can be instructed through the API, giving firms a faster process and better visibility of transfer progress.

**Partial in specie transfers are not supported.** Seccl currently supports partial cash transfers only.

**Do not use** **`amountToLeave`** **for ATG pension partial transfers.** Use `amountToTake` to provide the amount being transferred. `amountToLeave` is only supported for Origo pension partial transfers.

---

### Which providers support partial transfers?

Not all ceding providers support partial cash transfers. Support can also vary by wrapper type.

You can check whether a ceding provider supports partial cash transfers by checking the relevant masterparty, the Seccl’s record for a ceding scheme.

A masterparty can be used for a partial transfer when the relevant wrapper type has `partialCash` set to `true` for the transfer provider.

For example, for an ISA transfer through ATG, check:

`transferProviders[].ISA.partialCash`

Example response:

``` json
{
  "transferProviders": [
    {
      "transferProviderName": "ATG",
      "providerReference": "PAYUK02",
      "ISA": {
        "cashSupported": true,
        "inSpecieSupported": false,
        "partialCash": true,
        "supportsPayUk": true
      }
    }
  ]
}

 ```

In this example, the masterparty supports partial cash ISA transfers through ATG.

---

### Additional information required for partial ISA transfers

Partial ISA transfers require one additional piece of information: whether the transfer relates to the current tax year or previous tax years.

This is needed so Seccl can manage ISA subscription limits in line with regulatory requirements.

Provide this information in the `subscriptionAppliesTo` field.

Accepted values are:

| Value | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| `Current Year` | The transfer relates to current tax year ISA subscriptions |
| `Previous Year` | The transfer relates to previous tax years ISA subscriptions |

This field is required for partial ISA transfers.

---

### Compatibility with PayUK

Partial cash transfers are compatible with PayUK where the ceding provider supports PayUK.

For cash ISA transfers, PayUK can help reduce transfer times when the ceding provider has PayUK support enabled.

You can check PayUK support on the relevant wrapper type using the `supportsPayUk` flag.

---

## API Workflow: Pay.UK Transfer In - high level

To instruct a partial transfer via API

### 1\. `GET` Ceding providers

Search for ceding providers as normal

In the response, identify the masterparty you want to transfer from and check whether the relevant wrapper type has `partialCash` set to `true`.

For example:

- For an ISA transfer, check `transferProviders[].ISA.partialCash`
    
- For a GIA transfer, check `transferProviders[].GIA.partialCash`
    
- For a pension transfer, check `transferProviders[].PENSION.partialCash`
    

If the relevant wrapper type has `partialCash: true`, you can instruct a partial cash transfer for that wrapper.

---

### 2.`POST` to `portfoliotransactiongroup` to Create Transfer

- Submit the transfer-in request, with `partialTransfer: true` and `amountToTake` provided to denote the amount being transferred.
    
- For partial ISA transfers, also provide `subscriptionAppliesTo` with either `Current Year` or `Previous Year`.

request.description:
### Search for ceding account type - supported providers

The query parameters `cedingCashSupported` and `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported` can be used to retrieve a list of ceding providers that support Cash ISA/JISA or Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA ceding accounts (or vice versa).

| `cedingCashSupported` / `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported` value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `True` | Returns only masterparties where at least one transfer provider wrapper has the corresponding field set to true. |
| `False` | Returns masterparties where the corresponding field is false or not defined on any transfer provider wrapper. |
| _(omitted)_ | Returns all masterparties matching the rest of the query, regardless of ceding account type support. |

**Important:** When either `cedingCashSupported` or `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported` is supplied (whether `True` or `False`), the `transferWrapperType` query parameter is **required**. Omitting it will result in the following validation error:  
`transferWrapperType is required when cedingCashSupported or cedingStocksAndSharesSupported is provided`

Both parameters can be combined with each other and with the existing `productTransferType` filter (which narrows results by `cashSupported` / `inSpecieSupported`).

---

#### Ceding account type–specific Attributes

`transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.cedingCashSupported` boolean

Indicates whether the ceding provider supports **Cash** ISA/JISA transfers for the given wrapper type. When true, the provider can accept transfer-in instructions where the ceding account is a Cash ISA/JISA.

`transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.cedingStocksAndSharesSupported` boolean

Indicates whether the ceding provider supports **Stocks and Shares** ISA/JISA transfers for the given wrapper type. When true, the provider can accept transfer-in instructions where the ceding account is a Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA.

**Note**: Both fields are located within each wrapper type object under `transferProviders`, alongside existing fields such as `cashSupported` and `inSpecieSupported`. For example:

``` json
            "transferProviders": [
                {
                    "transferProviderName": "ATG",
                    "providerReference": "CEDING01",
                    "ISA": {
                        "cashSupported": true,
                        "inSpecieSupported": false,
                        "cedingCashSupported": true,
                        "cedingStocksAndSharesSupported": false
                    },
                    "JISA": {
                        "cashSupported": true,
                        "inSpecieSupported": false,
                        "cedingCashSupported": false,
                        "cedingStocksAndSharesSupported": true
                    }
                }
            ],

 ```

---

#### Matching behaviour

| Query | Matches masterparties where… |
| --- | --- |
| `transferWrapperType=ISA&cedingCashSupported=True` | transfer providers which have an `ISA` wrapper with `cedingCashSupported: true` |
| `transferWrapperType=JISA&cedingCashSupported=True` | transfer providers which have an `JISA` wrapper with `cedingCashSupported: true` |
| `transferWrapperType=ISA&cedingStocksAndSharesSupported=True` | transfer providers which have an `ISA` wrapper with `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true` |
| `transferWrapperType=JISA&cedingStocksAndSharesSupported=True` | transfer providers which have an `JISA` wrapper with `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true` |

item.name: Create a  transfer in for a ceding Cash or Stock and Share account

request.description:
## Instruct a transfer in with ceding account type

- Submit a Cash or Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA transfer-in request. The `previousProviderAccountType` field indicates whether the ceding (sending) account is a Cash ISA/JISA or a Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA, so the transfer can be routed and processed correctly.
    
- The `previousProvider` must reference a masterparty that supports the specified ceding account type on the relevant wrapper (i.e. `cedingCashSupported: true` or `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true`). Submitting a `previousProviderAccountType` that the masterparty does not support for that wrapper will result in a validation error.
    
- **Important:** `previousProviderAccountType` is **only valid** for ISA/JISA transfers. If it is omitted on an ISA/JISA transfer, the value defaults to `Stocks and Shares` (and the masterparty must therefore support `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true`).
    

### HTTP Method

`POST`

### Endpoint

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransactiongroup`

### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters:

- firmId (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction.
    
- accountId (string): The identifier for the account related to the transaction.
    
- transactions (array): An array of transaction objects, each containing:
    
    - firmId (string): The identifier for the firm related to the transaction.
        
    - transactionType (string): The type of transaction (e.g., "Product Transfer").
        
    - transactionSubType (string): The subtype of the transaction (e.g., "Cash").
        
    - movementType (string): Indicates the direction of the transaction (e.g., "In").
        
    - accountId (string): The identifier for the account involved in the transaction.
        
    - transferAccountAddress (object): An object containing the address details for the transfer account:
        
        - flatNumber (string): The flat number of the address.
            
        - buildingNumber (string): The building number of the address.
            
        - address1 (string): The first line of the address.
            
        - address2 (string): The second line of the address.
            
        - country (string): The country code (e.g., "GB").
            
        - postCode (string): The postal code.
            
    - **previousProvider** (string): The identifier for the previous provider — the masterparty _**which supports the specified ceding account type**_ on the relevant wrapper.
        
    - **previousProviderRef** (string): A reference for the transfer, used for your own record-keeping and identification purposes. This value is stored on the transaction but is _**not used in the processing of the transfer**_.
        
    - **previousProviderAccountType** (string): Indicates the ceding (sending) account type. Only valid for ISA/JISA transfers. Defaults to `Stocks and Shares` if omitted for an ISA/JISA transfer.  
        **Note:** This field works the same for manual transfer, details can be found in the "Create a Manual transfer for a ceding cash account" example.
        
        | previousProviderAccountType value | Description |
        | --- | --- |
        | `Cash` | The ceding account is a Cash ISA/JISA. Requires the masterparty to have `cedingCashSupported: true` on the relevant wrapper. |
        | `Stocks and Shares` | The ceding account is a Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA. Requires the masterparty to have `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true` on the relevant wrapper. |
        | _(omitted)_ | Defaults to `Stocks and Shares` for ISA/JISA transfers. Not accepted on non-ISA/JISA transfers. |
        

#### Validation Rules

- `previousProviderAccountType` is only valid for **ISA/JISA** transfers. Providing it on a non-ISA/JISA transfer will result in the validation error:  
    `previousProviderAccountType should only be set for transfers to ISA or JISA account`
    
- The value must be either `Cash` or `Stocks and Shares`. Any other value will result in the validation error:  
    `Previous provider account type must be either Cash or Stocks and Shares`
    
- When `previousProviderAccountType` is `Cash`, the `previousProvider` masterparty must have `cedingCashSupported: true` on the account's wrapper. Otherwise:  
    `Ceding Provider does not support Cash {WrapperType} transfers`
    
- When `previousProviderAccountType` is `Stocks and Shares` (including when omitted and defaulted for an ISA/JISA transfer), the `previousProvider` masterparty must have `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true` on the account's wrapper. Otherwise:  
    `Ceding Provider does not support Stocks and Shares {WrapperType} transfers`
    

### Expected Response

The API will return a JSON response including the transaction group ID.

item.description:
## Ceding account types for ISA and JISA

This section explains how to use the SECCL to instruct electronic ISA and JISA transfers. Previously, ISA and JISA transfers did not distinguish the ceding product being transferred. As a result, all transfer requests were treated as Stocks & Shares transfers. The API now supports explicitly identifying whether the ceding account is a **Cash ISA/JISA** or a **Stocks & Shares ISA/JISA**. Providing this information enables more accurate transfer instructions, reduces the likelihood of transfers being rejected by ceding providers, and helps minimise processing delays.  
In addition, provider (masterparty) records have been enhanced to identify which ISA and JISA account types each provider supports. This allows clients to validate that a selected provider supports the requested transfer type before submitting a transfer instruction.

### **Why ceding account types matter**

Many providers offer both Cash and Stocks & Shares ISA or JISA products, while others support only one account type. If the transfer request specifies an account type that the ceding provider does not support, the transfer is likely to be rejected or require manual clarification, resulting in delays for the end customer.  
To reduce these failures, ISA and JISA transfer requests can now include the type of account being transferred.  
For backwards compatibility, if this field is omitted the API will continue to default to **Stocks & Shares**, preserving the behaviour of existing integrations.

---

### New fields

We are introducing a new field on the product transfer request for ISA and JISA.

#### previousProviderAccountType

Use this to specify if the ceding account for the transfer is a Cash or a Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA

##### Values:

1. Cash
    
2. Stocks and Shares
    

**Important:**

- The system will still default to assuming S&S ISA if none is set to maintain backwards compatability for existing integrations.
    
- After this feature is live we will block transfers to providers which do not support the selected ceding account type, including defaulted S&S transfers. This will show up as a validation error on the initial creation request.
    

---

### Masterparty changes

We are adding two new fields to our masterparty provider wrapper record.

- transferProviders.\[ISA or JISA\].cedingCashSupported - boolean - indicates whether the provider supports Cash ISA/JISA transfers for the selected wrapper (ISA or JISA, depends on the path)
    
- transferProviders.\[ISA or JISA\].cedingStocksAndSharesSupported - boolean - indicates whether the provider supports Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA transfers for the selected wrapper (ISA or JISA, depends on the path)
    

We are also adding two new query search parameters to allow you to retrieve masterparties wich support Cash or S&S accounts for your selected wrapper

- cedingCashSupported - True or False - If set to True returns only providers that support transfers from a Cash ceding account for the selected wrapper. False returns those which do not (false or undefined)
    
- cedingStocksAndSharesSupported - True or False - If set to True returns only providers that support transfers from a Stocks and Shares ceding account for the selected wrapper. False returns those which do not (false or undefined)
    

---

## API Workflow: New ISA/JISA Transfer In - high level

To instruct an ISA/JISA transfer via API, follow these steps:

### 1\. Determine what is the ceding type of the account you want to transfer

---

### 2\. `GET` Cash or S&S-supported ceding providers

- Search for masterparties that support Cash or S&S ceding account transfers using the `cedingCashSupported` or `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported` search parameter.
    

---

### 3.`POST` to `portfoliotransactiongroup` to Create Transfer

- Submit the transfer-in request with the appropriate `previousProviderAccountType` for the account you want to transfer and that is supported by your selected masterparty as per the examples
This section contains details on how to instruct and how to view Joint GIA transfers.

item.name: Quickstart guide

request.description: Firstly, you will need an access token as a machine user. This will allow you to log into the Seccl sandbox environment.

Your client, Wilma Flintstone is excited to begin her investment journey. She would like to use your app to help build up a deposit for a new cave in the near future.

In order for you to create a client record for Wilma, she will need to add in all her details - including important regulatory information such as her nationality, so that she is eligible to use your Seccl-powered platform to trade. Originally from Bedrock, Wilma now is a British citizen living in the UK.

The response should provide you with a `clientId`. This is a unique identifier for your client so keep this handy!

Now let's add some assets to your platform so that Wilma can start investing. She's read about the benefits of compound interest and is excited to start investing in her future home purchase. She would like to invest in a fund.

To add an asset to your asset universe, send a `POST` request to the `/asset` endpoint. This makes the asset available to trade.

In order to invest her money, Wilma will need to create an investment account, such as an Individual Savings Account (ISA).

This can be created through a `POST` request to the `/account` endpoint.

item.name: Create a payment in and order expectation

request.description:
Great! Now Wilma is ready to add some cash into her account and invest.

By sending a **payment in and order** `POST` request, Wilma has agreed to send £10,000 from her bank account to her Seccl ISA, which then automatically creates an order expectation for the fund. Once the fund order is executed (usually after two days), she will then own £9,800 worth of the fund, as the remainder has been allocated to cover any potential fees over the years.

This will provide you with a unique `linkId` for this grouped transaction.

To mock a completed transaction - which would ordinarily be triggered by real life events - you can retrieve and settle a _payment in_ and the linked order .

Firstly, you will need to retrieve this `paymentId` and complete it using a `PUT` request.

When querying for pending orders using the `linkId` query param, providing the `eventId` or the `linkId` as a value in the param will retrieve pending order transactions.
This mocks a completed payment in or deposit.

Next, you will need to retrieve the `orderId` and manually settle it using this `PUT` request.

When querying for pending orders using the `linkId` query param, providing the `eventId` or the `linkId` as a value in the param will retrieve pending order transactions.
This mocks a completed order.

Wilma has been on the platform for over a month now, and it is time to take a platform fee from her account. By creating a fee transaction, you will be able to charge her with the amount agreed when she first created her account.

Wilma is keen to see a valuation of her account as well as some of the past transactions she has made. She can do this by viewing her account summary - which is facilitated by a `GET` request to the `/account/summary` endpoint.

And that's a wrap for now! This is just a snapshot of what's possible with our API. Check out the links below for more ways to invest:

\[to add links to investment strategies, accounts and payment methods\]

request.description:
Retrieves a list of nationalities and the relevant identifiers. This is important to obtain National Identifier information needed in the `investmentDecsion` array.

The `static` nationality endpoint provides a list of nationalities, the ISO country codes and the national identifier that the FCA requires for reporting when trading ETIs

##### Understanding the priority

This is logic used to determine which identifier is appropriate to report on any transactions under your client's name. Priority is scored and the relevant identifiers are listed in this order under the array.

The rules for the FCA-preferred nationality are:

1.  An EEA (European Economic Area) nationality takes priority over a non-EEA nationality
2.  The nationality that comes first when the list of the client's nationalities is sorted alphabetically by the country code takes priority
3.  CONCAT is, in most cases, a last resort identifier that if required will be generated by Seccl in accordance with MiFIR/MiFID guidelines
    

**Please note: CONCAT – a combination of the client's date of birth, first name, and surname – may only be used if the Priority 1 identifier shown in the nationalities checker is not applicable to the client**

#### **Attributes**

* * *

`id` string  
The unique two-letter identifier for the nationality. This is case sensitive.=

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = GB |

* * *

`code` string  
A two-letter country code

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = GB |

* * *

`name` string  
The name of the country

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = GB |

* * *

`adjective` string  
The country descriptor

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = British |

* * *

`inEEA` boolean  
This confirms whether or not a country is in the European Economic Area (EEA). Although the UK is not in the EU anymore, it is still reported as `inEEA: true` as per MiFIR/MiFID II rules

* * *

`identifiers` array  
An array which captures all forms of national identifiers for the chosen country

* * *

`identifiers.name` string  
The name of the national identifier. This will be National Insurance Number for British nationals and National Passport Number for all other nationalities

* * *

`identifiers.regex` string  
A regular expression denoting validation for the national identifier

* * *

`identifiers.localeName` string  
The name of the national identifier

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = British |

* * *

`identifiers.example` string  
An example of the alphanumeric national identifier format

* * *

`identifiers.priority` integer

The national identifier priority score

* * *

* * *

`nodeId` array **Required**

The unique identifier of the node that the user should be attached to

* * *

`scopes` array **Required**

The levels of access a user has. These are `read`, `read/write` and `action`. The scopes can be implemented across different areas of the system outlined below:

* * *

`scopes.scope` string **Required**

The area of the system which the user has access to.

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Client` | The ability to edit and create a client |
| `Account` | The ability to edit and create an account |
| `Model` | The ability to edit and create a model. This is strictly for DFMs. |
| `User` | The ability to edit and create a model. This is strictly for DFMs. |
| `Instrument` | The ability to view instruments and request for new assets in your universe. |

* * *

`scopes.ranges` string **Required**

The levels of access a user has. These are `read`, `read/write` and `action`.

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | The ability to view |
| `readWrite` | The ability to view and edit for example, updating an account with a new email address |
| `action` | The ability to carry out an action for example, creating a client record on the system |

The National Identifier for the firm user/decision maker. For GB nationals this is in the format XX123456X

`investmentDecision.personIdType` string **Required**
 
The type of National Identifier provided for the firm user/decision maker. For GB nationals this is NINO (National Insurance Number)

item.description:
You can also create a specific type of firm user with discretionary (DFM) permissions. 

This may be because you would like to manage your client’s investments separately. For instance they may be a high-net-worth investor with specific investment goals and needs. 

**Please note:** This is only a pre-requisite for setting up a Bespoke DFM investment strategy and is *not* needed for DFM Model Portfolios as the model records hold the Decision Maker details.

Users refer to people accessing the platform services as staff, including the platform operations team, administrators, advisers and paraplanners.

There are two types of users:

- **Machine user:** A user accessing Seccl's services via the API. All firms will have a machine user who can access the Seccl API via a system login
- **User:** An individual accessing our services via the off-the-shelf professional user interface
    

If you are accessing Seccl's services exclusively via the API, you will have a single machine user login for your application.

You will be responsible for managing the various users accessing your platform services.

#### **Endpoints**

```
/user

```

request.description:
This flow adds an asset to the platform asset universe, making it available to trade, or to add to a `model` or `recurringOrders` allocation.

#### Parameters

---

`firmId` string **Required**

The unique identifier for your firm

---

`id` string **Required**

The unique identifier of the asset

---

`availableToNodeId` array **Optional**

The nodeId(s) where the asset is made available. This will make the asset available to all sub-nodes as well

**Examples:**

- `"availableToNodeId": ["0"]` - all nodes, default if not provided
    
- `"availableToNodeId": ["2", "3"]` - select nodes (sub-nodes will inherit access)
    

---
This flow allows you to retrieve assets in your platform asset universe.

item.description:
Static assets are available via our API, including regulatory documents, settlement periods, and fund charges.

#### **Endpoints**

``` json
/ asset
/ masterinstrument

 ```

### The asset object

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the asset

---

`shortName` string

The short name of the asset

---

`longName` string

The long name of the asset

---

`instrumentType` enum value

The type of instrument

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| `Fund` |
| `Investment Trust` |
| `ETF` |
| `Equity` |

---

`isin` string

The ISIN of the asset

---

`mic` enum value

The Market Identifier Code (MIC), which is an international indicator that identifies security trading exchanges

---

`primaryMarket` booelan

This indicates whether the `mic` is the market where the asset was created and first issued

---

`currency` enum value

The currency the asset trades in

---

`countryOfIssue` enum value

The country where the asset was first issued

---

`countryOfIncorporation` enum value

The country where the asset was incorporated

---

`status` enum value

The status of the asset. They are the following:

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | Available to trade |
| `Pending` | Awaiting to be provisioned by Seccl |
| `Rejected` |  |
| `Suspended` | Unavailable to trade |
| `Delisted` | No longer listed |

---

---

`bid` float

The maximum that a buyer is willing to pay for the asset

---

`ask` float

The minimum that a seller is willing to pay for the asset

---

`mid` float

The midpoint of the bid and ask prices

---

`stampable` boolean

This indicates whether the asset is applicable for stamp duty. Stamp duty is a form of tax charged on assets in the UK

---

`ptm` boolean

This indicates whether the asset is applicable for the PTM levy. PTM stands for Panel Takeovers and Mergers and is a regulatory body setup to ensure all shareholders are treated equally during takeover bids

---

`nationalityDeclaration` boolean

This indicates whether the shares of the company require a nationality declaration when placing trades. It only applies to equities

---

`quoteUnit` integer

This indicates the number of units for the quote, or price. For example, if the asset is £10 and the `quoteUnit` is 1, then £10 is the quote for a single unit; if the asset is £100 and the `quoteUnit` is 100, then £100 is the quote for 100 units

---

`minimumTransferUnit` float

The number of decimal places that the asset can be held. For example, `0.0001` means the asset can be held to 4 decimal places. This is driven by the fund manager or instrument type

---

`settlementPeriod` integer

The number of days the asset takes to settle upon order execution

---

`incomeCurrency` enum value

The number of days the asset takes to settle upon order execution

---

`taxDetails` array

An array capturing how the asset is taxed

---

`taxDetails.taxDomicile` enum value

The tax country that applies to income. It will depend on where the company is incorporated

---

`taxDetails.reportCategory` enum value

This is either a UK Dividend or a Foreign Dividend depending on where the company is incorporated and income is taxed

---

`restricted` boolean

This indicates whether the asset is ring-fenced to your platform specifically

---

`ocfCalculated` float

This indicates the ongoing charges figure and applies to ETFs, funds, and investment trusts

---

`kiidDocumentUrl` string

The Key Investor Information Document (KIID) of the fund or ETF. This is retrieved from FundsLibrary and should be made available to investors ahead of investing in the asset

---

`fundDetail` array

An array capturing details of the fund

---

`fundDetail.accumulationOrIncome` enum value

This indicates whether the fund is `Income` or `Accumulation`

---

`mifidCharges` array

An array capturing all MiFID charges on the asset

---

`mifidCharges.exAnteOngoing` float

This describes the ex-ante ongoing costs of the asset. This applies to funds, ETFs and investment trusts only

---

`mifidCharges.exAnteIncidental` float

This describes the ex-ante incidental costs of the asset. This applies to funds, ETFs and investment trusts only

---

`mifidCharges.exAnteTransaction` float

This describes the ex-ante transaction costs of asset, which include both explicit and implicit transaction costs. This applies to funds, ETFs and investment trusts only

---

Prices of all the assets held in Seccl's Master Asset Universe are available via the API.

We update prices at 3:45am every business day, with yesterday's close of business prices. We recommend that you retrieve daily asset prices after 4:00am.

**Note: asset prices are also available via the** **`asset`** **endpoint. However, the** **`price`** **endpoint is more optimised so should be used for the daily job.**

**Endpoints**

```
/ price

 ```

### The price object

This is an object representing the price data of an asset. You can retrieve the price object of an asset to view daily pricing.

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the price record

---

`insertDate` string

The date the price was added to Seccl's system

---

`priceDate` string

The date of the price

---

`bid` float

The maximum price that a buyer is willing to pay for an asset

---

`ask` float

The minimum price that a seller is willing to pay for an asset

---

`mid` float

The midpoint between the bid and ask prices

---

`assetId` string

The unique identifier of the asset

---

`quoteUnit` integer

This indicates the number of units for the quote or price. For example, if the asset is £10 and the quoteUnit is 1, then £10 is the quote for a single unit. If the asset is £100 and the quoteUnit is 100, then £100 is the quote for 100 units

---

`minimumTransferUnit` float

The number of decimal places that the asset can be held. For example, 0.0001 means the asset can be held to 4 decimal places. This is asset specific and varies between a value of 0.0001 and 1

---

`currency` enum value

The currency the asset trades in

---

`exchangeRates` array

This details the exchange rate of the asset, where the currency is non-GBP

---

`instrumentType` enum value

The type of instrument

---

Seccl has "whole of market" access to funds, direct equities, investment trusts and exchange-traded instruments.

Assets are made available in Seccl's Master Universe. As the platform operator, you can select a sub-section of assets to make available to your investors and users.

**Please note: the master universe asset list in the staging environment differs to the master universe asset list in the production environment.**

item.name: Fees
Seccl fee run
item.description:
Seccl has the ability to calculate and instruct transactions for various fee types.

Ongoing fees taken by Seccl are calculated on a monthly basis using the daily average balance.

```
Sum for the calendar month ((daily_account_balance) / 365 * (fee_amount))

 ```

Where an investment account has insufficient uninvested cash to cover the fee amount, a sell-down is instructed, and the fee amount is taken when the order executes. The sell-down may include a 10% cash buffer to take into account market movements.

These are the fees we can facilitate:

| **Fee type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Platform fee | % amount with tiering set at the node level |
| Discretionary management fee | % amount set at the model level |
| Adviser fee | % amount with tiering set at the investment account level |
| Subscription fee | £ amount with tiering set at the node level |
| Product fee | % amount with tiering set at the node level |

If you're looking for a specific fee structure that isn't detailed below, please refer to the **DIY fee run** section**.**

item.description:
A DIY fee run gives you greater flexibility than a Seccl fee run. With this option, you are free to implement a unique fee structure that works for your platform.

For example, you may want to set charges based on wrapper types, or calculate fees according to the length of time an investor has been with your platform.

The operational flow for a DIY fee run works exactly the same as the Seccl fee run. However, you (the platform) are responsible for calculating the fee amount and instructing the fee transaction from the investment account.

We will pay out fees taken to the platform or relevant party.

The process works as follows:

1.  Calculate the fee amount using the daily average balance
2.  Check if the account has a sufficient uninvested cash balance to cover the fee
    1.  If yes - instruct the fee transaction
    2.  If no - instruct a group sell and fee transaction

This can be applied to any fee type and amount.

The adviser fee is taken when the money is allocated to the payment expectation. For example, if a user creates a £500 expectation with a £50 adviser fee, when the money is allocated, £50 is automatically deducted to cover the fee and the remainder - £450 - will be allocated to the investment account. #### Parameters `firmId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the firm --- `accountId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the investment account where the fee should be taken --- `transactions` object **Required** --- `transactions.firmId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the firm --- `transactions.accountId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the investment account for the payment/fee --- `transactions.transactionType` enum value **Required** The type of transaction taking place. This should be set to `Payment` --- `transactions.transactionSubType` enum value **Required** This should be set to `Deposit` --- `movementType` enum value **Required** This should be set to `In` --- `currency` enum value **Required** This should be set to `GBP` --- `amount` float **Required** The amount to be deposited. This will be gross of the fee amount --- `method` enum value **Required** The payment method used to deposit the money --- `transactions.transactionType` enum value **Required** The type of transaction taking place. item.description:
Seccl pays out fees taken from client investment accounts every Friday for fees accrued between the previous Friday and that Thursday.

You can access completed fees via the API.

Fees describe the charges paid by investors for platform, adviser and investment management services.

There are several different fee types:

- **Platform fee:** The charge paid by the client to the platform for platform services. Usually % of assets held on the platform
    
- **Subscription fee:** The charge paid by the client to the platform for platform services. Usually £ amount
    
- **Product fee:** The charge paid by the client to the platform for the use of certain wrappers. Can be a % or fixed £ amount
    
- **Discretionary management fee:** The charge paid by the client to the investment manager for discretionary services. Usually % of assets held in the relevant model
    
- **Adviser ongoing fee:** The charge paid by the client to the advice firm for financial advice services. Usually % of assets held on the platform
    
- **Adviser ad-hoc fee:** The charge paid by the client to the advice firm for financial advice services
    
- **Adviser initial fee:** The charge paid by the client to the advice firm for financial advice services
    

#### **Endpoints**

``` json
/ portfoliotransactiongroup
/ portfoliotransaction

 ```

There are three ways to take fees on the platform:

1. Seccl fee run
    
2. DIY fee run
    
3. Ad-hoc or initial fee transactions

request.description:
This retrieves a single notification.

#### Parameters

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the notification

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier for the firm

---

`notificationType` enum value

The type of notification

| **Enum value** | **Narrative** |
| --- | --- |
| `Exception` | Refers to errors generated by activity on the platform |
| `Information` | Refers to information on the platform. This is not currently in use |

---

`created` string

The date the notification was generated

---

`systemArea` string

The area of the system that the notification relates

---

`exceptionFirmId` string

The unique identifier of the notification

---

`status` enum value

The status of the notification

| **Enum value** | **Narrative** |
| --- | --- |
| `Open` | Status assigned when a notification is first generated |
| `Closed` | Updated status when a notification has been reviewed and actioned |

---

`message` enum value

Examples below:

| **Enum value** | **Narrative** |
| --- | --- |
| `Adviser charge not found` | Attempt to take an adviser charge where no adviser charge is set on the account |
| `Client must have valid national identifier for orders to be placed` | Missing national identifier on the client record when attempting to instruct order in an ETI |
| `Discretionary charge not found` | Attempt to take a discretionary charge where no discretionary charge is set on the account or model |
| `Disinvest amount required is greater than the current value of active account positions` | Attempt to instruct disinvestment that's greater than the available value |
| `Gocardless mandate search did not return a counterparty ID` | GoCardless mandate error |
| `Insufficient funds for auto-disinvestment` | Attempt to sell down more than the available assets |
| `Insufficient funds for this transaction` | Attempt to instruct a transaction but insufficient cash |
| `Insufficient stock for this transaction` | Attempt to instruct a transaction but insufficient units |
| `Internal Cash Movement` | Attempt to instruct a cash movement between two invalid wrappers |
| `Order quantity error` | Attempt to instruct an order for a number of units that doesn't comply with the minimum transfer units of the asset |
| `Pension Drawdown Transfer` | Attempt to instruct a drawdown transfer where the account isn't in `drawdownPending` status |
| `Rebalances are currently suspended for this asset allocation` | Attempt to rebalance a model where `suspendRebalance` flag is `true` |
| `Subscription limit for this year has been exceeded` | Attempt to instruct a payment expectation that takes the client over their subscription limit |
| `Trust accounts require LEI for this transaction` | Missing LEI for a trust account to execute an ETI order |

---

`systemAreaAction` enum value

The action type of the instruction

| **Enum value** | **Narrative** |
| --- | --- |
| `Create` | Attempt to create a resource |
| `Send` | Attempt to send a resource |
| `Action` | Attempt to action an instruction |

---

`queue` string

This will be `pfolio`

---

`queueMessage` array

This provides details of the specific API request that has errored

---

`exceptionType` enum value

This will be `Business`

---

`auditDetails` array

This provides audit details of the notification

---

request.description:
This updates the status of a notification.

This should be used once the notification has been investigated and actioned by the platform operations team.

#### Parameters

---

`exceptionAction` enum value **Required**

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Close | Closes the exception |
| Reprocess | Attempts to reprocess the initial instruction. This should be used after the issue is resolved. If a notification is reprocessed and the error persists, it will generate a new exception notification |

---

`actionReason` string **Required**

This field should be used to add narrative around why the exception is closed or reprocessed

---

item.description:
Suspicious activity refers to transactions which have been sent to checking due to not passing one or more of the following rules:

Rule - "Check transaction"  
Rule - "Bank details added within last 90 days"  
Rule - "Bank account status pending"

Each rule will return a result of passed as True or False with False sending the transaction to checking.

**Check transaction**  
This rule is to detect any suspicious clients which have been added as a sanctioned client. Please see the API documentation under section Client onboarding > Update a client > Update a client to PEP or sanctioned.

**Bank details added within last 90 days**

This rule will detect any changes made to the bank account details within the past 90 days for withdrawals. If the bank details have been changed the transaction will go to checking.

**Bank account status pending**

This rule will detect if the bank account the withdrawal is being paid to has the status of "Pending". This is for a soon to be released feature for bank account verification. Once a bank account has been verified it will have the status of "Active" and will pass the rule.

**Please note: this functionality should be used to trigger a manual process whereby the firms compliance function reviews, validates, and confirms if the transaction should proceed forwards from checking. Details of this exact procedure followed should be included in the firms AML policy.**

#### **Endpoints**

```
/portfoliotransaction 
/portfoliotransaction/action/authorise/

 ```

item.description:
The Secure data transfers API allows authorised users to retrieve structured data files in csv format via pre-signed URLs. These files are purpose-built to support platform operators with reconciliation activities by offering consistent, high-quality data across:

- Clients
    
- Accounts
    
- Account positions
    
- Transactions
    
- Client documents
    

These files are designed for platform operators and will, by design, include data across your entire node hierarchy. They cannot be configured to run at individual node levels.

## Available files

We provide five core files to support this activity. In addition, there are supporting files that enable change tracking across key entities, along with a new metadata file designed to make file processing and reconciliation more efficient.

| **File name {{fileType}}** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| Accounts | Detailed information for each account including ID, wrapper type, and status. |
| Clients | Data on individual clients such as ID, address, and account status. |
| Positions | Settled positions as of close of business the previous day. |
| Transactions | Full transaction history from day one, with a future plan for daily updates |
| Documents | Details of each document created for clients |
| Account status | Captures status transitions at account level |
| Client status | Highlights any status changes made to client level |
| Transaction status | Surfaces status changes to transaction records |
| Check file | A summary metadata file listing all available data files for the day, including file names, types, and record counts. |

Please note: files will be available for collection from 8am each day, and all information in these files reflects data as of the end of the previous business day.

## Testing in staging

If you would like to test this process in your staging environment, please contact your Account Manager. We can arrange for test files containing staging data to be made available for you to retrieve.

## Endpoint

``` json
{{apiRoute}}/data/{{fileType}}

 ```

Replace `{{fileType}}` with any of the other available file types as needed.

## Access permissions

We have created a new user scope to prevent unauthorised access. Please note, that users will need to have the **Bulk Data Download** scope in order to request these.

If you need your machine user to updated, please contact your Account Manager.

## Pre-signed URLs

- Each file is served via a pre-signed URL, valid for **1 minute** after creation.
    
- After expiry, a new request must be made to retrieve a new URL.
    

## File retention

- Files will be retained for **1 week** before being archived.
    
- Archived files are not accessible via this API.
    

## Error handling

| **Condition** | **Response code** | **Message** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User lacks `Bulk Data Download` scope | 403 Forbidden | `Access Denied - Scope missing` |
| User is not authorised for the requested `firmId` | 403 Forbidden | `Access Denied - Firm access unauthorised` |
| File not found | 400 Bad request | `File retrieval error` |
| File found - Pre-signed URL generated successfully | 200 OK | `{ "url": "https://..." }` |

---
