The unique identifier for the firm

---

`nodeId` integer  
The unique identifier for the firm node's account. This is a single number.

---

`clientType` string  
The type of client

| **Enum values** |  |
| --- | --- |
| `Individual` | An adult client |
| `Individual minor` | A child client |

---

`title` string  
The legal title of the client

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| `Dr` |
| `Professor` |
| `Mrs` |
| `Miss` |
| `Mr` |
| `Ms` |
| `Mx` |

---

`firstName` string **Required**  
The legal first name/s of the client

---

`surname` string **Required**  
The legal surname of the client

---

`gender` string  
The legal gender of the client

---

`currency` string  
Three-letter **ISO code for the currency** paid in or out of the account

---

`addressDetail` array  
Contains details of the client's home address

---

`addressDetail.flatNumber` or `addressDetail.buildingName` or `addressDetail.buildingNumber` string  
The flat number, building name, or building number of the client's home address

---

`addressDetail.address1` string **Required**  
The first line of the client's home address

---

`addressDetail.address2` string  
The second line of the client's home address

---

`addressDetail.country` string  
The client's country of residence

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| Great Britain = `GB` |

---

`addressDetail.postCode` string  
The postcode of the client's home address

---

`language` string  
The client's preferred language of communication

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| English = `en` |

---

`email` string **Required**  
The client's email address – this must be unique to other clients on the platform

---

`mobile` array  
Details capturing the client's mobile phone number

---

`mobile.number` number  
The client's mobile phone number

---

`mobile.locale` string  
The geographical location for the client's mobile phone number – uses `isMobilePhone` from [validator.js](https://github.com/validatorjs/validator.js)

---

`mobile.isMobile` boolean  
Confirms the client's phone number is a mobile phone number

---

`nationality` string  
The client's nationality

---

`nationalities` array  
Contains details of the client's nationality/s and the relevant national identifier. Required for trading Exchange-Traded Instruments (ETIs)

---

`nationalInsuranceNumber` string  
The client's National Insurance Number – this is a mandatory field for clients opening an ISA or SIPP

---

`dateOfBirth` string **Required**  
The client's birth date in the ISO format – `YYYY-MM-DD`

---

`taxDomicile` string  
The client's current place of residence

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| Great Britain = GB |

---

`amlStatus` string  
Before creating a client record, you must carry out necessary AML/KYC checks – once the client is deemed eligible, this should be set to `Approved`

---

`termsAccepted` boolean  
Indicates whether the client has accepted the platform's terms and conditions. This field must be explicitly set to `true` to confirm acceptance and move the client record to active status. A value of `false` indicates that the client has not accepted the terms. To transact on accounts this must be set to `true` once the client has agreed to platform terms and conditions.

---

`status` string

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has passed KYC and accepted the platform terms |
| `Pending` | The client has signed up but has not yet passed KYC or accepted platform terms |
| `Registered` | An illustration has been created for the client and a skeletal client record |

---

`bankDetails` array  
The client's bank details

---

`bankDetails.sortCode` number  
The client's bank's sort code. This is a six-digit number

---

`bankDetails.accountNumber` numerical string  
The client's account number. This is an eight-digit number

---

`kycData` object  
Flags to capture output from KYC (Know Your Customer) screening.

---

`kycData.domesticPep` boolean **Required**  
If true, client has a positive match as a Domestic PEP (Politically Exposed Person)

---

`kycData.domesticAssociatedPep` boolean **Required**  
If true, client has a positive match as an associated person of a Domestic PEP

---

`kycData.foreignPep` boolean **Required**  
If true, client has a positive match as a Foreign PEP

---

`kycData.foreignAssociatedPep` boolean **Required**  
If true, client has a positive match as an associated person of a Foreign PEP

---

`kycData.sanctioned` boolean **Required**  
If true, client has a positive match as having a sanction

---

`employmentStatus` string

The employment status of the client – this is required for clients opening a pension

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| `Employed` |
| `Retired` |
| `Self Employed` |
| `Care Under 16s` |
| `Care Over 16` |
| `Education` |
| `Unemployed` |
| `Other` |

---

`maritalStatus` string

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| `Single` |
| `Married` |
| `Divorced` |
| `Widowed` |

---

`retirementAge` integer

The date the client is expected to retire

---

`employers` array

Contains details of the client's employer – only required where the client is making employer payments to their pension

---

`recordCreationDate` numerical string

The date the client record was created in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD)

---

`updateHistory` array

Contains details of updates made to the client record

---

item.description:
This flow will show you how to create a new client record.

Before sending the request, the client should pass through the journey below:

- Signs up and sets a password via your application's authentication system
    
- Passes a AML/KYC check
    
- Enters the required information
    
- Views and accepts the platform terms
    

At this point, you can send the request to create the client record with a status of `Active` to indicate they are ready to trade

##### National Identifiers

For clients investing in Exchange Traded Instruments – including Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), Investment Trusts, and Equities – there might be additional national identifiers required for non-GB or dual nationals in line with FCA regulation. Please refer to the **Nationalities checker.**

##### Pension clients

For clients looking to open a pension, there are some additional regulatory fields required. Please refer to the **Pension** flows.

item.description:
This section provides you with all the information you need to add new trust clients to the system with all necessary trust details. This endpoint is designed to streamline the onboarding of trust clients, ensuring that all required information is captured accurately and efficiently.

All trust types must have at least one stakeholder. Stakeholder validation for a `Bare` Trust differs slightly to other trust types, and requires one `Beneficiary` stakeholder, and one `Trustee` stakeholder with `clientAndAccountManagement` set to true.

Once the client record has been created, a GIA can be opened for the trust client. This is created using the existing account opening flow, but is limited to advised only via `wrapperDetail.advised: true`.

This section lays out how to create our different client types.

We have three types of clients

- Individual client
    
- Corporate client
    
- Trust client
    

Each client type has different requirements in order to support the types of accounts available under each client type.

If a client has already been created via the illustration route the remaining required fields should be updated through the PUT request listed [here](https://seccl-1.postman.co/workspace/6cedc952-07bb-4ba1-81c4-30de15877671/request/25991236-7f55ae41-d409-4ccd-b8b9-3914f2ca3a5b?action=share&source=copy-link&creator=25991236&ctx=documentation)

* * *

* * *

* * *

* * *

* * *

* * *

`charges.platformCharge` boolean

Indicates whether you want the charges platform charges set against the node applied to the illustration – `true` means charges apply

* * *

`charges.productCharge` boolean

`periodType` string **Required**

item.description:
You can use this set of requests to generate a product illustration and a client record with minimal information. The illustration can be provided to the client ahead of fully onboarding to the platform.

The product illustration can be used in client suitabilities and covers pre-cost disclosures under MiFID II.

Client records created via this route have a status of `Registered` – this indicates that an illustration has been generated for them but the client is missing some of the mandatory information to make `Active` and ready to trade.

The user flow to create a client through an illustration is as follows:

*   Enter the required information to create the skeletal client record
*   Complete the required fields to create the illustration
*   Download the illustration and make it available to the client
    

When the client has reviewed the illustration and is ready to fully onboard to the platform, the client:

*   Signs up and sets a password
*   Passes the AML/KYC check
*   Enters the outstanding information
*   Views and accepts the platform terms
    

At this point, you can send the request to update the client record and move the status from `Registered` to `Active`.

This section covers the below flows:

1. Nationalities checker
2. Create a client from scratch
3. Create a client from an illustration
    

To create a pension client, which requires additional fields, please see the Pension flows under Investment Accounts.

When trading Exchange-Traded instruments (ETIs), you are required to declare the client's nationality and confirm the relevant national identifiers. This flow is outlined under "Nationalities checker" and should be used before creating the actual client record on our platform.

item.description:
# PATCH /client

## Overview

This endpoint is used to update a Corporate client for a firm to manage their investments. It allows users to update information about the corporate client, including their address, entity details, and stakeholders.

- **URL**: `/client`
    
- **Method**: `PATCH`
    
- **Authentication**: `API Token`
    

## Request

### URL Parameters

No URL parameters are required for this endpoint.

### Headers

| Header | Value | Description | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | The content type of the request body | Yes |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{YOUR_API_TOKEN}}` | The API token for authentication | Yes |

### Request Body

Only updateId is a required field which can be retrieved from the GET /client endpoint.

``` json
{
    "updateId": "{{clientUpdateId}}",
    "entityName": "New Entity Name",
    "entityDetails": { 
       "legalEntityIdentifier": "529900T8BM49AURSDO55Ï"
    }
}

 ```

### Field Descriptions

All field descriptions are as per the create corporate client flows. Some fields are locked down and cannot be changed. You can find a list of fields that can be updated below:

- `nodeId` (array of strings, **required**): An array containing the node IDs associated with the firm.
    
    - `nodeId[0]` (string, **required**): The node number in which the entity will exist.
        
- `currency` (string, **required**): The currency code for the entity. Use `GBP`.
    
- `language` (string, **required**): The language code for the entity. Use `en`.
    
- `taxDomicile` (string, **required**): The entity's tax domicile country code. Use `GB`.
    
- `addressDetail` (object, **required**): The address details of the entity.
    
    - `buildingNumber` (string, **optional**): The building number in the address. Example: `301`. Must include one of `buildingNumber`, `buildingName` or `flatNumber`.
        
    - `buildingName` (string, **optional**): The building number in the address. Example: `Building Name`. Must include one of `buildingNumber`, `buildingName` or `flatNumber`.
        
    - `flatNumber` (string, **optional**): The building number in the address. Example: `301`. Must include one of `buildingNumber`, `buildingName` or `flatNumber`.
        
    - `address1` (string, **required**): The first line of the address. Example: `Cobblestone Way`.
        
    - `address2` (string, **optional**): The second line of the address. Example: `Bedrock`.
        
    - `country` (string, **required**): The country code for the address. Example: `GB`.
        
    - `postCode` (string, **required**): The postal code for the address. Example: `B70 777`.
        
- `entityDetails` (object, **required**): The details of the entity.
    
    - `companyRegNo` (string, **required**): The company registration number. Example: `07845123`.
        
    - `stakeholders` (array of objects, **required**): The list of stakeholders associated with the entity. Must have at least one stakeholder object.
        
        - `stakeholders[0]` (object, **required**): A stakeholder object.
            
            - `clientId` (string, **required**): The unique identifier of an `Individual` client already on the system. Example `00005G8`.
                
            - `role` (string, **required**): The role of the stakeholder. Must be one of `Director`, `Significant Shareholder`, `Principal Or Partner`. Significant shareholders must be associated with an AML verified `clientId`. Example: `Director`
                
            - `clientAndAccountManagement` (boolean, **optional**): Indicates if the stakeholder is involved in client and account management. Client will need to be AML verified if true. Example `true`.
                
    - `legalEntityIdentifier` (string, **optional**): The legal entity identifier. Example: `529900T8BM49AURSDO55`.
        
    - `knowYourBusiness` (object, **optional**): Information about the Know Your Business (KYB) checks. Corporate and trust KYB checks scope required to edit field.
        
        - `checksPerformed` (string, **required**): The date when KYB checks were performed. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: `2024-05-20`.
            
- `entityName` (string, **required**): The name of the entity. Example: `Bedrock Corp`.
    
- `termsAccepted` (boolean, **required**): Indicates if the terms have been accepted. Corporate and trust KYB checks scope required to set to true. Example: `true`.
    

### Stakeholders

When updating the stakeholders field, you must provide the entire stakeholder object, including ALL stakeholders. Partial updates (e.g., sending just one stakeholder to update) will overwrite the entire block, replacing all previously existing stakeholders. For example, if you have two stakeholders and want to add a third, you must send all three in the request. Similarly, to remove one, you must provide only the two remaining stakeholders in the update. Always include the full, updated stakeholder list to avoid unintentional data loss.

## Overview

This endpoint is used to create a Trust client for a firm to manage their investments. It allows users to input detailed information about the trust client, including their address, entity details, and stakeholders, to register them in the system.

- **URL**: `/client`
    
- **Method**: `PATCH`
    
- **Authentication**: `API Token`
    

## Request

### URL Parameters

### Headers

| Header | Value | Description | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | The content type of the request body | Yes |
| `Authorization` | `apitoken` | The API token for authentication | Yes |

### Request Body

Only updateId is a required field which can be retrieved from the GET /client endpoint.

``` json
{
    "updateId": "{{clientUpdateId}}",
    "entityName": "New Entity Name",
    "entityDetails": { 
       "legalEntityIdentifier": "529900T8BM49AURSDO55Ï"
    }
}

 ```

### Field Descriptions

All field descriptions are as per the create trust client flows. Some fields are locked down and cannot be changed. You can find a list of fields that can be updated below:

- `nodeId` (array of strings, **required**): An array containing the node IDs associated with the firm.
    
    - `nodeId[0]` (string, **required**): The node number in which the entity will exist.
        
- `currency` (string, **required**): The currency code for the entity. Use `GBP`.
    
- `language` (string, **required**): The language code for the entity. Use `en`.
    
- `taxDomicile` (string, **required**): The entity's tax domicile country code. Use `GB`.
    
- `addressDetail` (object, **required**): The address details of the entity.
    
    - `buildingNumber` (string, **optional**): The building number in the address. Example: 301. Must include one of `buildingNumber`, `buildingName` or `flatNumber`.
        
    - `buildingName` (string, **optional**): The building number in the address. Example: `Building Name`. Must include one of `buildingNumber`, `buildingName` or `flatNumber`.
        
    - `flatNumber` (string, **optional**): The building number in the address. Example: `301`. Must include one of `buildingNumber`, `buildingName` or `flatNumber`.
        
    - `address1` (string, **required**): The first line of the address. Example: `Cobblestone Way`.
        
    - `address2` (string, **optional**): The second line of the address. Example: `Bedrock`.
        
    - `country` (string, **required**): The country code for the address. Example: GB.
        
    - `postCode` (string, **required**): The postal code for the address. Example: B70 777.
        
- `entityDetails` (object, **required**): The details of the entity.
    
    - `uniqueTrustReference` (string, **required**): Identifier assigned to a trust to distinguish it from other trusts. Example: `1234567890`.
        
    - `stakeholders` (array of objects, **required**): The list of stakeholders associated with the entity. A bare trust must have at least one trustee with `clientAndAccountManagement` and only one beneficiary. All other trust types must have at least one trustee.
        
        - `stakeholders[0]` (object, **required**): A stakeholder object.
            
            - `clientId` (string, **required**): The unique identifier of an `Individual` client already on the system. Example `03B2D6F`.
                
            - `role` (string, **required**): The role of the stakeholder. Must be one of `Settlor`, `Beneficiary`, `Trustee`. A Beneficiary must be associated with an AML verified `clientId`. Example: `Beneficiary`
                
            - `relationshipToBeneficiary` (string, **required**): The stakeholders relationship with the trust. Only a valid & required field where role is Settlor. Example: `Parent`.
                
            - `sourceOfWealth` (string, **required**): Origin of the assets or funds that are placed into the trust. Only a valid & required field where role is Settlor. Example: `Inheritance`.
                
            - `clientAndAccountManagement` (boolean, **optional**): Indicates if the stakeholder is involved in client and account management. Client will need to be AML verified if true. Example `true`.
                
    - `legalEntityIdentifier` (string, **optional**): The legal entity identifier. Example: `529900T8BM49AURDDO55`.
        
    - `knowYourBusiness` (object, **optional**): Information about the Know Your Business (KYB) checks. Corporate and trust KYB checks scope required to add field.
        
        - `checksPerformed` (string, **required**): The date when KYB checks were performed. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: `2024-05-20`.
            
- `entityName` (string, **required**): The name of the entity. Example: `Bedrock Corp`.
    
- `termsAccepted` (boolean, **required**): Indicates if the terms have been accepted. Corporate and trust KYB checks scope required to set to true. Example: `true`.
    

The trust `type` field should not be updated.

### Stakeholders

When updating the stakeholders field, you must provide the entire stakeholder object, including ALL stakeholders. Partial updates (e.g., sending just one stakeholder to update) will overwrite the entire block, replacing all previously existing stakeholders. For example, if you have two stakeholders and want to add a third, you must send all three in the request. Similarly, to remove one, you must provide only the two remaining stakeholders in the update. Always include the full, updated stakeholder list to avoid unintentional data loss.

            - `clientAndAccountManagement` (boolean, **optional**): Indicates if the stakeholder is involved in client and account management. Client will need to be AML verified if true. Example `true`.
                
    - `legalEntityIdentifier` (string, **optional**): The legal entity identifier. Example: `529900T8BM49AURDDO55`.
        
    - `knowYourBusiness` (object, **optional**): Information about the Know Your Business (KYB) checks. Corporate and trust KYB checks scope required to add field.
        
        - `checksPerformed` (string, **required**): The date when KYB checks were performed. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: `2024-05-20`.
            
- `entityName` (string, **required**): The name of the entity. Example: `Bedrock Corp`.
    
- `termsAccepted` (boolean, **required**): Indicates if the terms have been accepted. Corporate and trust KYB checks scope required to set to true. Example: `true`.
    

The trust `type` field should not be updated.

### Stakeholders

When updating the stakeholders field, you must provide the entire stakeholder object, including ALL stakeholders. Partial updates (e.g., sending just one stakeholder to update) will overwrite the entire block, replacing all previously existing stakeholders. For example, if you have two stakeholders and want to add a third, you must send all three in the request. Similarly, to remove one, you must provide only the two remaining stakeholders in the update. Always include the full, updated stakeholder list to avoid unintentional data loss.

There are a number of reasons you might need to change a client's details – such as a change in address or marital status. It's important this information is kept up to date has it may impact regulatory reporting.

Each time an update is made to a client record, it is stored in the `updateHistory` array

To update a client record, you can follow the below steps:

1.  Retrieve the client `updateId` on the client record
2.  Update the relevant fields using a PATCH request

item.description: When making updates to a client record, you will need to retrieve the most recent update ID for the client and then apply the vulnerable customer flag using the PATCH request. This folder has collected both of these requests to demonstrate the flow with some examples.

# Introducing an additional support flag for customers

We've added the ability to flag and record details for customers who may need extra support, either now or in the future. This aligns with the FCA's focus on ensuring these customers receive proper treatment and understanding.

### What and why?

This isn’t just a regulatory improvement. We know that understanding your customers is critical to the success of your business, and you’ll already have your own processes to manage and support those with additional needs. This feature simply helps with that.

As part of the client onboarding journey, users can record if a customer requires additional support, using the four drivers identified by the FCA – health, life events, resilience and capability. These help to identify if the customer needs extra support, without revealing sensitive information.

### Try it out!

This is currently **in** **staging** so feel free to test in your designated sandbox environment.

item.description:
We have added functionality for client onboarding AML checks to be completed in an automated way via a third party provider (Northrow). When client details are first input to the system a request is sent to Northrow to run AML checks. At this point the client will not be able to login to the system until the AML checks are complete and we have received a positive response back from Northrow. Once the positive response has been received the client onboarding journey will continue.

We have also added functionality to support bank account verification either by an integrated Northrow solution or manually via API. When a bank account is first entered into the system it will have a bank account verification status of Pending. Once the bank account has been verified, either by Northrow or manually via API, the bank account will have a bank account verification status of Active. If the bank account is updated it will have a pending verification status until it is verifed. if a withdrawal is instructed to a bank account which has the pending status it will go to checking. For more information about transactions in checking please see the API documentation under Suspicious activity

If the bank account verification status functionality is not configured on then the bank account verification status will have a value of bypassed.

If you are interested in using the automated AML client onboarding or bank account verification status functionality please contact your account manager.

item.name: Nationalities checker

request.description:
Retrieves a list of nationalities and the relevant identifiers

The `static` nationality endpoint provides a list of nationalities, the ISO country codes and the national identifier that the FCA requires for reporting when trading ETIs

##### Understanding the priority

This is logic used to determine which identifier is appropriate to report on any transactions under your client's name. Priority is scored and the relevant identifiers are listed in this order under the array.

The rules for the FCA-preferred nationality are:

1.  An EEA (European Economic Area) nationality takes priority over a non-EEA nationality
2.  The nationality that comes first when the list of the client's nationalities is sorted alphabetically by the country code takes priority
3.  CONCAT is, in most cases, a last resort identifier that if required will be generated by Seccl in accordance with MiFIR/MiFID guidelines
    

**Please note: CONCAT – a combination of the client's date of birth, first name, and surname – may only be used if the Priority 1 identifier shown in the nationalities checker is not applicable to the client**

#### **Attributes**

* * *

`id` string  
The unique two-letter identifier for the nationality. This is case sensitive.=

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = GB |

* * *

`code` string  
A two-letter country code

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = GB |

* * *

`name` string  
The name of the country

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = GB |

* * *

`adjective` string  
The country descriptor

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = British |

* * *

`inEEA` boolean  
This confirms whether or not a country is in the European Economic Area (EEA). Although the UK is not in the EU anymore, it is still reported as `inEEA: true` as per MiFIR/MiFID II rules

* * *

`identifiers` array  
An array which captures all forms of national identifiers for the chosen country

* * *

`identifiers.name` string  
The name of the national identifier. This will be National Insurance Number for British nationals and National Passport Number for all other nationalities

* * *

`identifiers.regex` string  
A regular expression denoting validation for the national identifier

* * *

`identifiers.localeName` string  
The name of the national identifier

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| United Kingdom = British |

* * *

`identifiers.example` string  
An example of the alphanumeric national identifier format

* * *

`identifiers.priority` integer

The national identifier priority score

* * *

item.description:
Seccl carries out Transaction Reporting, which requires us to report complete and accurate details of transactions to the FCA on a daily basis.

For clients investing in Exchange Traded Instruments – including Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), Investment Trusts, and Equities – there might be additional national identifiers required for non-GB or dual nationals in line with FCA regulation.

The **nationalities checker** confirms what national identifier is required in priority order.

**Please note:**

- National Insurance Number is mandatory for British clients
    
- CONCAT – an identifier generated automatically by the Seccl system – may only be indicated if higher priority identifiers are not applicable to the client.
    
- We are unable to accept US Citizens at this time.
    
- Where an order is submitted in an ETI, for a client that doesn't have the required national identifiers in the nationalities array, the order will generate an exception.

Before a client can start investing on your platform, you need to create a client record. The client object allows you to manage the client's information, then create tax wrappers and accounts to begin investing. Before creating a client record in Seccl's system, the client must pass through the below journey: - Signs up and sets a password via your application's authentication system - Passes a AML/KYC check - Enters the required information - Views and accepts the platform terms At this point, you can send the request to create the client record. Investment accounts can be created before a client is active, but will only allow account actions once the associated client record is active. We have four client types, each has specifc access to different types of investment accounts. | **Client Type** | **Description** | **Available wrappers** | | --- | --- | --- | | Individual | A single client investing their own money | GIA
ISA
Pension
Third party SIPP
Third party SSAS
Third party offshore bond | | Individual Minor | A single client under 18 years of age | JISA | | Corporate | A company investing on behalf of it's shareholders | GIA | | Trust | A trust investing on behalf of its beneficiaries | GIA | #### A word on regulation ##### Know Your Customer Before you add the client's details to the system, you are required to carry out the necessary AML (Anti-Money Laundering) and KYC (Know Your Customer) checks. When the client passes the check, you can declare the “Approved” status in the client object. For example: `"amlStatus": "Approved"` In addition, you are required to indicate results of PEPs and Sanctions checks within the `kycData` object. Seccl uses this data for regulatory reporting. ##### National Identifiers Seccl carries out Transaction Reporting, which requires us to report complete and accurate details of transactions to the FCA on a daily basis. For clients investing in Exchange Traded Instruments – including Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), Investment Trusts, and Equities – there might be additional national identifiers required for non-GB or dual nationality clients in line with FCA regulation. The **nationalities checker** confirms what national identifier is required in priority order. **Please note:** - CONCAT – an automatically-generated identifier – may only be selected if higher priority identifiers, as shown in the nationalities checker, are not applicable to the client - We are unable to accept clients who are US Citizens In this section, we'll cover: - The client object - How to create a client - How to retrieve a client - How to update a client's details **Endpoints** ``` / client / portfolio/summary ```

item.name: Client fee groups
The client fee group object
item.description:
Client fee groups are not an entity of their own, but rather a special case of an entity in Seccl's API called "portfolio groups", which will not be covered in detail here.

Client fee groups have the following fields:

``` json
{
  "_id": "000AA",
  "firmId": "ZEBRA",
  "nodeId": [
    "1"
  ],
  "name": "Addams Family Group",
  "groupIntent": "Client Fee Group",
  "intentDetails": {
        "adviserFee": false,
        "platformFee": true,
        "status": "Active"
    }
}

 ```

#### **Attributes**

---

`_id` string

The unique identifier of the portfolio group object

---

`firmId` string  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`nodeId` array  
An array containing the node ID for the new group

---

`nodeId[0]` string  
Unique identifier of the firm node for the new group

---

﻿`name` string  
The custom name for the portfolio group.

---

`groupIntent` string  
Denotes the intent of the portfolio group. For client fee groups, it should be "Client Fee Group".

| Enum values |  |
| --- | --- |
| `Client Fee Group` | Client fee group |
| `Pension Account Group` | Pension account group |

---

`intentDetails` object  
A set of additional fields which are different depending on the groupIntent.

---

`intentDetails.adviserFee` boolean  
Determines if adviser fees should be grouped within a client fee group.

---

`intentDetails.platformFee` boolean  
Determines if platform fees should be grouped within a client fee group.

---

`intentDetails.status` string  
A field specific to client fee groups which denotes their status, as explained below.

| Enum values |  |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The group is actively used for fee calculation |
| `Archived` | The group is deactivated and should not have any effect on fees |

---

**The client object and client fee groups**

The clients that belong to a client fee group are not stored within the group. Instead, the group's ID is stored within each client like so:

``` json
{
  ... // other fields of the client object
  "clientGroups": [
    "clientFeeGroupId": "000AA"
  ]
}

 ```

Therefore, adding a client to a group or removing a client from a group is done by sending a PATCH request to the client endpoint.

item.description:
Clients can be added to a group by creating a PATCH request to the client object.

In order to be able to add and remove clients, you must have the client fee group user scope.

There is no limit set on how many clients a group can have, however a client can only be in one group at a time. If an attempt is made to add a client to a second group, the request will fail. Should there be a need to add a client to a group who is already a member of another group, then they will need to be removed from that group first.

A client cannot be added to a group which has been archived, the group must have an active status in order to have members.

Once a client has been added to a group, the group ID will then be visible when doing a GET request for the client.

In order to return a list of all members of a group this can be done by using the following GET request

`{{pfolioApiRoute}}/client/{{pfolioUserFirmId}}/?clientGroups[clientFeeGroupId]={{portfolioGroupId}}`

item.description:
If a group is no longer required, it can be archived. This is done by a PATCH request to the group to change the `status` to `Archived`. The date of the archiving is recorded on the group.

In order to archive a group all members should be removed first. If an attempt is made to archive a group which still has members, then the request will fail.

A group can be reinstated after archiving and made active again.

**What is a client fee group?**

A client fee group is a grouping of clients so that they each pay fees based on the total value of all their assets combined. Applies to both platform and adviser fees.

**What are they designed to do?**

Clients are charged fees based on the total value of all their assets. This is done in tiers, so the higher the total value, the lower the proportional fee. Client fee groups are designed to save clients money by allowing them to collate their assets with other clients, so that the group can fall into a higher tier which charges a smaller fee. The overall effect is that each member of the group will pay less in fees than they would as an individual not in a group.

One example would be a family group, where a platform can allow members of a family to join a client fee group together so they can have lower fees because their total asset value is combined across the family for fee tier purposes. However, client fee groups are not limited to families, and platforms can decide how to use them and restrict them.

**What will be covered in this section**

- The client fee group object
    
- Creating a client fee group
    
- Adding a client to a client fee group
    
- Removing a client from a client fee group
    
- Archiving & reinstating a client fee group
    

**Endpoints**

Operations such as creating a group and changing its status to active or archived are done using the `/portfoliogroup` endpoint, `POST` or `PATCH` respectively.

Operations such as adding or removing a client to/from a group are done using the `/client` endpoint with a `PATCH` request.

```
/portfoliogroup
/client

 ```

item.name: Assigning an adviser fee structure to an account
Update account with adviser fee structure

request.description:
Updates an existing account to assign (or change) the adviser fee structure. Account-level assignment takes the highest priority in the fee hierarchy.

Returns the updated account record.

#### **Parameters**

---

`updateId` string **Required**  
The current `updateId` of the account (optimistic concurrency control). Obtain this from the GET response.

---

`feeStructures.adviserFeeId` string  
The unique identifier for the adviser fee structure. Must be a valid fee structure of type `Adviser Fee`. Set to `null` to remove.

---

#### **Mutual exclusivity**

Only one adviser fee can be set on an account at a time. The following fields are mutually exclusive:

- `feeStructures.adviserFeeId` – fee structure reference
    
- `adviserCharge` – flat percentage rate
    
- `adviserTieredCharges` – tiered percentage rates
    

If more than one is present, the API will return a `400` validation error.

#### **Migrating from flat charge to fee structure**

If an account currently has `adviserCharge` or `adviserTieredCharges` set and you want to switch to a fee structure, you must clear the existing fee in the same request:

``` json
{
  "updateId": "64c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a4",
  "adviserCharge": null,
  "feeStructures": {
    "adviserFeeId": "64f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1"
  }
}

 ```

> **Note**: If you only send `feeStructures.adviserFeeId` but the account already has `adviserCharge` persisted, the mutual exclusivity check will still fail because the merged entity would have both. You must explicitly null out the old fee structure. 
  

#### **Removing the adviser fee structure**

To remove an adviser fee structure from an account, set the value to `null`:

``` json
{
  "updateId": "64c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a4",
  "feeStructures": {
    "adviserFeeId": null
  }
}

 ```

#### **Error responses**

---

`400` Please provide only one: Adviser Tiered Charges, Adviser Charge, Fee Structures Adviser Fee Id  
Mutual exclusivity violated – more than one adviser fee structure is set

---

`400` Adviser fee structure is not permitted on TPOFFBOND accounts  
The account's wrapper type is `TPOFFBOND`

---

`400` Fee structure not found  
The provided ID does not match any fee structure

---

`400` Fee structure type is not Adviser Fee  
The fee structure exists but is not of type `Adviser Fee`

## Overview

Fee structures allow you to define and assign custom fee configurations to clients, accounts, and client fee groups. This provides flexibility in fee management without requiring client switching between nodes and repeatedly inputting the same fee.

Fee structures can be used to:

- Create and manage multiple fee configurations that can be reused across clients, accounts and client groups
    
- Seamlessly switch clients between different fee structures as needed
    

## Fee structure types

Two fee structure types are supported:

- **Platform fee** – assigned to **clients only** via `client.feeStructures.platformFeeId`
    
- **Adviser fee** – assigned to accounts, clients, or client fee groups via `feeStructures.adviserFeeId`
    

Self-service creation and management of fee structures is currently unsupported via the API and will come at a later date. You can list and retrieve existing fee structures using `GET /v1/fee-structures` and `GET /v1/fee-structures/:id`. If you are looking to create or update a fee structure for your firm, please raise a ticket with the support team.

## Fee priority hierarchy

### Platform fees

When a fee event is triggered, the system checks for adviser fee configuration in this order (first found wins):

1. Fee structure on client (`client.feeStructures.platformFeeId` )
    
2. Standard platform charge configured on the client's nearest node in the hierarchy
    

> **Note**: Platform fees are only supported at the client level. Setting `platformFeeId` on accounts or client fee groups is not **currently** supported. 
  

### Adviser fees

When fee event is triggered, the system checks for adviser fee configuration in this order (first found wins):

1. Fee structure on account (`account.feeStructures.adviserFeeId)`
    
2. Account legacy fee (`adviserCharge` or `adviserTieredCharges`) – flat or tiered rates directly on account
    
3. Fee structure on client (`client.feeStructures.adviserFeeId` )
    
4. Fee structure on group (`clientFeeGroup.intentDetails.feeStructures.adviserFeeId` )
    
5. Node charge (via node traversal)
    

> Note: Adviser fee structures can be set simultaneously at account, client and client fee group level — the fee priority hierarchy above determines which one is used when a fee event is triggered. Mutual exclusivity only applies within an account: `feeStructures.adviserFeeId`, `adviserCharge`, and `adviserTieredCharges` cannot coexist on the same account. To stop using an account-level fee and fall back to the client / group / node fee, explicitly set the active field (\`adviserCharge\` or `feeStructures.adviserFeeId`) to null.

item.name: Investment accounts
The client product object
item.description:
This represents the wrapper information of your client. A client product is automatically created when an investment account is created for the first time. There is a single client product per wrapper type per client record.

The client product record stores information related to the product including remaining allowance, date product terms accepted, details on the client's beneficiaries.

``` json
{
    "id": "{{clientProductId}}"
    "firmId": "{{firmId}}",
    "nodeId": "0",
    "clientIds": ["{{clientId}}"],
    "wrapperType": "PENSION",
    "schemeProductId": "{{schemeProductId}}",
    "declarationAcceptedDate":"2022-12-10",
    "declarationExpiryDate":"2023-12-10",
    "expressionOfWishNominations":[
        {
          "title": "Mr"
          "surname": "Flinstone"
          "firstName": "Fred"
          "beneficiaryRelationship": "Husband"
          "beneficiaryProportion": 1
        }    
    ],
    "productName":"Flinstone Pension Account",
    "externalIds":[
        {
          "value": "DW123456",
          "idType": "Gaudi"
        }
       ],
    "acceptedProviderTerms": true,
    "acceptedProviderTermsDate":"2022-12-10",
    "productStatus":"drawdownConfirmed",
    "incomeAccountId":"{{accountId}}",
    "auditDetails": {
        "updateDate": "2022-07-11T09:16:46.220Z",
         "userFirmId": "SECCI",
         "userId": "029B3FF",
         "version": 1,
         "application": "PfolioAPI"
        },
      "updateId": "62cbea7e556e7ce6230b80f0",
}

 ```

### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the client product

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`nodeId` numerical string

The node Id that the client record is attached to

---

﻿`clientIds` array

Contains the associated client Ids

---

`wrapperType` string

The type of wrapper that the client product relates

| Enum values | Description |
| --- | --- |
| GIA | General Investment Account |
| ISA | Individual Savings Account |
| PENSION | SIPP |
| TPPENSION | Third Party Pension |
| JISA | Junior ISA |
| SSAS | Small Self-Administered Schemes (Pension) |
| TPOFFBOND | Third Party Offshore Bonds |

---

`schemeProductId` alphanumerical string

The scheme product Id of the product – this is relevant for pension products

---

`declarationAcceptedDate` numerical string

The date the client accepted the ISA terms

---

`declarationExpiryDate` numerical string

The date the ISA declaration expires – if the client opens an ISA, accepts the declaration and doesn't contribute for an entire tax year, they will be required to re-accept the ISA declaration in order to contribute

---

`expressionOfWishNominations` array

Contains details of the client's nominated beneficiaries for their pension

---

`productName` string

Name of the product

---

`updateId` string

The unique identifier assigned to the record the last time it was updated

---

`externalIds` array

Contains details of external account Ids of the product provider

---

`acceptedProviderTerms` boolean

Indicates that the client has accepted the pension terms

---

`acceptedProviderTermsDate` numerical string

The date the client accepted the pension terms

---

`productStatus` string

The status of the pension

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `drawdownPending` | The clients wants to take income from their pension |
| `drawdownConfirmed` | The client has taken income from their pension |

---

`productDetail` array

Contains details of the client's drawdown pension, including crystallisation amount, the benefit commencement date, the money purchase allowance, and the lifetime allowance percentage

---

`incomeAccountId` string

The unique identifier of the investment account that the client wishes to take income from – this is relevant for Gaudi pensions only

---

`updateHistory` array

Contains details of updates made to the client product record

---

item.name: The scheme product object
item.description:
This represents a scheme product setup in Seccl's system

\* Each scheme is a legal entity that has the ability to appoint an administrator  
\* This endpoint returns all scheme products setup for your firm, which could include multiple pension schemes, as well as other third party product, such as Small Self-Administered Pensions (SSAS) and offshore bonds  
\* Within the scheme, you can have different products which can be white labelled

request.description:
Creates a GIA for a client Returns the unique identifier `accountId` (`id`) for the GIA To create a GIA with an investment strategy, refer to the examples under this request. #### **Parameters** --- `firmId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the firm --- `nodeId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the firm node's account --- `accountType` string **Required** The type of account - current functionality only supports wrapper type | **Enum values** | | --- | | Wrapper | --- `name` string **Required** The name of the investment account --- `status` string **Required** The status of the account | **Enum values** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | `Pending` | The client hasn't viewed and accepted the platform terms | | `Active` | The client has viewed and accepted the platform terms.

Active accounts can only be created when linked to an active client. | --- `adviserCharge` decimal string The fee amount charged by an adviser for managing the investment account --- `discretionaryManagementCharge` decimal string The fee amount charged by a discretionary fund manager for managing the investment account --- `currency` string **Required** Three-letter **ISO code for the currency** paid in or out of the account. Currently only GBP --- `clientId` string **Required** The unique identifier for a client. --- `wrapperDetail` The details of the chosen investment account --- `wrapperDetail.wrapperType` enum **Required** The type of tax wrapper | **Enum values** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | GIA | General Investment Account | `wrapperDetail.discretionary` boolean Indicates that the investment decision maker is the discretionary fund manager if set to `true` – this impacts transaction reporting --- `wrapperDetail.advised` boolean Indicates that the management of the account is owned by the adviser if set to `true` --- `wrapperDetail.trust` boolean Indicates if the account is a trust. Trust account will require an LEI to trade in ETIs --- `wrapperDetail.assetAllocationId` The unique identifier for a model attached to the account – any transactions created with an auto-invest flag set to true will be invested into this allocation. Please note, changing the model on an account will automatically trigger a rebalance. --- `wrapperDetail.clientProductId` The unique identifier for the clientProduct that the account is contained within --- `recurringOrders` object Contains details of the recurringOrders allocation, if applicable. If this account is attached to a model (i.e. has `assetAllocationId` set in `wrapperDetail` - it should not contain `recurringOrders`. See documentation on Investment Strategies > Recurring orders for more information. --- `recurringOrders.movementType` string **Required when recurringOrders present** The movement of cash or assets – this should be set to `Invest` --- `recurringOrders.investmentType` **Required when recurringOrders present** The type of investment strategy – this should be set to `Bespoke` --- `recurringOrders.details` array **Required when recurringOrders present** Contains details of the asset allocation --- `recurringOrders.details.assetId` string **Required when recurringOrders present** The unique identifier of the asset --- `recurringOrders.details.percentage` number **Required when recurringOrders present** The percentage allocation of the asset, expressed as a decimal, eg. 0.1 --- `recurringOrders.orderDay` integer **Required when recurringOrders present** A recurring day of the month, when the orders will be created. --- `recurringPayments` array Contains details of recurring contributions to the account. See documentation on Investment Strategies > Recurring orders > Auto-invest a payment to recurring order allocation for more information. --- `recurringPayments.paymentDay` integer **Required if recurringOrders present** A recurring day of the month, when the payment will be made by the client into their investment account. --- `recurringPayments.amount` number **Required if recurringOrders present** A recurring amount which will be requested as a bank transfer into the investment account. --- `recurringPayments.movementType` string **Required if recurringOrders present** Whether cash is travelling in or out of an account. | **Enum value** | | --- | | In | | Out | --- `recurringPayments.method` string **Required if recurringOrders present** Method by which payment will be made. | **Enum values** | | --- | | Bank transfer
Direct debit | --- `recurringPayments.autoInvest` boolean Whether the incoming cash is automatically invested in assets. --- `externalReference` string A maximum of 256 characters containing alphanumeric, spaces, dashes and underscores only.

item.description:
An income statement is a regulated document which shows how much income your client's investments have produced and any tax deducted.

It also shows the investor's share of the fund’s income and the fund manager decides how to invest it.

These are generated for clients that hold a GIA annually, after Tax Year End.

This section will show you how to generate and retrieve an income statement.

**Please note: our API refers to the Income statement as a** **`taxstatement`**

A General Investment Account (GIA) is a tax wrapper in which a client can hold both investments and cash. A GIA can be opened by any UK adult over the age of 18. Unlike ISAs or SIPPs, GIAs do not benefit from tax advantages. As such, any realised gains or losses caused by the purchase or sale of assets are subject to **capital gains tax** – payable by the investor. The GIA may also be subject to income tax on any income paid. Before an investment account is created, the client must have viewed and accepted the platform terms. GIAs are available for the following client types | **Available to** | | --- | | Individuals
Corporate clients
Trust clients | ## GIA Account Object ``` json { "id": "{{accountId}}" "firmId": "{{firmId}}", "nodeId": "{{nodeId}}", "accountType": "Wrapper", "name": "Wilma's GIA", "status": "Active", "adviserCharge": 0.01, "discretionaryManagementCharge": 0, "currency": "GBP", "clientId": "{{clientId}}", "wrapperDetail": { "wrapperType": "GIA", "discretionary": false, "advised": false, "assetAllocationId": "{{modelId}}", "clientProductId": "{{cliendProductId}}" } } ```

item.name: Joint General Investment Account (Joint GIA)
Create a Joint GIA

request.description:
Creates a Joint GIA that is owned equally by two clients.

Returns the unique identifier `accountId`(`id`) for the Joint GIA. Only one Joint GIA client product can be created per client, though multiple accounts can be created under this client product. The joint GIA client product is considered a separate entity from an individual GIA client product.

To create a Joint GIA with an investment strategy, refer to the examples under this request. Ownership of assets within the joint GIA are considered joint.

We use the `isLeadClient` flag for one of the clients to denote use of personal details for certain account flows, such as using bank details for matching deposits and paying out withdrawals.

To create a Joint GIA between two clients, provide the `clients` property, instead of the `clientId` property on request.

#### **Parameters**

---

`firmId` string **Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`nodeId` string **Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm node's account

---

`accountType` string **Required**  
The type of account

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| Wrapper |

---

`name` string  
The name of the investment account

---

`status` string  
The status of the account

| **Enum values** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The clients have viewed and accepted the product terms |
| `Suspended` | The account is suspended – all transactions are blocked |
| `Pending` | The account is created however requires clients to view and accept product terms. |

---

`adviserCharge` decimal string  
The fee amount charged by an adviser for managing the investment account

---

`discretionaryManagementCharge` decimal string  
The fee amount charged by a discretionary fund manager for managing the investment account

---

`currency` string **Required**  
Three-letter **ISO code for the currency** paid in or out of the account

---

`clients` Array **Required**  
The unique identifier for a client pairing to create a joint GIA. Two clients must be specified.

---

`clients.id` string **Required**  
The client Id of clients associated with the joint gia, must be a valid client `individual client`

clients must be of status `pending` or `active`

---

`clients.isLeadClient` boolean **Required**  
An identifier for the client whose bank details will be used for the account. Only one client within the provided `clients` array can be set to the lead client.

---

`wrapperDetail` array **Required**  
The details of the chosen investment account

---

`wrapperDetail.wrapperType` string **Required**  
The type of tax wrapper

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| `GIA` |

---

`wrapperDetail.discretionary` boolean

Indicates whether the account is managed on a discretionary basis

---

`wrapperDetail.advised` boolean

Indicates whether the account is managed on an advised basis

---

`wrapperDetail.assetAllocationId` numerical string

The unique identifier of the model attached to the account

---

`wrapperDetail.declarationAcceptedDate` Date

A flag to signify that GIA declaration terms have been accepted by clients prior to account creation, this flag will be used to note that clients have accepted product terms and the account will be active.

item.description:
A Joint General Investment Account (Joint GIA) allows two individual clients to co-own and manage investment assets within a single account structure. Typically used by family members, spouses, or partners, these accounts provide a streamlined way to build and manage an investment portfolio.

## Key features

- **Dual ownership**: Assets held within the account legally belong to both account holders via joint tenancy
    
- **Shared access**: Both account holders have equal authority to view account information, execute trades, and withdraw funds. Joint GIAs will appear on both clients' valuation statements.
    
- **Easy movement of funds:** Both account holders can easily move cash between their individually owned and jointly owned accounts, subject to usual wrapper rules and limits

item.description: This section shows you how to retrieve a client's portfolio summary and manage their ISA allowance.

An Individual Savings Account (ISA) is a tax-efficient wrapper which allows investors to save up to £20,000 annually tax free. Seccl operates a **flexible Stocks and Shares ISA**. This means that withdrawals deposited within the same tax year do not impact the investor's ISA £20,000 annual allowance.

To be eligible to subscribe to a Stocks and Shares ISA the client must be: 18 or over and a resident in the UK (or if not a resident, must meet the conditions set in the declaration).

Seccl is both an ISA manager and administers ISAs for other ISA managers. For more details and guidance around ISAs and becoming an ISA manager, please refer to the [HMRC website](https://www.gov.uk/individual-savings-accounts).

Before a client account is created, they must accept the relevant documents associated with ISAs:

\* Terms & Conditions  
\* Key Features  
\* Product terms  
\* Tax declaration

This above is captured under **Accept the ISA declaration**.

You can open an ISA with the declaration accepted by passing in the relevant property under the `wrapperDetail` property. After the ISA is opened, you will need to retrieve the ISA to make available the ISA replay which confirms the declaration that the client has accepted.

ISAs are available for the following client types:

| **Available to** |
| --- |
| Individuals |

## ISA Account Object

``` json
{
    "id": "{{accountId}}"
    "firmId": "{{firmId}}",
    "nodeId": "{{nodeId}}",
    "accountType": "Wrapper",
    "name": "Wilma's ISA",
    "status": "Active",
    "adviserCharge": 0.01,
    "discretionaryManagementCharge": 0,
    "currency": "GBP",
    "clientId": "{{clientId}}",
    "wrapperDetail": {
        "wrapperType": "GIA",
        "discretionary": false,
        "advised": false,
        "assetAllocationId": "{{modelId}}",
        "clientProductId": "{{clientProductId}}",
        "declarationAcceptedDate": "2025-01-01"
    }
}

 ```

item.description:
This section shows you how to create and retrieve a Junior Individual Savings Account (JISA) and child clients under a parent client.

The JISA product is a single account which holds two clients - The adult client and the child client.

In order to create a JISA, you will need:

\- A parent client  
\- A JISA account under the parent client  
\- A child client who will sit under the JISA product alongside the parent. They will need minimal details and will inherit most contact information from their parents by default - unless specified.

item.description: This section shows you how to close a JISA account when there is no transactional history.

A Junior Individual Savings Account (JISA) is a tax-efficient wrapper which allows investors to save up to £9,000 annually tax-free. A JISA cannot be operated as a flexible account. Investments (including cash and the income earned by Junior Individual Savings Account investments) may only be withdrawn in the following circumstances according to HMRC:

- where a terminal illness claim made on behalf of the child has been agreed
    
- on closure of the Junior ISA (JISA)
    
- to meet certain provider management charges and other specific expenses – allowable charges and deductions under the management agreement include redemption of units at the investor’s request to pay charges due to their adviser
    

To be eligible to subscribe to a Stocks and Shares JISA, the adult client must be over 18, a registered contact for the child client such as a parent or guardian and a resident in the UK. The child client must be under 18 and a resident in the UK (or if not a resident, must meet the conditions set in the declaration).

Seccl is both a JISA manager and administers JISAs for other JISA managers. For more details and guidance around JISAs and becoming an JISA manager, please refer to the [HMRC website](https://www.gov.uk/junior-individual-savings-accounts).

Before a client account is created, they must accept the relevant documents associated with JISAs:

\* Terms & Conditions  
\* Key Features  
\* Product terms  
\* Tax declaration

The above is captured under **Accept the JISA declaration**.

After the JISA is opened, you will need to retrieve the JISA client product which confirms the the client's declaration acceptance and date.

As this is an individual client product, your client's JISA allowance will not be affected by other adjacent client products such as another JISA or ISA.

JISAs are available for the following client types

| **Available to** |
| --- |
| Individual minors |

## JISA Account Object

``` json
{
    "id": "{{accountId}}"

            "id": "{{childClientId}}",

        }

        "assetAllocationId": "{{modelId}}",
        "clientProductId": "{{clientProductId}}",

}
 ```

item.description:
Creates a Seccl pension account

## Pension Account Groups

Each Seccl pension account belongs to a type of Pension Account Group:

- uncrystallised - accounts that are still in accumulation
    
- crystallised - accounts that have been crystallised at Seccl
    
- crystallised transfer - crystallised accounts that have been transferred to Seccl
    
- beneficiary - inherited pension accounts
    

The type of Pension Account Group determines what actions are allowed. For example, income payments cannot be made out of uncrystallised accounts.

Crystallised transfer and beneficiary accounts have an additional name property for their Pension Account Group. This is required for us to segregate different transfers. For example, your old pension account from one provider would be kept separate from your account from another provider by having different names on the Pension Account Group.

If a Pension Account Group is not specified in the account creation request, it will by default belong to an uncrystallised group.

#### **Parameters**

---

`firmId` string **Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`nodeId` string **Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm node's account

---

`accountType` string **Required**  
The type of account

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| `Wrapper` |

---

`name` string **Required**  
The name of the investment account

---

`status` string **Required**  
The status of the account – you can create the account with a status of `Active` if the client has viewed and accepted the product terms and declaration

| **Enum values** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Pending` | Client needs to view and accept terms – transactions blocked |
| `Active` | Client has viewed and accepted terms |
| `Suspended` | Account suspended – transactions blocked |

---

`adviserCharge` decimal string

The fee amount charged by an adviser for managing the investment account

---

`discretionaryManagementCharge` decimal string

The fee amount charged by a discretionary fund manager for managing the investment account

---

`currency` string **Required**

Three-letter **ISO code for the currency** paid in or out of the account

---

`clientId` string **Required**

The unique identifier for a client

---

`wrapperDetail` object **Required**

The details of the chosen investment account

---

`wrapperDetail.wrapperType` string **Required**

The type of tax wrapper

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| `PENSION` |

---

`wrapperDetail.schemeProductId` **Required**

The unique identifier of the Seccl pension – this should be retrieved from the GET scheme product endpoint

---

`wrapperDetail.nominations`

Contains details on the client's nominated beneficiaries of their pension

---

`wrapperDetail.nominations.title` string

The title of the client's nominee

---

`wrapperDetail.nominations.firstName` string **Required if nomination being submitted**

The first name of the client's nominee

---

`wrapperDetail.nominations.surname` string **Required if nomination being submitted**

The surname of the client's nominee

---

`wrapperDetail.nominations.beneficiaryRelationship` string **Required if nomination being submitted**

The relationship of the nominee to the client

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| `CHARITY` |
| `HUSBAND` |
| `WIFE` |
| `DAUGHTER` |
| `SON` |
| `PARTNER` |
| `OTHER` |

---

`wrapperDetail.nominations.beneficiaryProportion` integer **Required if nomination being submitted**

The percentage allocation as a decimal place to the nominated beneficiary. Across beneficiaires this must equal 100%

---

`wrapperDetail.acceptedProviderTerms` boolean **Required** **`true`** **to open the account as Active**

A boolean denoting that the provider terms have been accepted

---

`wrapperDetail.acceptedProviderTermsDate` string **Required to open the account as Active**

A date string for when the provider terms were accepted, for example `'2026-01-15'`

---

`productDetail` object **Required**

Contains mandatory regulatory information about the client

---

`productDetail.flexibleBenefitsAccessed` boolean **Required**

Indicates whether the client has triggered the money purchase allowance rules. Where a client is under 55 this can be defaulted to false.

---

`productDetail.flexiAccessDate` numerical string **Required if** **`flexibleBenefitsAccessed: true`**

Year in which the client triggered money purchase allowance rules in ISO date format

---

`productDetail.pensionOptOut` boolean **Required**

Indicates if the client has opted out of joining an employer's scheme

---

`portfolioGroups` array **Required if account is of crystallised, crystallised transfer or beneficiary types**

Contains an object describing the pension account group that this account should belong to

---

`portfolioGroups.groupIntent` string **Required**

The intent of the portfolio group

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| `Pension Account Group` |

---

`portfolioGroups.groupType` string **Required**

The type of the Pension Account Group

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| `Uncrystallised` |
| `Crystallised` |
| `CrystallisedTransfer` |
| `Beneficiary` |

---

`portfolioGroups.name` string

The name of the Pension Account Group, only used with groupTypes of `CrystallisedTransfer` and `Beneficiary` to segregate multiple transfers from different providers

---

`externalReference` string

A maximum of 256 characters containing alphanumeric, spaces, dashes and underscores only.

When a client opens a pension, they are required to review and accept the product declaration, product terms and key features document. These should be presented to the client during sign-up.

To indicate that the client has viewed and accepted the regulatory documents, you need to update the `clientproduct` record. This only needs to be done when the first pension account is opened.

item.description:
As of April 6th, 2024, the 'lifetime allowance' (LTA), which formerly limited the total amount of pension benefits you could accumulate while still enjoying full tax benefits, has been replaced by a 'lump sum allowance' (LSA). The LSA sets a limit on the tax-free cash you can receive from your pension, typically £268,275. This section outlines how you can use our API to comply with these legislative changes. ## Mini Glossary | Variable | Definition | **Comments** | | --- | --- | --- | | Transitional tax free certificate

`transitionalTaxFreeAmount` | A member can request one of these from a scheme. This certificate provides evidence of all pre April 6th 2024 LSA (lump-sum allowance) and LSDBA (lump-sum death benefits allowance) used. | If one of these is provided the crystallisation will be held at waiting until our operations team certifies its validity. | | Lump sum allowance used pre 6th April 2024 - "Deemed LSA usage"

`lumpSumAllowanceUsedPreApril2024` | This is the calculated figure that converts a members LTA usage pre 6th April 2024 to an equivalent LSA usage. | This figure is in replacement to the transitional tax free amount certificate. | ## This section shows you how to: - Retrieve the `clientproduct` Id from the account record - Retrieve the `clientproduct` updateId - Update the `clientproduct` with the required information ## Flow diagrams of how our UI guides users down relevant journeys

item.description:
This section details how to perform a regular crystallisation. The body of the requests are outlined below and differ depending on the crystallisation type UFPLS (uncrystallised funds pension lump sum), or FAD (flexi access drawdown).

## UFPLS

``` json
{
    "accountId": "{{accountId}}",
    "advised": true,
    "fcaIndividualReference": "ABC123",
    "benefitsTakenBefore2006": false,
    "protectedRetirementAgeOrLumpSum": false,
    "crystallisationDetails": {
        "type": "UFPLS",
        "frequency": "Regular",
        "crystallisationDay": 21,
        "amount": 2000,
        "expiryDate": "2026-02-01"
    },
    "firmId": "{{pfolioUserFirmId}}",
    "guidance": true
}

 ```

## FAD

``` json
{
    "accountId": "{{accountId}}",
    "advised": true,
    "fcaIndividualReference": "ABC123",
    "benefitsTakenBefore2006": false,
    "protectedRetirementAgeOrLumpSum": false,
    "accountDetails": {
        "name": "Drawdown Account"
    },
    "crystallisationDetails": {
        "type": "FAD",
        "frequency": "Regular",
        "crystallisationDay": 28,
        "amount": 3812,
        "expiryDate": "2026-02-01"
    },
    "firmId": "{{pfolioUserFirmId}}",
    "guidance": true,
    "withdrawalDetails": [
        {
            "transactionType": "Payment",
            "transactionSubType": "PCLS",
            "amount": 953,
            "frequency": "Single",
            "method": "BACS Credit",
            "movementType": "Out"
        },
        {
            "transactionType": "Payment",
            "transactionSubType": "FAD",
            "grossAmount": 1057,
            "frequency": "Single",
            "method": "BACS Credit",
            "movementType": "Out"
        }
    ]

 ```

## Attributes

### Crystallisation summary

`accountId` string **\- Required**

The uncrystallised account that was used for the benefit crystallisation instruction

---

`advised` boolean **\- Required**

Whether regulated advice was given for the benefit application - must be true

---

`fcaIndividualReference` string **\- Required**

The FCA individual reference number for the benefit application

---

`benefitsTakenBefore2006` boolean **\- Required**

Whether the client has taken benefits from their pension before the 6th April 2006

---

`protectedRetirementAgeOrLumpSum` boolean - **Required**

Whether the client has a protected early retirement age or scheme-specific tax-free lump sum protection

---

`accountDetails` objects **\- Required for FAD only**

Initial details provided about the crystallisation account for FAD. Will contain either

---

`accountDetails.name` string **\- Required**  
if a new account was to be created

or

`accountDetails.id` string **\- Required**  
if an existing account was to be used

---

### Crystallisation details

`crystallisationDetails` object **\- Required**  
The details of the crystallisation that was performed

---

`crystallisationDetails.type` string **\- Required**

Describes the pension access option

---

`crystallisationDetails.frequency` string **\- Required**

Describes the cadence of the crystallisation for regular please provide `Regular`

---

`crystallisationDetails.day` number **\- Required**

Dictates the day of the crystallisation each month (validation for this being < 28)

---

`crystallisationDetails.amount` number **\- Required**

Dictates the gross amount being crystallised

---

`crystallisationDetails.expiryDate` string

Dictates the date of the last crystallisation in the series. Crystallisations will be processed up to but not including this date.

---

### Firm metadata

`firmId` string **\- Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`guidance` boolean **\- Required**

Whether the client received guidance from Pension Wise

---

### Withdrawal details

`withdrawalDetails` array **\- Required for FAD only**  
The details of the any associated withdrawals for the instruction for FAD. It can contain an array of the following fields

---

`withdrawalDetails.transactionType` string **\- Required for FAD only**  
The type of transaction, usually Payment

---

`withdrawalDetails.transactionSubType` string **\- Required for FAD only**  
The sun type of transaction, which will be PCLS or FAD

---

`withdrawalDetails.method` string **\- Required for FAD only**  
The type of payment method

---

`withdrawalDetails.movementType` string **\- Required for FAD only**  
The movement type, which will be Out

---

`withdrawalDetails.frequency` string **\- Required for FAD only**  
This will be Single (a single withdrawal every month)

---

`withdrawalDetails.amount` number **\- Required for FAD only**  
The amount of a PCLS payment

---

`withdrawalDetails.grossAmount` number **\- Required for FAD only**  
The gross amount requested for a FAD payment
