To cancel a regular crystallisation series `PATCH` with the status cancelled

``` json
{
    "status": "Cancelled",
    "updateId": "{{bcirUpdateId}}"
}

 ```

## Attributes

`status` string **\- Required**

The status of the regular crystallisation, patch to `Cancelled` in order to cancel the regular crystallisation sereis

---

`updateId` string **\- Required**

Unique update ID

There are potentially considerable tax, income stream, and investment strategy advantages in drip feeding your pension benefits through a series of crystallisations rather than crystallising your whole pot in one go.

This can be done on an ad-hoc basis, whereby benefit crystallisations are carried out as and when required by the end client (we already support this)

**OR** it can be done by a series of identical crystallisations over a prolonged period of time - **Regular crystallisations** - which is the scope of this piece of work:

- Removes human error from ad-hoc crystallisations
- Removes manual burden on advisers having to conduct ad-hoc crystallisations
- End investors gains tax, income, and investment advantages

Drawdown describes the process of using your pension pot to provide income for retirement.

This income can be taken in various ways, depending on your situation.

This drawdown flow is for advised offerings only.

Seccl administer tax reclaims, payroll systems and the instruction of tax and withdrawal amounts for your clients.

**Income types offered by Seccl:**

\* Pension Commencement Lump Sum (PCLS) - this enables you to take a portion of your pension without paying any tax up to 25%.  
\* Flexi-Access Drawdown (FAD) - this is income from your pension that doesn’t have a tax free portion.

\* Uncrystallised Funds Pension Lump Sum (UFPLS) - this enables you to take a lump sum of your pension without paying any tax up to 25% and without creating a drawdown account.

This section will show you how your client can draw an income from their Seccl pension.

**Pre-requisites**

\* The client must have an existing accumulation pension with Seccl.  
\* The client must be aged 55 or older.

item.name: Produce SMPI
item.description:
Seccl is introducing functionality to produce Statutory Money Purchase Illustrations (SMPI). The output of this will be used in Seccl-produced annual statements for clients in accumulation. You will not need to use this endpoint unless you are producing your own annual statements.

This will be an illustration projecting fund values to the client's selected retirement age following the methodology laid out by the Financial Reporting Council (FRC) in [AS TM1 - Actuarial Standard Technical Memorandum](https://www.frc.org.uk/library/standards-codes-policy/actuarial/actuarial-standard-technical-memorandum-as-tm1/)

The illustration aims to provide a projected value (in real terms) of a client's uncrystallised pension, and also give an estimate of the annual annuity that this could produce (under certain assumptions).

As the Seccl SIPP supports having multiple uncrystallised accounts, the SMPI tool is designed to project each account separately and aggregate the results at the end to provide the overall position at the client's retirement date.

The body of the SMPI request will be of the following form:

``` json
{
    "type": "SMPI",
    "firmId": "{{pfolioUserFirmId}}",
    "clientId": "{{clientId}}",
    "clientProductId": "{{clientProductId}}",
    "nodeId": "{{nodeId}}",
    "valuationDate": "2024-05-01",
    "valuationData": [
        {
            "accountId": "{{account1Id}}",
            "startValuation": 1234.56
        },
        {
            "accountId": "{{account2Id}}",
            "startValuation": 3456.78
        },
    ],
    "retirementAge": 67,
    "retirementDate": "2042-03-24",
    "otherPlatformHoldings": 456.78
}

 ```

## Attributes

`type` string **\- Required**

The type of illustration to be produced - must be "SMPI" for these illustrations

---

`firmId` string **\- Required**

The unique identifier for the firm

---

`clientId` string **\- Required**

The client that the SMPI is for

---

`clientProductId` string **\- Required**

The clientProductId that the SMPI is for - this must be for a PENSION or TPPENSION wrapperType

---

`nodeId` string **\- Required**

The nodeId for the client

---

`valuationDate` string - **Required**

The date that the SMPI will project from

---

`valuationData` array - **Required**

A collection of account details for the illustration consisting of the following:

`accountId` string - **Required**

A PENSION or TPPENSION account ID

`startValuation` number - **Required**

The valuation of the associated account as at `valuationDate`

---

`retirementDate` string - **Required**

The date when the client expects to retire. This will be the end point of the illustration. This must be in the future.

---

`retirementAge` number - **Required**

The client's age at retirementDate.

---

`otherPlatformHoldings` number - **Optional**

If provided, this value will be taken into account when detemining platform charges for the illustrated accounts.

## Output

When you retrieve an SMPI illustration, it will consist of the following:

`id` string - the ID of the illustration

`updateId` string - the updateId of the illustration

`firmId` string - the ID of the firm

`request` object - an object containing the original request data

`assumptions` object - an object containing the assumptions used in the illustration. This will include growth rates, annuity factors and inflation rates

`calculations` array - an array containing period by period calculations for each account throughout the duration of the illustration

`outputs` object - an object containing the pertinent results of the illustration:

`endValue` number - the nominal value at the end date

`endValueReal` number - the inflation adjusted end value to give the value in real terms at valuation date.

`annuityValue` number - the estimated annual annuity figure provided in real terms at valuation date.

The Seccl personal pension is operated and administered by Seccl. Its aim is a fully digital, inherently flexible and infinitely scalable pension solution, built using our in-house technology.

This section shows you how to:

- Create a client record, including the data fields required to open a pension.
    
- Create a Seccl pension account.
    
- Accept the pension terms.
    
- Retrieve the pension declaration confirmation.
    
- Retrieve the pension cancellation document.
    
- Update nominees.
    
- Take income.
    

**Creating a client**

When opening a pension for a client, you'll need to collect some additional information. This includes the client's title, retirement age, marital status and employer information.

There are two ways to create a pension client:

1. Create a pension client through an illustration – creates an illustration PDF and a skeletal client record with a status of `Registered`
    
2. Create a pension client – creates a full client record with a status of `Active`
    

**Creating a payment contribution**

When contributing to a pension, the client needs to specify whether the payment is a personal contribution or an employer contribution.

**Regulatory documents**

There are some additional regulatory documents related to the client's pension that are made available via the Seccl API. These include:

\* Pension cancellation letter  
\* P60  
\* Payslip

Seccl has the ability to hold third party products on the platform. These describe wrappers whereby the administration is carried out by another provider; Seccl provides trading & custody services only in regards to these accounts.

This functionality allows clients and users to:

\* Consolidate the platform serviceable assets held in third party products onto the platform  
\* Link the third party product's bank account – any cash contributions or withdrawals are processed to these bank details  
\* Store a Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) on the account – this is used for regulatory transaction reporting

**Please note: Withdrawals instructed on investment accounts that have bank details set are sent to those bank details, not the bank details held on the client account**

| --- | --- |
| `TPPENSION` | Third Party Pension |
| `SSAS` | Small Self Administered Scheme |
| `TPOFFBOND` | Third Party Offshore Bond |

There are many reasons why you might need to update a client's investment account. This might include:

\*   Switching the investment strategy
\*   Updating the adviser charge
\*   Adding a recurring payment
\*   Editing the account name
    

To update an investment account, you can follow the below steps:

1.  Retrieve the `updateId` from the account object
2.  Instruct a `PATCH` request with the fields to be updated and the account `updateId`
    

An audit trail of updates made to the account record can be viewed in the `updateHistory` array

An investment account holds cash and assets that your client can buy and sell. In Seccl's system, these operate as sub-pots. This means you can have multiple investment strategies within a single wrapper. For example: - ISA account 1 – cautious model - ISA account 2 – adventurous model Seccl offers the following tax wrappers: - General Investment Account (GIA) available to individuals, corporations and trusts - Individual Savings Account (ISA) - Junior Individual Savings Account (JISA) - Self Invested Personal Pension (SIPP) - Third-party products such as SSAS, SIPP, and Offshore Bonds This sections shows you how to open an investment account for the specified wrapper, as well as some of the additional flows required when operating a GIA, ISA, JISA, and pension. --- #### Account statuses Accounts also have statuses similar to the client record. This means that an active client can continue trading in any active accounts, whilst opening another account in a status of pending. Each wrapper type has different requirements linked to their regulations, once a 'type' of wrapper is active the client can go on to open additional active accounts within that wrapper type. This is managed in the client product object. | **Status** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | Pending | The client has not yet accepted the wrapper specific declaration and/or the client record is not active.
Account actions blocked | | Active | Client has accepted the wrapper specific declaration and the client record is active.
Account actions available | | Suspended | Account closed or voided. Transaction instructions blocked. | --- #### The client product This represents the wrapper information of your client. A client product is automatically created when an investment account within one wrapper type is created for the first time. There is a single client product per wrapper type per client record. The client product record stores information related to the product including remaining allowances (such as ISA subscription or Lump Sum Allowance (LSA), date product terms accepted, details on the client's beneficiaries. --- #### Endpoints ``` /account /clientProduct /schemeProduct ``` ---

item.description:
The `portfolioTransaction` object is used to capture transactions including single or regular payments in, withdrawals, orders and sells on an account.

Transactions are grouped to perform two actions at once. For example, if a client pays into their account and invests in a fund, this is considered two transactions and returns a singular `linkId.`

## **Creating transactions**

The portfolioTransactionGroup endpoint creates a group of `portfolioTransactions` united by a single `linkId`

### Validation

When using the `/portfoliotransactiongroup` endpoint to submit transaction groups, there are two types of validation error responses you can expect to observe, these are split between:

1. API response errors
    
    1. These are responses directly from the API after you send a request
        
2. Exception notifications
    
    1. Asynchronous handling of errors that cannot be handled by the API response
        

#### API response errors

These occur when the API can immediately validate the request. You can expect to find errors related to:

- The request format is not valid
    
- Cannot find the given accountId
    
- There is insufficient cash and/or stock for the instructed transactions
    

#### Exception notifications

These occur when the system needs to validate the transactions asynchronously, such as when submitting a group of transactions. This applies whether submitting one or many transactions in a group - the validation of each transaction is processed asynchronously.

You can find further information on viewing and managing exceptions in the **Platform Management / Notifications** section.

You can expect to find exceptions related to:

- Transaction types not recognised
    
- There is insufficient cash when the withdrawal is triggered after some other transactions completing (e.g. linked sell orders)
    

## **Retrieving transactions**

The portfolioTransaction endpoint is where you can retrieve individual transactions using the `transactionId` – this could relate to a payment, order, stock transfer, dividend payment, etc.

### **Understanding transaction statuses**

The portfolioTransactionGroup creates a group of portfolioTransactions with a status of `Pending` or `Waiting`. For example, a pay-in and invest group:

\* Payment is created with a status of `Pending`  
\* Linked orders have a status of `Waiting`  
\* When the payment completes, the status moves from `Pending` to `Completed`  
\* This triggers the the linked orders to switch status from `Pending` to `Completed` – and the orders are routed to market

This indicates the percentage of cash to invest. The scope of the cash depends on if the transaction shares a group with another transaction that has the `includeCash` attribute.

If `includeCash` is in the same group (identified by a `linkId` attribute), then the `percentage` refers to all the available cash on the account, at the time the transaction with the `percentage` attribute moves from `status: Waiting -> Pending`. If there is no `includeCash` in the group, the `percentage` refers to only the cash raised by other transactions in the same group.

When the transaction moves from `status: Waiting -> Pending`, the percentage is calculated in to a monetary amount, and an `amount` attribute will be added to the transaction. This is the actual amount that will be sent in the market instruction.

request.description:
This endpoint lets you query a wide range of fields to retrieve portfolio transaction objects.

---

**Get a single transaction**

If you just want a single transaction object, and you know the `id`, you can use this endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/{{transactionId}}`

---

**Use parameters to get many transactions**

If you don't know the `id`, or you want to get many transactions, you can use query parameters on this endpoint to narrow down your search.

When querying for pending orders using the `linkId` query param, providing the `eventId` or the `linkId` as a value in the param will retrieve pending order transactions.

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?{{queryParamName}}={{queryParamValue}}`

You can most of the transaction object attributes, separated by "&" if using multiple parameters, as parameters in the endpoint call.

For example, if I wanted to see all Payment Deposit transactions on a client's account, I could use the following endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?accountId=00BXGDHX&transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit`

Or, if I want to get all Pending Payment Deposit expectations:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit&status=Pending`

request.description:
This mocks a completed order.

In this scenario, we want to invest £1000, and we know the price of the asset is 228.7697, so the quantity we will receive is:

quantity = ROUND( amountToInvest / assetPrice, minimumDecimalPlaces)

In our example:

- amountToInvest = 1000
    
- assetPrice = 228.7697
    
- minimumDecimalPlaces = 4 (because the minimumTransferUnit is 0.0001, which is to 4 decimal places)
    

quantity = ROUND( 1000 / 228.7697, 4) = 4.3712

We have entered the relevant values in the request for you, assuming you are following the tutorial.

item.description:
This folder gives you the example API calls you need to set an account up to eventually place sells on the account, including:

1. Authenticating in to the Pfolio API
    
2. Adding the valid Raise Trade asset
    
3. Creating the client that we will be using to do the investing and trading
    
4. Creating an account for that client
    
5. Depositing some cash
    
6. Investing in an asset
    

These API calls are not explicitly related to Raise Trades, but they give you the pre-requisites need to do a Raise Trade.

Once you have completed the setup, you can move on to the Use Case examples.

## Environment variables

To successfully follow this tutorial, you will need to set these environment variables in Postman:

### Firm and client

- `firmId` = your staging firmId
    
- `firmNodeId` = your staging nodeId (which node your account sits on)
    
- `clientEmail` = an email that belongs to your test client, we recommend using an email that you have access to, so you can receive the account setup emails. You can use a trick to create unique email addresses without actually creating them - for example if you have [myEmail@myDomain.com](https://mailto:myEmail@myDomain.com), you can then use [myEmail+uniqueAddress@myDomain.com](https://mailto:myEmail+uniqueAddress@myDomain.com), and you will still receive emails to your original inbox
    
- `clientNiNumber` = a globally unique national insurance number for this client
    

### **Assets**

We have specifically chosen and verified that the below asset IDs are valid for use in this tutorial:

- `rtAssetId` = 29F55
    
- `rtAssetId2` = 27G1M
    
- `equityAssetId` = 286D7

request.description:
This is an API call to sell some assets in an account. Use this if you want to raise cash from, or reduce exposure to, specific assets your client holds.

Currently, you can only instruct sells as a quantity of units or shares. Please refer to the /assets endpoint to check an asset's `minimumTransferUnit` before submitting a trade, to know how many decimal places you can submit in the `transactions.quantity` field.

You can instruct many sells in the same group, each for different assets, so long as they are all on the same `accountId`.

#### **Parameters**

`firmId` string **Required**  
Unique identifier for the firm

---

`accountId` string **Required**  
Unique identifier for the client’s account

---

`transactions` object **Required**  
Universal object used for buys, sells, transfers and withdrawals

---

`transactions.firmId` string **Required**

Unique identifier for the firm

---

`transactions.accountId` string **Required**  
Unique identifier for the client’s account

---

`transactions.transactionType` string **Required**  
The type of transaction taking place

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| Order |

---

`transactions.transactionSubType` string **Required**  
The action performed on the account

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| At best |

---

`transactions.movementType` string **Required**  
Whether cash or assets are travelling in or out of an account.

| **Enum values** |
| --- |
| Sell |

---

`transactions.currency` string **Required**  
Three-letter ISO code for the currency paid in or out of the account

---

`transactions.assetId` string **Required**  
Unique identifier for a type of asset

---

`transactions.quantity` decimal string **Required**  
The share quantity of the asset sold down

---

#### **Returns**

Returns an order expectation

---

`data.id` string  
Successful response, the `id` relates to the `linkId` you will find on any transactions created within that group. You can retrieve transactions using GET `/portfoliotransactions/?linkId={{linkId}}`

---

**Failed requests**

Please see the **The orders portfolioTransactionGroups** folder for information on how we validate and surface errors.

item.name: Raise Trades (sell by amount)
Observe the available cash and stock on the account before the Raise Trade

request.description:
This command returns the Live Account Summary (LAS) object for the specified account. The LAS represents the account's available cash and stock balances, which are the completed balances less any in-flight transactions that are being ring-fenced.

Use this endpoint to know how much available cash and stock you have, when calculating new transactions prior to requesting them.

You can see how much available stock value you have for each asset. If you have followed this tutorial closely, you will see a `currentValue` of £1000 for assetId 29F55, with a current sell price of 228.7697, and a minimum transfer unit of 0.0001.

This means the following constraints apply when creating a Raise Trade:

- Minimum raise amount = 0.02
    
- Maximum raise amount = 800
    

#### Attributes

---

`id`

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`firmId`

The unique identifier of the firm

---

`nodeId` string

The unique node identifier that the client record is attached to

---

`name`

The full name of the client, including title, first name and surname

---

`currency`

The three-letter ISO currency code of the account. Currently only GBP is supported

---

`accountType`

The type of account

---

`wrapperType` enum value

The wrapper type of the investment account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `ISA` | Individual Savings Account |
| `JISA` | Junior Individual Savings Account |
| `GIA` | General Investment Account |
| `PENSION` | Pension |
| `TPPENSION` | Third-party pension |

---

`wrapperDetail`

Contains details of the investment account

---

`recurringPayment` boolean

States whether or not there is a recurring payment on the account

---

`recurringOrders` array

Contains details of any recurring order allocation on the account

---

`status` enum value

The status of the account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has accepted the product terms and declarations |
| `Pending` | The client hasn't accepted the product terms and declarations |

---

`clientId`

The unique identifier of the client account

---

`positions` array

Contains a summary of the individual cash and asset positions within the portfolio

---

`positions.id` string

The unique identifier of the position.  
For cash positions consisting of `accountId`|`C`|`position currency`  
For stock positions consisting of `accountId`|`S`|`isin`

---

`positions.postitionType` enum value

The type of position that the values within the array are referring to

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Stock` | Asset holdings |
| `Cash` | Cash holdings |

---

`positions.isin` string

The ISIN of the asset

---

`positions.assetId` string

The unique identifier of the of asset

---

`positions.instrumentType` enum

The type of instrument this position represents

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Equity` | An equity |
| `ETF` | An ETF |
| `Investment Trust` | An investment trust |
| `Fund` | A fund |

---

---

`positions.assetName` string

The name of the asset

---

`positions.accountId` string

The ID of the account for this position

---

`positions.amount` float

For cash positions, the amount of available cash in the account. This will exclude ring fenced cash that is being used for other transactions.

---

`positions.quantity` float

The current number of available units in the holding, after any units have been removed for ring-fencing. For previously held assets, they will be included in the response with a zero amount of units

---

`positions.currentValue` float

The value of the available position as at the last known price for this asset.

---

`positions.currency` enum value

The three-letter ISO currency code of the position

---

`positions.prices` array

An array of the prices used to calculate the value of the position. See 'Prices' in the platform management section for more detail on the prices object.

---

`positions.currentPrice` float

The current price of the asset – this is the `ask` of the latest price in the system

---

`positions.currentSellPrice` float

The current sell price of the asset.

---

`positions.currentPriceDate` string

The date of the current price in the system. This is the date of the price being used and may be prior to the current date or toDate used (for example when the toDate is a non-trading day)

---

`positions.updateId` string

The unique identifier assigned to the position when it was last updated

---

`positions.minimumTransferUnit` float

The number of decimal places the assets can be held

---

`positions.auditDetails` nested object

Details of when the position was last updated

---

`currentValue` float

The current available value of the account.

---

`uninvestedCash` float

The amount of available uninvested cash in the account. This will exclude ring fenced cash that is being used for other transactions.

---

request.description:
Raise Trades are instructions to sell a monetary amount from a given asset.

Immediately below are some cases that will cause an API error. Below that are the required attributes to make a successful API call.

Any of the following will return an API error (see examples for error responses):

1. If no `amount` is included on the request (you must provide an amount to raise)
    
2. If `amount: 0` is on the request (amount must be greater than 0)
    
3. If `amount` is less than the minimum raise amount for this asset (see below for more details
    
4. If `amount` is more than the maximum raise amount for this asset on this account (see below for more details)
    
5. If `quantity` or `percentage` is included on the request
    
6. If the `assetId` is of `instrumentType` `Equity`, `Investment Trust` or `ETF`
    
    1. Except, if your firm has fractional trading enabled, and you do not charge dealing fees for ETF assets, then you can instruct a Raise Trade on `ETF` assets
        

## Error message examples not included here

If your firm:

1. Does not fractionally trade, or
    
2. Charges dealing fees on asset
    

Then you will receive an API erorr if trying to raise on Equity, Investment Trust and ETF assets (fractional trading validation), or if you charge fees on the asset in the request (any `instrumentType`).

To provide real examples in this documentation would require you to create:

1. A new firm without fractional trading enabled (if you currently have it enabled)
    
2. A new node which charges dealing fees on the asset in the request
    

In lieu of that, we will provide the API responses you can expect in those scenarios.

### Instruct a Raise Trade when your firm does not fractionally trade

``` json
{
    "error": {
        "type": "DataValidationError",
        "errorMessage": "The request has failed validation",
        "statusCode": 400,
        "fieldErrors": [
            {
                "fieldName": "movementType",
                "errorMessage": "Raise requires Firm to support fractional trading",
                "type": "usage"
            }
        ]
    }
}

 ```

### Instruct a Raise Trade when your firm charges dealing fees on the asset requested

``` json
{
    "error": {
        "type": "DataValidationError",
        "errorMessage": "The request has failed validation",
        "statusCode": 400,
        "fieldErrors": [
            {
                "fieldName": "movementType",
                "errorMessage": "Raise is not supported with node dealing charges for instrument type of ETF",
                "type": "usage"
            }
        ]
    }
}

 ```

## Minimum raise amount for this asset

### Reason for the validation

The reason for this minimum amount validation, is to prevent you instructing a trade that is not likely to be executed in the market.

The reason for adding the 10% buffer (the x1.1), is because the prices that we provide are the previous day's closing price. Therefore the price is likely to change between you instructing the trade, and when the trade is executed. So, we factor in a 10% price rise, to give a higher likelihood that your trade will succeed.

### Calculation of minimum raise amount

The minimum Raise Trade amount is calculated as:

`minAmount = ROUNDDOWN( assetPrice x (minimumTransferUnit x 1.1), 2)`

#### Examples

For example:

- assetPrice = 100
    
- minimumTransferUnit = 0.01
    

`minAmount = ROUNDDOWN( 100 x (0.01 x 1.1) , 2) = 1.1`

#### Example for this tutorial

Worked example for the asset we are using:

- assetPrice = 228.7697
    
- minimumTransferUnit = 0.0001
    

`minAmount = ROUNDUP( 228.7697 x ( 0.0001 x 1.1) , 2) = 0.02`

If you are still using the asset suggested in this tutorial, then the minimum raise amount is £0.03.

Therefore, if we try to instruct a Raise Trade for less than this, we will get an API error.

## Maximum raise amount for this asset on this account

### Reason for the validation

The reason for this maximum amount validation, is to prevent you instructing a trade that is at risk of selling more quantity than your client account holds.

The validation is based on 80%\* of the account's current available stock value.

\* 80% is the current maximum percentage of a single asset holding's value that Seccl will allow you Raise Trade. This number is subject to change, based on Seccl's risk-based view of market volatility. We will communicate any change to this number.

### Calculation of maximum raise amount

The maximum Raise Trade amount is calculated as:

`maxAmount = ROUNDDOWN( (availableStockQuantity x maxPercentForRaiseTrade) x latestBidPrice, 2)`

#### How we validate this

When a Raise Trade order request is received, we will estimate the quantity that is required to raise the amount. We include a -20% buffer on the last known price of the asset (directly related to 1 - `maxPercentForRaiseTrade`, e.g. 1 - 0.8 = 0.2). Then, we check if the estimated quantity is > the available stock on the account, and if it is then we return an error.

#### Examples

For example:

- `availableStockQuantity` = 100
    
- `maxPercentForRaiseTrade` = 0.8
    
- `latestBidPrice` = 1
    

`maxAmount = ROUNDDOWN( (100 x 0.8) x 1, 2) = 80`

#### Example for this tutorial

Worked example for the asset we are using:

- `availableStockQuantity` = 4.3712 (as identified in the Live Account Summary call in this folder)
    
- `maxPercentForRaiseTrade` = 0.8
    
- `latestBidPrice` = 228.7697
    

`maxAmount = ROUNDDOWN( (4.3712 x 0.8) x 228.7697, 2) = 799.99`

If you have not yet placed a new trade on this asset in the tutorial, then your maximum raise trade amount will be £799.99.

Therefore, if we try to instruct a Raise Trade for more than this, we will get an API error.

# Parameters

---

`firmId` string **Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`transactionType` string **Required**

Must be `Order`

---

`transactionSubType` string **Required**

Must be `At Best`

---

`movementType` string **Required**

Must be `Raise` for Raise Trades

---

`accountId` string **Required**

The unique identifier for the account

---

`currency` string **Required**

Must be `GBP`

---

`assetId` string **Required**

The unique identifier for the asset you want to trade

---

`amount` int or float **Required**

The GBP value you want to raise from selling the asset holding.

Must be:

- Greater than 0.01
    
- Greater than or equal to the minimum raise amount
    
- Less than or equal to the maximum raise amount
    
- No greater than 2 decimal places

request.description:
This endpoint lets you query a wide range of fields to retrieve portfolio transaction objects.

---

**Get a single transaction**

If you just want a single transaction object, and you know the `id`, you can use this endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/{{transactionId}}`

---

**Use parameters to get many transactions**

If you don't know the `id`, or you want to get many transactions, you can use query parameters on this endpoint to narrow down your search.

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?{{queryParamName}}={{queryParamValue}}`

You can most of the transaction object attributes, separated by "&" if using multiple parameters, as parameters in the endpoint call.

For example, if I wanted to see all Payment Deposit transactions on a client's account, I could use the following endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?accountId=00BXGDHX&transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit`

Or, if I want to get all Pending Payment Deposit expectations:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit&status=Pending`

In this scenario, we have sold £500, and we know the price of the asset is 228.7697, so the quantity we must sell to raise £500 is:

quantity = ROUNDUP( amountToRaise / assetPrice, minimumDecimalPlaces)

request.description:
This command returns the Live Account Summary (LAS) object for the specified account. The LAS represents the account's available cash and stock balances, which are the completed balances less any in-flight transactions that are being ring-fenced.

If you have followed this tutorial closely, you will now be able to see that the stock quantity and value of the raise trade asset has been reduced, since you have sold £500 worth of stock. In turn, you can see the available cash has been increased by £500.

---

`firmId`

The unique identifier of the firm

---

`nodeId` string

The unique node identifier that the client record is attached to

---

---

`currency`

The three-letter ISO currency code of the account. Currently only GBP is supported

---

`accountType`

The type of account

---

`wrapperType` enum value

| --- | --- |
| `ISA` | Individual Savings Account |
| `JISA` | Junior Individual Savings Account |

| `PENSION` | Pension |

---

---

`positions.instrumentType` enum

The current number of available units in the holding, after any units have been removed for ring-fencing. For previously held assets, they will be included in the response with a zero amount of units

The current sell price of the asset.

---

`positions.currentPriceDate` string

item.description:
The first use case made available is to create a singular Raise Trade. This will not be linked to any other transactions, but will introduce the concept of the Raise Trade, how it is instructed, how it looks as a transaction in different states, and what happens to the cash and stock on the client account once completed.

The set of instructions in this folder will take you on the end to end journey of:

1. Observing the available cash and stock balances on the account before you make the trade
    
2. Describe what API errors you might find
    
3. Create a valid Raise Trade instruction
    
4. Observing what the transaction looks like when it is at Pending status
    
5. Completing the order (emulating the production environment)
    
6. Observing what the transaction looks like when it is at Completed status
    
7. Observing the cash and stock movements that happen on the account as a result of the trade
    
8. Observing the available cash and stock balances on the account as a result of the trade
    

## Valid asset types

- Fund
    
- ETF, only if:
    
    - Your firm has fractional trading enabled, and
        
    - You do not charge dealing fees on ETF orders
        

## Invalid asset types

- ETF, only if:
    
    - Your firm does not have fractional trading enabled, or
        
    - You charge dealing fees on ETF orders
        
- Equity
    
- Investment Trust
    
- Bond

item.description:
A Portfolio Transaction Group (PTG) is an instruction to perform a set of `transactions` . The transactions are linked together (by a `linkId` ) and progress as a chain of events. Most often, Sell-like transactions (such as Raise) progress first, and other linked transactions wait for the sells to `Complete` before moving on to their next state.

In contrast to the Single Raise Trade instruction, PTGs are instructed as an array of transactions to the `/portfolioTransactionGroup` endpoint. This returns a `linkId` in the `data.id` attribute after a valid instruction is accepted.

item.name: Sell and Withdraw (Raise Trade)

request.description:
You can define your own sell amounts and withdraw the proceeds. By leaving the Withdrawal amount blank, you can withdraw the full proceeds of the linked Raise orders.

Returns a `linkId` in the `data.id` attribute.

**Parameters**

---

`firmId` string **Required**  
Unique identifier for the firm

---

`accountId` string **Required**  
Unique identifier for the client’s account

---

`transactions` array **Required**  
Universal array used for buys, sells, transfers and withdrawals

---

`transactions.firmId` string **Required**  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`transactions.transactionType` string **Required**

- `Order` for Raise Trade
    
- `Payment` for Withdrawal
    

---

`transactions.transactionSubType` string **Required**

Must be `At Best` for Raise Trades

- `At Best` for Raise Trade
    
- `Withdrawal` for Withdrawal
    

---

`transactions.movementType` string **Required**

- `Raise` for Raise Trade
    
- `Out` for Withdrawal
    

---

`transactions.accountId` string **Required**

The unique identifier for the account

---

`transactions.currency` string **Required**

Must be `GBP`

---

`transactions.assetId` string **Required**

- The unique identifier for the asset you want to trade
    
- Not required for the Withdrawal
    

---

`transactions.amount` int or float **Required**

**For Raise** **`movementType`**

The GBP value you want to raise from selling the asset holding.

item.name: Auto-disinvest with Raise Trades
Create a withdrawal with auto-disinvest using Raise Trades

request.description:
This command creates a single withdrawal with auto-disinvest and specifically using Raise Trades (sell by amount). To specify that you want to use Raise Trades in the disinvestment, you must use `autoDisinvestmentMethod: "Amount"` If `autoDisinvestmentMethod` is not specified, or if "Quantity" is passed in to it, then quantity-based sells will be generated. A successful request returns a `linkId` as the `data.id`. #### Parameters --- `firmId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the firm --- `accountId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the client’s investment account --- `transactions` object **Required** --- `transactions.firmId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the firm --- `transactions.accountId` string **Required** The unique identifier for the client's investment account --- `transactions.transactionType` string **Required** The type of transaction taking place – this will be set to `Payment` --- `transactions.transactionSubType` string **Required** The action to be performed on the account – this will be set to `Withdrawal` --- `transactions.method` string **Required** The payment method facilitating the withdrawal – this will be set to `BACS Credit` --- `transactions.movementType` string **Required** Whether the cash is travelling in or out of the investment account – this will be set to `Out` --- `transactions.amount` float **Required** The amount that the investor is contributing to their investment account --- `transactions.currency` string **Required** Three-letter ISO code for the currency paid in or out of the account – this should be set to `GBP` --- `transactions.autoDisinvest` string **Required** The type of auto-disinvestment | **Enum value** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | `Largest` | Instructs a sell-down from the largest holding in the investment account | | `Proportional` | Instructs a sell-down proportionally across the investment account | | `Full` | (Not available if `autoDisinvestmentMethod = "Amount"`)

Instructs a full sell-down with all the available stock in the investment account, and withdrawal the proceeds | --- `transactions.autoDisinvestSellType` string **Optional** The sell method to be used for the auto-disinvestment | **Enum value** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | `Amount` | Uses Raise Trade sells (sell by amount) | | `Quantity` | Uses Quantity sells | | `null` | If not defined, default is `Quantity` |

item.description:
Auto-disinvest is an instruction to let the Pfolio API decide which assets to sell down, to achieve your intended outcome. It removes the responsibility on the firm or user to calculate and decide which asset to sell. We provide 3 disinvestment methods:

- `Largest` (start with the largest eligible asset by value)
    
- `Proportional` (spread the sells across eligible assets given their weighted proportion)
    
- `Full` (sell down all holdings)
    

Raise Trades is currently available with only the `Largest` and `Proportional` methods.

The API will respond with a `linkId` which can be used to retrieve all the transactions created to satisfy the request, which will be the original transaction (withdrawal, fee etc.) and one or many sells.

## How `autoDisinvest: Largest` works with Raise Trades

Auto-disinvest is an attribute attached to a non-order transaction, such as a Withdrawal, or a Fee. When Pfolio API receives a request to auto-disinvest with the Largest method, we:

1. Retrieve the holdings and available balances on the account
    
2. Select only the holdings eligible for Raise Trades (reference the main folder documentation to identify which assets are eligible for Raise Trades)
    
3. Identify the smallest raise amount out of all the eligible holdings
    
    1. And validate that the amount to raise is not smaller than this
        
4. Sum the value of the eligible holdings (subject to the maximum percentage available to raise per holding)
    
    1. And validate that the amount to raise is not greater than this
        
5. Sort the eligible holdings by value (largest to smallest)
    
6. Then starting from the largest asset:
    
    1. Calculate the Raise Trades required to get at least the requested amount as the minimum of: _Requested amount_ or _Value of holding eligible for raise trade_
        
        1. If the calculated raise trade is less than that asset's minimum sell value, it is rounded up to the minimum
            
    2. Repeat until the requested amount can be satisfied by the calculated sells
        

If you are requesting an amount that can be satisfied from just the largest asset, there will only be one sell. If however the requested amount cannot be satisfied from one asset, there will be multiple sells.

## How `autoDisinvest: Proportional` works with Raise Trades

Auto-disinvest is an attribute attached to a non-order transaction, such as a Withdrawal, or a Fee. When Pfolio API receives a request to auto-disinvest with the Proportional method, we:

1. Retrieve the holdings and available balances on the account
    
2. Select only the holdings eligible for Raise Trades (reference the main folder documentation to identify which assets are eligible for Raise Trades)
    
3. Identify the smallest raise amount out of all the eligible holdings
    
    1. And validate that the amount to raise is not smaller than this
        
4. Sum the value of the eligible holdings (subject to the maximum percentage available to raise per holding)
    
    1. And validate that the amount to raise is not greater than this
        
5. Calculate the proportion of the overall raise amount to allocate to each eligible holding
    
    1. This takes into account the maximum percentage available to raise for each holding
        
6. Then applying this proportion to each position:
    
    1. Calculate the Raise Trades required to get _**at least**_ the requested amount by multiplying the _Disinvest proportion_ by the _Value of holding eligible for raise trade_
        
        1. The result is **rounded up** to 2 decimal places. This ensures that calculated trades will always raise _**at least**_ the required amount.
            
    2. We then validate that each Raise Trade is above the minimum amount for the relevant asset
        
    3. If any assets are found to be ineligible, they are removed, and we repeat this process from Step 5.
        
7. The resulting set of orders will respect the account's current value proportions such that each position should have the same overall value weighting before and after the orders are completed.
You can chain transaction events together to automate investor workflows (and reduce time out the market).

This section will show you how to realign an investment account with an attached recurring orders allocation

When a `Portfolio Realign` is instructed, it calculates the relevant buys and sells to bring the investment account holdings in line with the attached recurring orders allocation.

**An example**

Recurring orders allocation:

\*   50% Asset A
\*   30% Asset B
\*   20% Asset C
    

Actual holdings:

\*   60% Asset A
\*   15% Asset B
\*   25% Asset C
    

Portfolio realign would create the following orders:

\*   Sell 10% Asset A
\*   Sell 5% Asset C
\*   Buy 15% Asset B

item.description:
This section will show you how to create recurring orders

Recurring orders can be used for various investment strategies, including:

\* Thematic investing  
\* Investing in a single asset  
\* Advisory models

In these investment strategies, the investor decision maker is the client.

This functionality allows you to attach an asset or a blend of assets to an investment account. Any payments into the investment account can be auto-invested into the recurring order allocation, and holdings in the account can be realigned in line with the asset allocation on an ad-hoc basis.

**Understanding recurring orders**

The recurringOrders allocation is set on the account object. You can include as many assets as you like. The total percentage of assets cannot be more than 1. Any remainder will be allocated to cash. For example:

\* 40% Asset A  
\* 40% Asset B  
\* 20% Cash

**An example flow**

The end-to-end user flow for an investment strategy using recurring orders could work as follows:

\* Create a client  
\* Client selects the desired investment strategy and the wrapper type  
\* Create an investment account and assign the investment strategy  
\* Create a payment with auto-invest

item.description:
As a Discretionary Fund Manager, you may want to manage your client’s investments separately using a bespoke allocation and not using the Model Portfolio Service. This may be because they are a **high-net-worth investor** with specific investment goals and needs.

Using the Seccl API, DFMs have the ability to create a bespoke allocation whilst reporting as the decision maker on behalf of the client. An `LEI number` assigned to the DFM will be reported to the regulators every time a trade is created on the client’s account.

To create a DFM user, you will need to provide the following:

- A decision maker with discretionary permissions
    
- A Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) number for the firm
    

Accounts managed by DFM users have been mandated by the client to make investment decisions on their behalf. Therefore all orders placed on the account will have the `investmentDecision` attached.

You can create a DFM user by using the request named `Create a DFM platform user` in these API docs.

item.name: Rebalance a discretionary model

request.description:
Rebalances the model. This is a bulk action which rebalances all accounts using the model. This feature is only available for discretionary models.

Returns an 'eventId'.

**Validation**  
When using the `/event` endpoint to initiate a model-level rebalance, the system does not validate the request at the time of submission. Instead, a bulk action is created, and validation occurs when attempting to generate a rebalance for each individual account associated with the model.

If an account already has a rebalance in progress, a firm-level notification is generated which will contain the below `message` and details of any accounts which have failed validation in the `fieldErrors` array.

`message` - string - Cannot create a new rebalance event whilst an account is processing an incomplete rebalance

You can find further information on viewing and managing exceptions in the **Platform Management / Notifications** section.

Rebalances are still created for valid accounts that do not currently have a rebalance in progress.

This functionality is strictly for Discretionary Fund Managers (DFMs). This is because our Model Portfolio Service requires a registered Decision Maker with the necessary FCA-approved permissions to create and manage investments on behalf of the client.

When trading Exchange-Traded instruments (ETIs), DFMs are required to declare both the client and DFM's nationality, domicile and also confirm the relevant national identifiers including the firm Legal Entity Identifier (LEI).

This section will cover how to:

*   Create and update a model
*   Retrieve models
*   Invest in a model
*   Rebalance a model
    

If you do not have discretionary permissions but would like the ability to rebalance your client's portfolio, please see **Realign your client's portfolio** under **Recurring orders.**

Note that, for advisory models, rebalancing can only be done at the account/portfolio level. Bulk rebalancing (i.e. rebalance all accounts attached to the model at the same time) is not possible.

This functionality enables a firm without discretionary permissions to create and manage model portfolios for their clients.

Discretionary Fund Managers (DFMs) should refer to **Discretionary model portfolios** as this requires additional decision maker information.

Please note the following limitations with advisory models:

1. **Assets cannot be changed** after a model has been created (a new version must be created with the new asset(s) and clients switched to the new model as required)
2. **Bulk rebalancing is not possible** with advisory models. Rebalancing can only be done on individual accounts where `accountId` is specified in the Rebalance `event`.
    

This section will cover how to:

- Create a model
- Retrieve models
- Invest in a model
- Rebalance a portfolio

item.description: This section will show you how to retrieve your firm's models. This action is useful for seeing an overview of all models available and making any updates to the models.

This section will help you create a model portfolio service for clients who would benefit from active management but who do not require a full bespoke service. These can be targeted at different investment objectives such as growth, balanced, or income.

As the investment firm, you may construct and  
manage these portfolios itself or outsource the investment activity to a 3rd party discretionary manager.

These solutions fall within the following types of structure:

• **Discretionary** – the client gives discretion for a firm to manage a portfolio on their behalf on a  
professional basis. Clients may wish to use this type of service if they are too busy or not experienced enough to look after their own investments and prefer to use the investment experience of a firm providing these services.

• **Advisory** (non-discretionary) – clients rely on the firm for professional and independent advice on investment  
decisions, but the client takes the final decision to deal.

We currently do not offer an execution-only solution.

item.description:
Investment strategies determine how assets are allocated in a client's portfolio. This usually takes into consideration:

*   The client's net-worth
*   The length of their investment
*   The specific investment goals e.g purchasing a home
*   Their attitude to risk
*   The nature of your business and FCA permissions you have (DFM/Adviser/D2C)
    

All investment strategies are stored as transactions in the API. These transactions are presented as single orders, recurring orders and models in the code.

**A note on regulation**

Seccl carries out daily transaction reporting to the FCA that records the details of the investor decision maker that submitted the order in any exchange traded assets. The investor decision maker is determined by the specific investment strategy.

For example, where a client is investing in discretionary managed model portfolios, the investor decision maker is the Discretionary Fund Manager (DFM). As such, we need to report the details of the DFM, and not the investor.

The able below outlines the possible investment strategies and what functionality you should use.

| **Investment strategy** | **Seccl functionality** |
| --- | --- |
| Discretionary managed model portfolios | Discretionary model portfolios |
| Bespoke discretionary managed model portfolios | Discretionary model portfolios |
| Advisory models | Advisory model portfolios |
| Individual orders | Single orders |
| Thematic investing | Recurring orders |
| Investing in a single asset | Recurring orders |

**This section shows you how to:**

*   Attach, create and update an investment strategy
*   Pay in and auto-invest
*   Retrieve pending and completed orders

item.description:
The `Payment` `portfoliotransaction` object describes payment transactions.

We sometimes call Payment transactions "expectations", because we expect them to happen once the instruction is created through the API. For example, a Payment expectation is created, once we receive the cash, we can allocate the actual money to the expectation.

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

---

`firmId` string  
The unique identifier for the firm

---

`accountId` string  
The unique identifier for the client’s investment account

---

`transactionType` enum value  
The type of transaction taking place. This will be set to `Payment`

---

`transactionSubType` enum value  
The sub-type of the transaction taking place. These can be one of:

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Deposit` | Payment expectation |
| `Employer` | Employer payment expectation (for pension contributions only) |
| `Employee` | Employee payment expectation (for pension contributions only) |

---

`movementType` string  
Whether the cash is travelling in or out of the investment account. This should be set to `In`

---

`currency` string  
Three-letter ISO code for the currency paid in or out of the account. This should be set to `GBP`

---

`amount` float  
The amount that the investor is contributing to their investment account

---

`method` enum value  
The payment method facilitating the amount paid in.

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Bank Transfer` | Payment expectation |
| `Seccl GoCardless` | Payment is collected via GoCardless direct debit |
| `Bulk Bank Transfer` | Child expectation for bulk payment |

---

`transactionDate` string

The date the payment transaction was instructed

---

`status` string

The status of the transaction

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Completed` | Money received and allocated to a client account |
| `Pending` | Expectation created and awaiting receipt of money |
| `Deleted` | Expectation deleted, this cannot be allocated |

---

`accountName` string

The name of the investment account

---

`accountType`

The type of account

---

`statusChange` array

Contains a list of changes to the transaction's `status` field

---

`linkId` string

The unique identifier of the portfolio transaction group

---

`nodeId` string

The unique identifier of the node attached to the client account

---

`createdDate` string

The date the transaction was created

---

`completedDate` string

The date the transaction switched to `Completed`

---

`updateId` string

A unique identifier of this transactions' current state. You will need this if you want to update a transaction later.

item.name: Bank transfer

request.description:
This endpoint lets you query a wide range of fields to retrieve portfolio transaction objects.

---

**Get a single transaction**

If you just want a single transaction object, and you know the `id`, you can use this endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/{{transactionId}}`

---

**Use parameters to get many transactions**

If you don't know the `id`, or you want to get many transactions, you can use query parameters on this endpoint to narrow down your search.

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?{{queryParamName}}={{queryParamValue}}`

You can most of the transaction object attributes, separated by "&" if using multiple parameters, as parameters in the endpoint call.

For example, if I wanted to see all Payment Deposit transactions on a client's account, I could use the following endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?accountId=00BXGDHX&transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit`

Or, if I want to get all Pending Payment Deposit expectations:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit&status=Pending`

This flow creates a bank transfer expectation. It can also be used to auto-allocate payments via open banking.

The response returns a `linkId` which can be queried to retrieve all `portfoliotransaction` 's in the group.

#### Parameters

---

`firmId` string **Required**

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`accountId` string **Required**

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`transactions` object **Required**

Contains details of the transactions within the portfolio transaction group

---

`transactions.firmId` string **Required**

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`transactions.accountId` string **Required**

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`transactions.transactionType` enum value **Required**

This should be set to `Payment`

---

`transactions.transactionSubType` enum value **Required**

This will be `Deposit`, or if the contribution is to a pension wrapper, it will be `Employer` or `Employee`

---

`transactions.method` enum value **Required**

The way the payment will be collected – this should be set to `Bank Transfer`

---

`transactions.movementType` enum value **Required**

This indicates the movement of the cash or assets – this should be set to `In`

---

`transactions.currency` enum value **Required**

The three letter ISO currency code - this should be set to `GBP`

---

`transactions.autoInvest` boolean

This indicates whether the money should be auto-invested into the `recurringOrders` or model attached to the account

---

item.name: Create account with a recurring payment

request.description:
You can also set up recurring monthly expectations to generate on client accounts. Just like with one-time expectations, the `Method` still determines how the cash gets to Seccl, but a new expectation will exist to match with the receipt. You can set this up at the same time as creating the client account (this flow) or you can always add it to the account another time (the next flow).

This flow allows you to create an investment account with a recurring payment built in. The investor will need to set up a standing order for the relevant payment date and include the correct payment reference.

When you create a recurring payment on an investment account, the payment expectation is generated at 8 am in the morning with a status of `Pending`. The `Pending` expectation remains until the money is allocated or it is manually deleted by Seccl on request.

A single investment account can have multiple recurring payments within the `recurringPayment` array.

This returns the unique identifier of the created investment account.

item.description:
To allow an investor to use bank transfer as their payment method, you need to create a `portfoliotransaction` object.

We have the functionality to instantly allocate payments to the investment account. Seccl matches money received via bank transfer dependent on three factors:

1. A corresponding payment expectation that matches the amount received
2. The payment reference in the form of `{{firmId}}-{{accountId}}`
3. Bank details on the transaction that match those held on the client record
    

Where an exception occurs due to one or more of the above being incorrect, the payment falls to unidentified receipts, and manual input is required from your operations team.

**Please note: payment transactions do not settle in the staging environment. To simulate real life events, you need manually settle the payment expectation using the** **`PUT`** **request here described in this section "Staging mock - complete a payment".**

We will start with showing you how to retrieve existing transaction objects, before moving on to show you how to create new ones.

item.description: Here, we will show you how to instruct a recurring direct debit from your client's bank account.

A [direct debit](https://desktop.postman.com/?desktopVersion=9.27.0&userId=10007743&teamId=604381) is an automated payment method that allows merchants to collect payments directly from a customer's bank account. To facilitate direct debits on your platform, you will need to integrate with a third-party direct debit provider.

There are two key parts to facilitating direct debits: setting up mandates with your customers' bank accounts, and collecting payments against your mandates.

A direct debit instruction or direct debit mandate is an authorisation from your customer for you to collect future payments. The details of each authorisation are standardised:

1. All future payments are authorised so you can collect any amount at any time from your customer
2. Your customer must be notified of each payment before it is collected
3. All payments are covered by the Direct Debit Guarantee, which protects customers from payments taken in error
    

You can retrieve direct debit mandate acceptance confirmations and direct debit advance notices from the our API.

To authorise a direct debit mandate, you can follow this flow:

- Investor indicates that they wish to contribute via direct debit
- Investor views and accepts the direct debit mandate shown in your application
- Investor receives a direct debit mandate confirmation document
    

To instruct a direct debit payment, you can follow this flow:

- Investor confirms the amount and the payment date if it's a recurring payment
- Investor receives a direct debit advance notice document
- The payment is automatically collected and allocated to the investor's investment account

item.description:
Bulk payments describe the process of funding many client investment accounts by sending one aggregated payment amount to Seccl. The flow works as follows:

1. The platform creates individual child expectations against each investment account, including a unique `providerRef`
2. A bulk payment is transferred to Seccl's client money bank account
    1. The `providerRef` of the child expectations matches the payment reference of the bulk payment
    2. The sum of the child expectations corresponds to the bulk payment amount
3. Seccl allocates the bulk payment against the child expectations
    

This payment method can be applied to any of the following scenarios:

- Client money: If your firm has client money permissions, you can collect payments directly from end investors and send a single bulk payment to Seccl to allocate
- Third-party payment providers: This could be an e-money wallet provider or a debit card provider. The payment provider collects the money from the end investor and sends a single bulk payment to Seccl to allocate
- Incentive or redress payments: This could apply to an incentive initiative run by the platform, or a goodwill or redress payment funded by the platform. The platform sends a single bulk payment to Seccl to allocate
- Tax rebates from HMRC

request.description:
This endpoint lets you query a wide range of fields to retrieve portfolio transaction objects.

---

**Get a single transaction**

If you just want a single transaction object, and you know the `id`, you can use this endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/{{transactionId}}`

---

**Use parameters to get many transactions**

If you don't know the `id`, or you want to get many transactions, you can use query parameters on this endpoint to narrow down your search.

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?{{queryParamName}}={{queryParamValue}}`

You can most of the transaction object attributes, separated by "&" if using multiple parameters, as parameters in the endpoint call.

For example, if I wanted to see all Payment Deposit transactions on a client's account, I could use the following endpoint:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?accountId=00BXGDHX&transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit`

Or, if I want to get all Pending Payment Deposit expectations:

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/{{firmId}}/?transactionType=Payment&transactionSubType=Deposit&status=Pending`

item.description:
The delete payment deposit expectation API request can be used to delete a payment expectation. It is only possible to delete payment expectations which are at status `Pending` and for the payment methods of `Bank Transfer` and `Truelayer`

The key use cases for this API request are:

- The amount the client wishes to contribute to their account has changed
    
- The client will no longer be proceding with the deposit
    
- A mistake was made when creating the expectation
    
- Cleaner view of transactions on the account by deleting unused expectations
    
- A historic expectation is preventing a client from contributing within their permitted subscription allowance, such as for an ISA or JISA contribution
    

This deletion will also delete any orders linked to the pending payment expectation.

Firms receive feedback about the status of their request either via Transactions Webhook (success on deleting) or via Exceptions Webhook (not successfully deleted).

Payment methods are ways for investors to deposit money to their investment accounts. You can create single and regular payments.

Payment instructions can be created as part of a `portfoliotransactiongroup` with any other `transactionType`, such as a fee or order. It can also include things like `autoInvest` or `investToModel` flags, which invests the money according to the account's asset allocation.

You can process the following payment methods via this API. These might need integrations with third-party payment providers.

- **Bank Transfer:** An end investor sends the money directly to our client money bank account and we allocate to the investment account
- **Bulk Bank Transfer:** A single bulk payment is sent directly to our client money bank account that we allocate to multiple investment accounts
- **Debit card:** A debit card provider collects the money from investors and sends a bulk payment to our client money bank account for us to allocate
- **Open banking:** An automated payment is made to our client money bank account, initiated by the investor via their mobile banking app or online banking portal
- **Direct debit:** An investor instructs their bank to authorise a direct debit provider to collect payments from their account and send a bulk payment to our client money bank account for us to allocate
    

We'll show you how to set up each of these payment methods in this section.

#### **Endpoints**

```
/portfoliotransactiongroup
/portfoliotransaction
/account

```

`accounts.adjustedGrowthPercent` float

The percentage growth achieved only on this platform. (ie. does not consider the provided original book cost of transferred assets)

---

`accounts.transferValue` float

The total transfer value of holdings in the account

---

`accounts.allocation` float

The allocation of the investment account within the whole client portfolio

---

`accounts.openingValue` float

The value of the account at close of business on the fromDate parameter provided. If no fromDate parameter is provided or if the fromDate is before the inception of the account/portfolio, this will show as zero.

---

`bookValue` float

The sum of the `positions.bookValue` in the `positions` array

---

`nonTransferBookValue` float

The sum of the `positions.nonTransferBookValue` in the `positions` array

---

`openingValue` float

The value of the portfolio at close of business on the fromDate parameter provided. If no fromDate parameter is provided or if the fromDate is before the inception of the account/portfolio, this will show as zero.

---

`currentValue` float

The value of the portfolio as at close of business on the toDate parameter provided. If no toDate parameter is provided then today’s date will be used.

---

`uninvestedCash` float

The amount of available uninvested cash across all acounts in this portfolio. This will exclude ring fenced cash that is being used for other transactions.

Important! If a any date parameters is passed, this will no longer accurately represent the amount of available, non-ring-fenced cash.

---

`closingCashValue` float

The amount of cash in the portfolio

---

`growth` float

The growth amount achieved taking into account the provided original book cost of transferred assets

---

`adjustedGrowth` float

The growth amount only achieved on this platform. (ie. does not consider the provided original book cost of transferred assets)

---

`growthPercent` float

The percentage growth taking into account the provided original book cost of transferred assets

---

`adjustedGrowthPercent` float

The percentage growth achieved only on this platform. (ie. does not consider the provided original book cost of transferred assets)

---

`transferValue` float

The sum of the `transferValue` within the `positions` array

---

`products` array

Contains details of tax wrappers held within the client portfolio

---

`products.wrapperType` enum value

The relevant tax wrapper

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| JISA | Junior Individual Savings Account |
| ISA | Individual Savings Account |

---

`products.remainingSubscriptionAmount` float

The remaining subscription amount of the client – this is done at the portfolio level, not the individual sub-account level

---

`realisedProfitLoss` float

The sum of the difference between the value of assets at the time of disposal and their book cost for all disposals in the date range selected

---

`realisedProfitLoss`float

The sum of the difference between the value of assets at the time of disposal and their book cost for all disposals in the date range selected

---

`unrealisedProfitLoss` float

The being the difference between the value of assets that are still held in a portfolio as of the end date of the date range and their book costs.

---

`closingGiaStockValue` float

The value of **GIA** stock holdings in the **portfolio** as at close of business on the toDate parameter provided. If no date parameters are provided, this refers to today's date

`disclaimers` array

`disclaimers.type` string

Type of disclaimer. This constant can be used for mapping purposes

`disclaimers.text` string

Text shown when the disclaimer is present

---

`disclaimers.fields` array

Array containing fields affected by the disclaimer present

`disclaimers.entity` object

object containing details about entity causing the disclaimer

---

`disclaimers.entity.type` string

The type of entity causing the disclaimer. I.e. position, transaction etc

---

`disclaimers.entity.ids` array

Ids of the entities causing the disclaimer

request.description:
This command returns a summary of transactions that have taken place in the client portfolio. This includes:

*   Payments
*   Charges
*   Income (dividends and cash interest)
*   Transfers
*   Internal cash movements
*   Sell and invest orders
    

#### Attributes

* * *

`id` string

The unique identifier of the portfolio

* * *

`name` string

The full name of the client

* * *

`firmId` string

The unique identifier for your firm

* * *

`currency` string

The three-letter ISO currency code

* * *

`payments` array

Contains details of payments in and out of the portfolio

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn` array

Contains details of payments in

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.transactionId` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.transactionCode` string

The transaction code of the transaction

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.narrative` string

The description of the transaction

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.postDate` numerical string

The date the transaction completed

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.valueDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was created

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.amount` numerical string

The value of the transaction

* * *

`payments.transactionsIn.subscriptionAmount` float

The amount the transaction impacted the client's subscription allowance for JISAs or ISAs

* * *

`payments.transactionsOut` array

Contains details of payments out

* * *

`payments.transactionsOut.transactionId` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

* * *

`payments.transactionsOut.transactionCode` string

* * *

* * *

* * *

`payments.transactionsOut.valueDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was created

* * *

`payments.transactionsOut.amount` float

The value of the transaction

* * *

`payments.transactionsOut.subscriptionAmount` float

* * *

`payments.totalIn` float

* * *

`payments.totalOut` float

* * *

`charges.transactions` array

* * *

`performance.transactionsRealised.transferBookValue` float

* * *

`performance.transactionsRealised.nonTransferBookValue` float

The book cost since the in-specie transfer settled

* * *

`performance.positionsRetained` array

Contains a summary of positions retained within the portfolio

`performance.positionsRetained.isin` string

`performance.positionsRetained.assetName` string

* * *

`peformance.positionsRetained.growth` float

The growth of the holding since on the platform

* * *

`performance.positionsRetained.adjustedGrowth` float

The growth of the holding since the book cost

* * *

The sum of the value of realised holdings

request.description:
This command returns the portfolio objects for all clients on the platform

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the client

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of the firm

---

`name` string

The full name of the client

---

`status` enum value

The status of the client account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has viewed and accepted the platform terms |
| `Pending` | The client hasn't yet viewed and accepted the platform terms |
| `Registered` | Skeletal record created for the client from an illustration. Client hasn't viewed or accepted the platform terms |

---

`nodeId` array

The unique identifier of the node that the client is attached to

---

`nodeName` string

The name of the node that the client is attached to

---

`currency` string

The three-letter ISO currency code

---

`currentValue` float

The current value of the portfolio. If no date parameters are provided, this will show as of today's date

---

`accounts` integer

The number of investment accounts in the client's portfolio

---

`uninvestedCash` float

The amount of available uninvested cash across all accounts in this portfolio. This will exclude ring fenced cash that is being used for other transactions.

Important! If a any date parameters is passed, this will no longer accurately represent the amount of available, non-ring-fenced cash.

---

`growth` float

The portfolio's growth since book costs

---

`growthPercent` float

The portfolio's growth since book costs as a percentage

---

`adjustedGrowth` float

The portfolio's growth since assets on the platform

---

`adjustedGrowhtPercent` float

The portfolio's growth since assets on the platform as a percentage

---

item.description: A client's "portfolio" refers to all cash and assets held in their investment accounts, which might consist of multiple tax wrappers and sub-accounts.

item.name: Account

request.description:
This command returns the account summary object for the specified account

#### Attributes

---

`id`

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`firmId`

The unique identifier of the firm

---

`nodeId` string

The unique node identifier that the client record is attached to

---

`name`

The full name of the client, including title, first name and surname

---

`currency`

The three-letter ISO currency code of the account. Currently only GBP is supported

---

`accountType`

The type of account

---

`wrapperType` enum value

The wrapper type of the investment account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `ISA` | Individual Savings Account |
| `JISA` | Junior Individual Savings Account |
| `GIA` | General Investment Account |
| `PENSION` | Pension |
| `TPPENSION` | Third-party pension |

---

`wrapperDetail`

Contains details of the investment account

---

`recurringPayment` boolean

States whether or not there is a recurring payment on the account

---

`recurringOrders` array

Contains details of any recurring order allocation on the account

---

`status` enum value

The status of the account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has accepted the product terms and declarations |
| `Pending` | The client hasn't accepted the product terms and declarations |

---

`clientId`

The unique identifier of the client account

---

`positions` array

Contains a summary of the individual cash and asset positions within the portfolio

---

`positions.id` string

The unique identifier of the position.  
For cash positions consisting of `accountId`|`C`|`position currency`  
For stock positions consisting of `accountId`|`S`|`isin`

---

`positions.postitionType` enum value

The type of position that the values within the array are referring to

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |

﻿`growthPercent` float

object containing details about entity causing the disclaimer
