item.name: Retrieve the live account summary (available balances)

request.description:
This command returns the Live Account Summary (LAS) object for the specified account. The LAS represents the account's available cash and stock balances, which are the completed balances less any in-flight transactions that are being ring-fenced.

Use this endpoint to know how much available cash and stock you have, when calculating new transactions prior to requesting them.

#### Attributes

---

`id`

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`firmId`

The unique identifier of the firm

---

`nodeId` string

The unique node identifier that the client record is attached to

---

`name`

The full name of the client, including title, first name and surname

---

`currency`

The three-letter ISO currency code of the account. Currently only GBP is supported

---

`accountType`

The type of account

---

`wrapperType` enum value

The wrapper type of the investment account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `ISA` | Individual Savings Account |
| `JISA` | Junior Individual Savings Account |
| `GIA` | General Investment Account |
| `PENSION` | Pension |
| `TPPENSION` | Third-party pension |

---

`wrapperDetail`

Contains details of the investment account

---

`recurringPayment` boolean

States whether or not there is a recurring payment on the account

---

`recurringOrders` array

Contains details of any recurring order allocation on the account

---

`status` enum value

The status of the account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has accepted the product terms and declarations |
| `Pending` | The client hasn't accepted the product terms and declarations |

---

`clientId`

The unique identifier of the client account

---

`positions` array

Contains a summary of the individual cash and asset positions within the portfolio

---

`positions.id` string

The unique identifier of the position.  
For cash positions consisting of `accountId`|`C`|`position currency`  
For stock positions consisting of `accountId`|`S`|`isin`

---

`positions.postitionType` enum value

The type of position that the values within the array are referring to

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Stock` | Asset holdings |
| `Cash` | Cash holdings |

---

`positions.isin` string

The ISIN of the asset

---

`positions.assetId` string

The unique identifier of the of asset

---

`positions.instrumentType` enum

The type of instrument this position represents

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Equity` | An equity |
| `ETF` | An ETF |
| `Investment Trust` | An investment trust |
| `Fund` | A fund |

---

---

`positions.assetName` string

The name of the asset

---

`positions.accountId` string

The ID of the account for this position

---

`positions.amount` float

For cash positions, the amount of available cash in the account. This will exclude ring fenced cash that is being used for other transactions.

---

`positions.quantity` float

The current number of available units in the holding, after any units have been removed for ring-fencing. For previously held assets, they will be included in the response with a zero amount of units

---

`positions.currentValue` float

The value of the available position as at the last known price for this asset.

---

`positions.currency` enum value

The three-letter ISO currency code of the position

---

`positions.prices` array

An array of the prices used to calculate the value of the position. See 'Prices' in the platform management section for more detail on the prices object.

---

`positions.currentPrice` float

The current price of the asset – this is the `ask` of the latest price in the system

---

`positions.currentSellPrice` float

The current sell price of the asset.

---

`positions.currentPriceDate` string

The date of the current price in the system. This is the date of the price being used and may be prior to the current date or toDate used (for example when the toDate is a non-trading day)

---

`positions.updateId` string

The unique identifier assigned to the position when it was last updated

---

`positions.minimumTransferUnit` float

The number of decimal places the assets can be held

---

`positions.auditDetails` nested object

Details of when the position was last updated

---

`currentValue` float

The current available value of the account.

---

`uninvestedCash` float

The amount of available uninvested cash in the account. This will exclude ring fenced cash that is being used for other transactions.

---

request.description:
This command returns a summary of transactions that have taken place in an investment account. This includes:

- Payments
    
- Retained Interest
    
    - Where the Interest payable to the account has been retained by the firm due to firm/account configuration
        
    - The value of the interest was never allocated to the account, but this supplies a record of interest payment that was retained
        
    - Retained interest is considered a charge by the regulator
        
- Charges
    
- Income (dividends and cash interest)
    
- Transfers
    
- Internal cash movements
    
- Sell and invest orders
    

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`name` string

The name of the investment account

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier for your firm

The three letter ISO currency code

request.description:
Returns the account objects for all investment accounts on the platform

#### Attributes

---

`id`

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`firmId`

The unique identifier of the firm

---

`nodeId` array

The unique node identifier that the client record is attached to

---

`name`

The full name of the client, including title, first name and surname

---

`currency`

The three-letter ISO currency code

---

`accountType`

The type of account

---

`wrapperType` enum value

The wrapper type of the investment account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `ISA` | Individual Savings Account |
| `JISA` | Junior Individual Savings Account |
| `GIA` | General Investment Account |
| `PENSION` | Pension |
| `TPPENSION` | Third-party pension |

---

`wrapperDetail`

Contains details of the investment account

---

`recurringPayment` array

Contains details of any recurring payments on the account

---

`recurringOrders` array

Contains details of any recurring order allocation on the account

---

`status` enum value

The status of the account

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has accepted the product terms and declarations |
| `Pending` | The client hasn't accepted the product terms or declarations |

---

`clientId`

The unique identifier of the client account

---

`positions` array

Contains a summary of the individual cash and asset positions within the portfolio

---

`positions.postitionType` enum value

The type of position that the values within the array are referring to

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `stock` | Asset holdings |
| `cash` | Cash holdings |

---

`positions.isin` string

The ISIN of the asset

---

`positions.assetId` string

The unique identifier of the of asset

---

`positions.assetName` string

The name of the asset

---

`positions.quantity` float

The number of units in the holding

---

`positions.bookValue` float

The book value of the holding (cost of purchasing the holding) since inception

---

`positions.transferBookValue` float

The number of units multiplied by the price on the day the transfer settled – this will be the same as the `positions.bookValue` if there's been no in-specie transfer

---

`positions.nonTransferBookValue` float

The book cost since the transfer settled

---

`positions.openingValue` float

The opening value of the account. If no date parameters are provided, this will show as 0

---

`positions.currentValue` float

The current value of the account. If no date parameters are provided, this will show as today's date

---

`positions.growth` float

The growth since the book cost

---

`positions.adjustedGrowth` float

The growth since assets on platform

---

`positions.currency` enum value

The three-letter ISO currency code

---

`positions.growthPercent` float

The growth since assets on platform as percentage

---

`positions.adjustedGrowthPercent` float

The growth since the book cost as percentage

---

`positions.currentPrice` float

The current price of the asset. This is the `ask` of the latest price in the system

---

`positions.currentPriceDate` string

The date of the current price in the system

---

`positions.minimumTransferUnit` float

The number of decimal places the assets can be held

---

`positions.allocation` float

The percentage allocation of the holding within the investment account

---

`bookValue` float

The sum of the `positions.bookValue` in the `positions` array

---

`nonTransferBookValue` float

The sum of the `positions.nonTransferBookValue` in the `positions` array

---

`openingValue` float

The opening value of the account. If no date parameters are provided, this will show as 0

---

`currentValue` float

The current value of the account. If no date parameters are provided, this will show as of today's date

---

`uninvestedCash` float

The amount of cash in the account

---

`closingCashValue` float

The amount of cash in the account

---

`growth` float

The growth since book costs

---

`adjustedGrowth` float

The growth since assets on platform

---

`growthPercent` float

The growth since book costs as percentage

---

`adjustedGrowthPercent` float

The growth since assets on platform as percentage

---

`transferValue` float

The sum of the `transferValue` within the `positions` array

---

item.name: Cash and stock postings

request.description:
This command returns the transaction types. The transaction codes can be used to filter the `/posting/cash` and `/posting/stock` endpoints.

#### Attributes

* * *

`id` enum value

The transaction code

* * *

`name` enum value

The name of the transaction

* * *

`transactionType` enum value

The type of transaction

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| Cash |
| Order |
| Notional |
| Payment |
| Product transfer |
| Stock transfer |

* * *

`transactionSubType` enum value

`movementType` enum value

The movement of the cash or assets

* * *

`accountReportGroup` string

Indicates what category the transaction relates

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| `Payments In` |
| `Payments Out` |
| `Charges` |
| `Income` |
| `Transactions Realised` |
| `Investments Realised in Period` |
| `Transfers In` |
| `Transfers Out` |
| `Internal Transfers Out` |
| `Internal Transfers In` |
| `Product Transfers in` |
| `N/A` |

* * *

`products` array

Specifies which wrapper types can support the transaction

* * *

`cgt` boolean

Indicates whether the transaction could impact the client's capital gains tax

* * *

`subscription` boolean

Indicates whether the transaction impacts the client's annual subscription allowance

* * *

`allowWithdrawal`

Indicates whether the transaction can be withdrawn. This only shows on withdrawal transactions

* * *

request.description:
This command returns the cash posting objects.

#### Attributes

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`nodeId` numerical string

The unique identifier of the node

---

`accountId` alphanumerical string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`accountName` string

The name of the investment account

---

`currency` string

The three-letter ISO code

---

`positionType` string

This will be set to `Cash`

---

`transactionId` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

---

`transactionCode` string

The transaction code, which can be retrieved from the static data

---

`narrative` string

The description of the transaction

---

`postDate` numerical string

The date the transaction completed

---

`valueDate` numerical string

The date the transaction took effect (e.g. an historic date if the transaction was backdated)

---

`amount` float

The value of the transaction

---

`clients` array

Contains details of the client

---

request.description:
#### Attributes

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`nodeId` numerical string

The unique identifier of the node

---

`accountId` alphanumerical string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`accountName` string

The name of the investment account

---

`currency` string

The three-letter ISO code

---

`positionType` string

This will be set to `Stock`

---

`assetId` alphanumerical string

The unique identifier of the asset

---

`isin` string

The ISIN of the asset

---

`transactionId` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

---

`transactionCode` string

The transaction code, which can be retrieved from the static data

---

`narrative` string

The description of the transaction

---

`postDate` numerical string

The date the transaction completed

---

`valueDate` numerical string

The date the transaction took effect (e.g. an historic date if the transaction was backdated)

---

`quantity` float

The number of units

---

`clients` array

Contains details of the client

---

item.description:
Cash and stock posting objects show any completed transactions that affect positions of cash and stocks in an investment account. You can use these endpoints to either show or store these transactions.

Details on the positions webhook can be found **here**.

#### **Endpoints**

``` json
/posting/cash
/posting/stock

```

item.name: CGT report

request.description:
## Download CGT Report

Returns a URL to download the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) report for a specific client as a spreadsheet file.

---

### Endpoint

`GET {{apiRoute}}/portfolio/cgtreport/spreadsheet/{{firmId}}/{{clientId}}`

---

### Path Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `firmId` | string | The unique identifier of your firm |
| `clientId` | string | The unique identifier of the client |

---

### Headers

| Header | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Must be set to `application/json` |
| `fromDate` | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Start date of the CGT report period |
| `toDate` | `YYYY-MM-DD` | End date of the CGT report period |

---

### Response

A successful response returns a `200 OK` with a JSON body containing a `data` object with a pre-signed download URL.

``` json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "C06PCJ3",
    "url": "https://..."
  }
}

 ```

#### Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data.id` | string | The unique identifier of the client |
| `data.url` | string | A pre-signed URL to download the CGT spreadsheet |

---

### Client Attributes

The following attributes describe the client record associated with the report:

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | The unique identifier of the client |
| `name` | string | The full name of the client, including title, first name and surname |
| `firstName` | string | The first name of the client |
| `surname` | string | The surname of the client |
| `language` | enum | The language set at the client record |
| `currency` | enum | The three-letter ISO currency code |
| `nodeId` | array | The unique node identifier(s) the client record is attached to |
| `nodeName` | string | The name of the node the client record is attached to |
| `status` | enum | The status of the client record (see below) |

#### Client Status Values

| Enum Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Active` | The client has accepted platform terms and passed KYC checks |
| `Pending` | The client record has been created, but they haven't accepted terms, set up a password or passed KYC checks |
| `Registered` | A skeletal client record is created from an illustration |

---

### Positions

The response may include a `positions` array summarising individual cash and asset positions within the portfolio.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `positions.positionType` | enum | The type of position (`stock` or `cash`) |
| `positions.isin` | string | The ISIN of the asset |
| `positions.assetId` | string | The unique identifier of the asset |
| `positions.assetName` | string | The name of the asset |
| `positions.quantity` | float | The number of units in the holding |
| `positions.bookValue` | float | The book value of the holding (cost of purchasing) since inception |
| `positions.transferBookValue` | float | The number of units multiplied by the price on the day of transfer |

#### Position Type Values

| Enum Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `stock` | Asset holdings |
| `cash` | Cash holdings |

---

### Notes

- The `fromDate` and `toDate` headers must be provided in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.
    
- The returned `url` is a link and may expire after a short period — download the file promptly after receiving the response.

request.description:
## CGT Report

Retrieves the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) report data for a specific client. The response includes a summary of the client's accounts, current values, book values, and CGT figures covering both realised and unrealised profit/loss.

---

## Path Variables

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `firmId` | The unique identifier of the firm |
| `clientId` | The unique identifier of the client |

---

## Response Structure

A successful request returns a `200 OK` with a top-level `data` object containing:

- **`id`** – The client's unique identifier
    
- **`name`** – Full name of the client
    
- **`firmId`** – The firm the client belongs to
    
- **`currency`** – The client's base currency (e.g. `GBP`)
    
- **`status`** – Client status (e.g. `Active`)
    
- **`clientType`** – Type of client (e.g. `Individual`)
    
- **`currentValue`** – Current total portfolio value
    
- **`bookValue`** – Total book (cost) value of the portfolio
    
- **`growth`** – Overall portfolio growth
    
- **`cgtData`** – Client-level CGT summary:
    - `realisedProfitLoss` – Total realised profit or loss
        
    - `unrealisedProfitLoss` – Total unrealised profit or loss
        
    - `closingGiaStockValue` – Closing stock value for GIA wrappers
        
- **`accounts`** – Array of account objects, each containing:
    - `id`, `name`, `accountType`, `wrapperType`, `currency`, `status`
        
    - `currentValue`, `bookValue`, `growth`
        
    - `cgtData` – Account-level CGT figures (`realisedProfitLoss`, `unrealisedProfitLoss`)
        
    - `positions` – Array of held positions within the account. Each position object contains:
        - `accountId` – The ID of the account the position belongs to
            
        - `accountName` – The name of the account
            
        - `accountType` – Type of account (e.g. `Wrapper`)
            
        - `assetId` – The unique identifier of the asset
            
        - `assetName` – Full name of the asset
            
        - `isin` – ISIN code of the asset
            
        - `currency` – Currency of the position
            
        - `firmId` – The firm identifier
            
        - `positionType` – Type of position (e.g. `Stock`)
            
        - `quantity` – Number of units held
            
        - `currentValue` – Current market value of the position
            
        - `currentPrice` – Current price per unit
            
        - `currentSellPrice` – Current sell price per unit
            
        - `currentPriceDate` – Date of the current price
            
        - `bookValue` – Book (cost) value of the position
            
        - `growth` – Growth in value
            
        - `growthPercent` – Growth as a percentage
            
        - `adjustedGrowth` – Adjusted growth value
            
        - `wrapperType` – Wrapper type (e.g. `GIA`)
            
        - `instrumentType` – Instrument type (e.g. `Fund`, `Equity`)
            
        - `assetInstrumentType` – Asset instrument type
            
        - `assetCountryOfIssue` – Country of issue for the asset
            
        - `openingValue` – Opening value of the position
            
        - `cgtData` – Position-level CGT data:
            - `realisedProfitLoss` – Realised profit or loss (may be `null` for unsupported asset types)
                
            - `unrealisedProfitLoss` – Unrealised profit or loss (may be `null` for unsupported asset types)
                
        - `transactions` – Array of transactions for this position, each containing:
            - `transactionId` – Unique transaction identifier
                
            - `transactionCode` – Code indicating transaction type (e.g. `BUY`, `SELL`)
                
            - `narrative` – Human-readable description (e.g. `Buy`, `Sell`)
                
            - `quantity` – Number of units transacted
                
            - `value` – Value of the transaction
                
            - `postDate` – Date the transaction was posted
                
            - `valueDate` – Value date of the transaction
                
            - `executionTime` – Execution timestamp
                
            - `bookValue` – Book value of the transaction
                
            - `profitLoss` – Profit or loss on the transaction
                
            - `adjustedProfitLoss` – Adjusted profit or loss
                
            - `accountWrapperType` – Wrapper type of the account
                
            - `cgtData` – Transaction-level CGT data:
                - `realisedProfitLoss` – Realised profit or loss (may be `null`)
                    
                - `matches` – Array of CGT matching records, each with:
                    - `matchType` – Type of match (e.g. `SAME_DAY_MATCH`)
                        
                    - `matchDate` – Date of the match
                        
                    - `matchedUnits` – Number of units matched
                        
                    - `matchedTotalBookValue` – Total book value of matched units
                        
                    - `buyTransactionIds` / `sellTransactionId` – Related transaction IDs
                        
        - `disclaimers` – Array of disclaimer objects for unsupported asset types, each with:
            - `type` – Disclaimer type (e.g. `ASSET_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`)
                
            - `text` – Human-readable disclaimer message
                
            - `fields` – Fields affected by the disclaimer (e.g. `["cgtData"]`)
                
        - `prices` – Array of price objects for the asset

item.name: Capital gains scenario tool

request.description:
## Simulator without orders

Retrieves a Capital Gains Tax (CGT) portfolio report for a given account **without** any simulated orders applied. Use this endpoint to get the baseline CGT position for an account before modelling any buy/sell scenarios.

This is the counterpart to the **Simulate orders** endpoint — use this first to establish the current state, then compare against a simulated scenario.

---

### Authentication

Requires a valid API token passed as a request header:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `api-token` | `{{apiToken}}` |
| `content-type` | `application/json` |

---

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountId` | string | ✅ | The account identifier to retrieve the CGT report for |
| `firmId` | string | ✅ | The firm identifier associated with the account |
| `simulatedOrders` | object | ❌ | Pass an empty object `{}` or omit entirely to retrieve the baseline report with no simulated trades |

**Example body (no simulated orders):**

``` json
{
    "accountId": "00DGD9B",
    "firmId": "SECCI",
    "simulatedOrders": {}
}

 ```

---

### Response

Returns a CGT portfolio report including:

- **Account metadata** — `accountId`, `wrapperType`, `status`, `currency`, `fromDate`, `toDate`
    
- **Investments** — a list of holdings with `assetId`, `assetName`, `isin`, `positionId`, `bookValue`, `allocation`, `quantity`, `value`, `realisedProfitLoss`, `price`, and any applicable `disclaimers`
    
- **Totals** — aggregate `value`, `bookValue`, and `realisedProfitLoss` across all holdings
    
- **Disclaimers** — any asset-level warnings (e.g. unsupported asset types for CGT calculation)
    

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

request.description:
## Simulate orders

Simulates one or more sell orders against an account and returns a projected Capital Gains impact, showing the estimated impact on the account without executing any real trades.

This is useful for modelling the tax implications of potential trades before committing to them.

---

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountId` | string | ✅ | The ID of the account to simulate orders for |
| `firmId` | string | ✅ | The ID of the firm the account belongs to |
| `simulatedOrders` | object | ✅ | A map of asset IDs to order details (see below) |

#### `simulatedOrders` — per asset

Each key in `simulatedOrders` is an **asset ID** (e.g. `28PPL`), and the value is an object with the following fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | number | ✅ | The number of units or the monetary amount to trade |
| `unitType` | string | ✅ | Either `"Quantity"` (number of units) or `"Value"` (monetary amount) |
| `movementType` | string | ✅ | Either `"Sell"` |

#### Example request body

``` json
{
    "accountId": "00DGD9B",
    "firmId": "SECCI",
    "simulatedOrders": {
        "28PPL": {
            "unit": 1,
            "unitType": "Quantity",
            "movementType": "Sell"
        }
    }
}

 ```

---

### Response

Returns the full CGT report for the account, with a `simulatedOrder` object appended to any affected investment positions. The `totals.simulatedOrders` field summarises the overall projected profit/loss, value, and book value of the simulated trades.

#### Key response fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `data.investments[].simulatedOrder` | Projected outcome for the simulated order on this position |
| `data.investments[].simulatedOrder.profitLoss` | Estimated profit or loss from the simulated trade |
| `data.investments[].simulatedOrder.value` | Estimated sale/purchase value |
| `data.investments[].simulatedOrder.bookValue` | Book value of the units being traded |
| `data.totals.simulatedOrders` | Aggregate summary across all simulated orders |

---

item.description:
## Capital Gains Scenario Tool

This folder contains requests for simulating **Capital Gains Tax (CGT) scenarios** using the CGT Simulator API. It is useful for testing and exploring potential CGT outcomes before executing real orders.

### Requests

- **Simulator without orders** — Runs a CGT simulation against an account with no proposed orders. Use this as a baseline to understand the current CGT position for the current tax year without any trading activity.
    
- **Simulate orders** — Runs a CGT simulation with a set of proposed orders included. Use this to model the CGT impact of specific trades before they are placed.
    

Both requests POST to `/cgtsimulator/orders` on the and return a simulated CGT breakdown based on the provided account and order data.

This section covers the balances and valuations of an investor's portfolio. We'll cover:

*   How to retrieve a portfolio summary and report
*   How to generate a list of portfolio summaries
*   How to retrieve an account summary and report
*   How to generate a list of account summaries
*   Cash and stock postings – including how to list transaction codes, cash postings and stock postings
    

### The balance and valuation object

You can retrieve this object to view the current valuation of a client's portfolio, or their individual investment account. This will include a breakdown of the investor's individual asset holdings, as well as the overall performance using the [modified Dietz method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modified_Dietz_method).

Seccl provides growth rates at an investment account level, portfolio level, and individual asset level.

The portfolio and account level growth rates use the modified Dietz method (as linked above), which is a time-weighted calculation that takes into account cash movements.

There are two unique growth rates:

1.  `growth` This looks at growth since the start of time, relying on the `bookValue`
2.  `adjustedGrowth` This looks at growth since assets on platform, relying on the `transferBookValue` (the value of the assets when they arrived on the platform)
    

These growth rates will only differ if an [in-specie stock transfer](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/in_specie.asp) completes on the investment account or portfolio.

You can also retrieve a portfolio or investment account report. This report contains a list of transactions that contribute to the valuation (charges, payments, orders etc).

This section shows you how to retrieve `portfolio` and `account` balances and valuations.

#### **Endpoints**

```
/portfolio/summary
/portfolio/report
/account/summary
/account/report
/posting/cash
/posting/stock

```

item.name: Transfers
The product transfer in object
item.description:
The product transfer in object represents a transfer request into the system.

The individual stock and cash transactions that make up the client's transfer are linked to the Product Transfer. When all linked stock and cash transactions are complete, the product transfer's `transferStatus` updates to `Completed`.

There are three types of transfer in objects:

1. `Product Transfer:`An umbrella object that represents the whole transfer instruction
    
2. `Stock Transfer:` An object that represents an individual stock line within the transfer (one per asset)
    
3. `Payment Transfer:`An object that represents the individual cash line within the transfer
    

Stock and Payment transfers are actually just `portfoliotransaction` objects, like you will have found throughout the API. Later in this section we show how to create these, but they are often created automatically by Seccl when the ceding provider supplies the information (i.e. what investments the account holds and how much cash they have).

A `Product Transfer` can be made up of any combination of single or multiple `Stock Transfer`s and `Payment Transfer`s - it all depends on what assets are already held at the ceding provider, and which assets you can accept on your platform.

Directly below, we describe the `Product Transfer` object for transfer in only.

#### Attributes

`id` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`transactionType` string

The type of transaction. This will be set to `Product Transfer`

---

`transactionSubType` string

The sub-type of the transaction

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `In Specie` | Transfer should take place in-specie |
| `Cash` | Transfer should take place in cash |

---

`actionTag` string

A high-level status hint attached to a portfolio transaction that communicates whether further action is required and who should act. This field is intended to drive UI prompts, client notifications, routing rules, and automated workflows. This may be expanded.

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `ClientActionRequired` | There is an outstanding client action with a ceding scheme |
| `Resubmit` | The transfer has been rejected and should be resubmitted |
| `None` | No outstanding actions |

---

`movementType` string

The movement of the assets and/or cash. This should be set to `In`

---

`accountId` string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`transferAccountAddress` array

Contains details of the client's address sent as part of the transfer instruction. This must match what the ceding provider has on their system for the transfer to proceed

---

`transactions.transferAccountAddress.flatNumber` or

`transactions.transferAccountAddress.buildingName` or

`transactions.transferAccountAddress.buildingNumber` string

The number or name of the client's address

---

`transferAccountAddress.address1` string **Required**

The first line of the client's address

---

`transferAccountAddress.address2` string

The second line of the client's address

---

`transferAccountAddress.address3` string

The third line of the client's address

---

`transferAccountAddress.address4` string

The fourth line of the client's address

---

`transferAccountAddress.country` string

The country of the client's address

---

`transferAccountAddress.postCode` string

The post code of the client's address

---

`previousProvider` string

The unique identifier of the ceding provider

---

`previousProviderRef` string

The account reference number held by the ceding provider

---

`productDrawdownStatus` string

The part of the pension account to be transferred.`No Drawdown` is the only option available for accumulation pensions (applicable to pension account transfers only)

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `No Drawdown` | Uncrystallised portion only |
| `Partial Drawdown` | Crystallised portion only |
| `Full Drawdown` | Uncrystallised and crystallised portions only |

---

`transferValue` float

The estimated value of the transfer as inputted by the user

---

`status` string

The status of the product transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Pending` | Transfer instruction created |
| `Placed` | Transfer instruction successfully received – this should switch instantaneously |
| `Completed` | Linked stock and cash transactions completed |
| `Deleted` | Transfer instruction deleted |

---

`transferStatus` string

The transfer status of the product transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `With Previous Provider` | Transfer instruction awaiting acceptance from the ceding provider |
| `Onboarding Assets` | Transfer instruction accepted by the ceding provided and onboarding of assets in progress |
| `Completed` | Transfer complete |
| `Rejected` | Transfer rejected by ceding provider |
| `Deleted` | Transfer instruction has been deleted |

---

`linkId` string

The unique identifier of the portfolio transaction group

---

`transferSystem` string

The external system facilitating the transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Origo` | Origo Transfer System |
| `ATG` | Altus Transfers Gateway |

---

`transferSystemRef` string

The unique identifier of the ceding provider

---

`previousProviderName` string

The name of the ceding provider

---

`externalIds` array

Contains details of the ceding provider account reference number

---

`externalIds.externalTransferId` string

Ceding provider account reference

---

`transactionDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was instructed

---

`createdDate` numerical string

The date and time the transaction was instructed

---

`statusChanges` array

Contains details of the `transferStatus` updates

---

`autoInvest` boolean

Triggers automatically investing the transfer according to either a model set for the account or recurring orders, with model taking precedence if both are present. Orders get issued based on the the state of the account at the time the payment settles and a position is created. This option is only valid for cash transfers.

If there is no model or recurring order set up for the account, auto-invest of the product transfer cannot be set. To auto-invest the cash transfer, the adviser will need to first add recurring orders or a model to the account, then request the transfer.

---

`partialTransfer` boolean

Indicates whether the pension is a partial transfer. Only applicable for cash transfers into accumulation pension accounts.

---

`amountToTake` float **Required if** **`partialTransfer`** **set to** **`true`**

The amount to take from the ceding account. This should match the `transferValue` above.

If `amountToLeave` is present, this field **must not** be provided.

---

`amountToLeave` float **Required if** **`partialTransfer`** **set to** **`true`**

The amount to leave in the ceding account.

If `amountToTake` is present, this field **must not** be provided.

---

`overrides.firstName` string

Optional field. Allows for overriding the client first names sent to Origo in case of name conflicts with different providers.  
! Only works for Origo transfer !

item.name: Create a transfer in request

request.description:
This command returns the available ceding providers for Origo and ATG.

To reduce the number of rejected transfer instructions, we suggest that you include the data available on this endpoint in your application.

Adding Query Params to the endpoint narrows your search to the relevant ceding providers:

- `transferWrapperType`
    
    - the account `wrapperType`
        
- `productTransferType`
    
    - the Product Transfer `transactionSubType`
        - "Cash" or "In Specie"
            
- `name`
    
    - fuzzy match criteria on the `name` attribute
        
- `status`
    
    - The status of the ceding provider record
        
- `id`
    
    - the ceding provider id
        
- `supportsManuals`
    
    - Shows only ceding providers which support a manual transfer in or only those that will not support it
        
        - "True" or "False"
            

**Please note: The ceding provider list differs depending on the wrapper type and whether the instruction is in-specie or cash.**

---

#### Attributes

`id` string

The unique identifier of the ceding provider

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`name` string

The name of the ceding provider

---

`status` string

The status of the ceding provider

---

`partyType` string

---

`externalIds` array

Contains details of the ceding provider's external Ids in Origo and/or ATG

---

`externalIds.idType` string

The system that the identifier relates to

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Origo Provider ID` | The ceding provider identifier in Origo |
| `ATG Reference` | The ceding provider identifier in ATG |

---

`externalIds.value` string

The ceding provider's identifier in the external system

---

`companyType` string

The type of company. This will be set to `Platform`

---

`auditDetails` array

Contains audit details of the object

---

`transferProviders` array

Contains details of what the ceding provider can facilitate for each system. If this does not exist for a given masterparty object, then it is not available to request a transfer from electronically - please contact Seccl.

---

`transferProviders.providerReference` string

The ceding provider's identifier in the external system

---

`transferProviders.transferProviderName` string

The external transfer system that the information contained in the array relates to

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `ATG` | Altus Transfers Gateway |
| `Origo` | Origo Transfers System |

To submit a transfer in instruction, you can use the following steps:

1. Retrieve the list of ceding providers available – display this as a dropdown in your application
2. Allow the user to select the ceding provider that they wish to transfer from – retrieve the ceding provider Id
3. Instruct a product transfer in
    

---

#### **Some helpful hints**

Transfer in instructions are validated on two things:

1. The ceding account reference provided in the transfer instruction exactly matches the actual ceding account reference
2. The client's address provided in the transfer instruction exactly matches the client address held by the ceding provider
    

If either of these are incorrect, the transfer will be instantly rejected.

Transfer instructions can also be rejected due to insufficient cash on the investment account or pending transactions.

---

item.name: Update a single transfer's book value

request.description:
You can update the book value of a single "Stock Transfer - External/Migration" transaction using this endpoint.

If `bookValue` is set to `auto`, then it will be set to the current `transferValue`.

If the transfer has not been completed, the `bookValue` will be re-calculated and set to `transferValue` when it does.

When a float `bookValue` is provided, the transaction and corresponding account position will be updated to the new value.

If successful, this request will trigger the below actions depending on the `status` of the transaction:

- For transactions at `status` `Pending` or `Completed`:
    - updates the `bookValue` of the Stock Transfer transaction to the value given in the request
    - updates or adds the transaction's `autoSetBookValue` field to `true` or `false` depending on whether `auto` was passed as the `bookValue`
- And only if the transaction is at `status` `Completed`:
    - updates the related Portfolio Position transaction's `value` to the number given in the request (or the transfer value if `auto`)

### Parameters

---

`bookValue` float | 'auto' **Required**  
The mechanism to use when updating bookValue. Accepts either a value or 'auto' to instruct the system to calculate the bookValue automatically.

---

This command returns a successful array. You can update the book value of many stock transactions in a single request.

Please see the documentation for updating the book value of a single transfer for more information on the effect of the `bookValue` parameter.

#### Parameters

`transactions` array **Required**

Contains details of the stock transfer transactions to updated

---

`transactions.id` string **Required**

The unique identifier of the stock transaction

---

`transactions.firmId` string **Required**

The unique identifier of your firm

item.description:
Book costs describe the the price the investor originally paid for the holding they have currently. Ceding providers don't always provide book costs of assets for in-specie transfers. This information is particularly important for GIAs, where any realised gains could be applicable for [Capital Gains Tax.](https://www.gov.uk/capital-gains-tax)

**Please note: book costs can only be amended when the** **`Stock Transfer`** **transaction is at** **`Placed`** **,** **`Pending`** **or** **`Completed`** **status.**

To update the book value of stock transactions, you can follow the below steps:

1. Retrieve stock transaction Ids and stock transaction updateIds
2. Update the book values – this data must be provided by the investor, adviser or ceding provider.

item.name: The product transfer out object
item.description:
The product transfer out object represents a transfer request out from the system.

The individual cash transactions or sell orders that make up the client's transfer are linked to the Product Transfer. When all linked orders and cash transactions are complete, the product transfer's `transferStatus` updates to `Completed`.

There are three types of transfer in objects:

1. `Product Transfer:`An umbrella object that represents the whole transfer instruction
2. `Payment Transfer:`An object that represents the individual cash line within the transfer
3. `Order:`An object that represents the individual sell orders within the transfer (only applicable in a sell and transfer out group)
    

Payment transfers and orders are actually just `portfoliotransaction` objects, like you will have found throughout the API. Later in this section we show how to create these.

A `Product Transfer` can be made up of any combination of single `Payment Transfer` (standard cash transfer out) or single `Payment Transfer` and multiple sell `Order` (sell and transfer out)

Directly below, we describe the `Product Transfer` object for transfer out only.

#### Attributes

`id` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`transactionType` string

The type of transaction. This will be set to `Product Transfer`

---

`transactionSubType` string

The sub-type of the transaction

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Cash` | Transfer should take place in cash |

---

`movementType` string

The movement of the cash. This should be set to `Out`

---

`accountId` string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`receivingProvider` string

The unique identifier of the receiving provider

---

`receivingProviderRef` string

The reference to denote the transfer

---

`status` string

The status of the product transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Pending` | Transfer instruction created |
| `Completed` | Transfer completed |
| `Deleted` | Transfer instruction deleted |

---

`transferStatus` string

The transfer status of the product transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Awaiting sell down` | Waiting for the linked sell orders to settle |
| `Pending` | Transfer instruction created |
| `Completed` | Transfer complete |
| `Deleted` | Transfer instruction deleted |

---

`linkId` string

The unique identifier of the portfolio transaction group

---

`transferSystem` string

The external system facilitating the transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Manual` | Transfers out are currently all set to Manual |

---

`receivingProviderName` string

The name of the receiving provider

---

`transactionDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was instructed

---

`createdDate` numerical string

The date and time the transaction was instructed

---

`statusChanges` array

Contains details of the `status` and `transferStatus` updates

---

item.description:
To submit a transfer out instruction, you can use the following steps:

1. Retrieve the list of receiving providers available – display this as a dropdown in your application
2. Allow the user to select the receiving provider that they wish to transfer to – retrieve the receiving provider Id
3. Instruct a product transfer out with the payment transfer out
    

---

#### **Some helpful hints**

The accountId must be the same in all transactions within the portfolio transaction group. If this is incorrect, the product transfer will be automatically rejected.

Additionally, transfer out instructions can also be rejected due to:

1. Insufficient cash on the investment account
2. Pending transactions
3. Invalid receivingProvider
4. Non active account
    

After instructing a transfer out, the account status is updated to “Transfer Out”. Other transactions cannot be posted to the account to ensure we do not use the cash position whilst the transfer out is in progress.

The account status is **automatically** updated following the completion of the transfer out based on the account position.

- If the account still has cash / assets left after the transfer out, the account status will be reverted back to "Active"
- If no balance left in the account after transfering out, e.g. after instructing a full sell and transfer out, the account status will be updated to "Suspended".
    

---

        1. amount of transfer out

#### **Some helpful hints**

The accountId must be the same in all transactions within the portfolio transaction group. If this is incorrect, the product transfer will be automatically rejected.

Additionally, transfer out instructions can also be rejected due to:

1. Insufficient cash on the investment account
2. Pending transactions
3. Invalid receivingProvider
4. Non active account
    

After instructing a transfer out, the account status is updated to “Transfer Out”. Other transactions cannot be posted to the account to ensure we do not use the cash position whilst the transfer out is in progress.

The account status is **automatically** updated following the completion of the transfer out based on the account position.

- If the account still has cash / assets left after the transfer out, the account status will be reverted back to "Active"

item.name: Transfers workbench

request.description:
This command returns the product transfer object of all transfers processed on the platform.

The endpoint can be filtered by different parameters to allow you to build specific workflows to monitor transfers within your application.

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the `Product Transfer`

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`accountId` string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`transactionType` string

The type of transaction - this will be set to `Product Transfer`

---

`transactionSubType` string

The sub-type of the transaction - this will be set to `Cash` for cash transfers or `In Specie` for in-specie transfers

---

`movementType` string

The movement of cash or assets - this will be set to `In`

---

`transferAccountAddress` array

Contains details of the address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.flatNumber` array

The flat number of the client held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.buildingName` string

The building name of the client held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.buildingNumber` string

The building number of the client held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.address1` string

The first line of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.address2` string

The second line of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.country` string

The country of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.postCode` alphanumerical string

The post code of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`previousProvider` alphanumerical string

The unique code for the ceding provider as stored in Seccl's system

---

`previousProviderRef` alphanumerical string

The account reference of the account held by the ceding provider

---

`transferValue` float

The estimated value of the transfer as entered by the user instructing it

---

`status` string

The transaction status of the transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Completed` | All linked `Cash` and `Stock` transactions are complete |
| `Pending` | Instruction created |
| `Placed` | Instruction successfully sent to the transfer provider – this is an automated flow and happens instantly |
| `Deleted` | Instruction deleted |

---

`transferStatus` string

This can be used to show the progress of the transfer in your application

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `With Previous Provider` | Instruction sent to ceding provider and awaiting for them to accept |
| `Onboarding Assets` | Instruction accepted by ceding provider and re-registration requests sent for stock transfers - this only applies to in-specie transfers |
| `Completed` | Transfer completed - all stock and cash settled |
| `Rejected` | Instruction rejected by ceding provider |

---

`linkId` string

The unique identifier of transactions in the group

---

`transactionDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was instructed

---

`nodeId` numerical string

The unique identifier of the node attached to the client

---

`createdDate` numerical string

The date and time the transaction was instructed

---

`statusChanges` array

Contains details of the each time the `transferStatus` is updated

---

`wrapperType` string

The wrapper type of the account

---

`clientName` string

The name of the client

---

`clientId` string

The unique identifier of the client

---

`actionRequired` boolean

Indicates whether book costs need to be added

This will have a value of `true` when there are any`Stock Transfers In` (either `transactionSubType` `External` or `Migration`) linked to the Product Transfer by a linkId, that meet both of the following criteria:

- The `bookValue` is `0.00`
- The `autoSetBookValue` is either `false` or `null`
    

In all other scenarios this will have a value of `false`

---

`estimatedValue` float

The estimated value based on the valuation provided by the ceding provider

---

item.name: Retrieve stock transfers in the product transfer

request.description:
This command returns the stock transfer transactions of the product transfer under the given `linkId`.

#### Attributes

---

`id` alphanumerical string

The unique identifier of the stock transfer transaction

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`nodeId` numerical string

The unique identifier of the node attached to the client object

---

`accountId` string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`transactionType` string

The type of transaction – this will be set to `Stock Transfer`

---

`transactionSubType` string

The sub-type of the transaction – this will be set to `Migration`

---

`movementType` string

The movement of the – this will be set to `In`

---

`currency` string

The three letter ISO currency code

---

`assetId` string

The unique identifier of the asset

---

`linkId` string

The unique identifier of the group transaction that relates to all cash and stock transfers in the group

---

`quantity` float

The number of units

---

`bookValue` float

The inputted book cost of the asset

---

`autoSetBookValue` boolean

If `true`: ensures the `bookValue` equals the `transferValue`

If `false|null`: `bookValue` has been set manually

---

`previousProvider` string

The unique code for the ceding provider as stored in Seccl's system

---

`status` string

The status of the transaction

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Completed` | Units posted to investment account |
| `Pending` | Awaiting units |
| `Deleted` | Transaction deleted |

---

`transferDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was instructed

---

`assetName` string

The name of the asset

---

`isin` string

The ISIN of the asset

---

`instrumentType` string

The type of instrument

| **Enum value** |
| --- |
| Fund |
| Investment Trust |
| ETF |
| Equity |

---

`transferValue` float

The estimated value of the transaction if inputted when created

---

`createdDate` numerical string

The date and time the transaction was instructed

---

`auditDetails` array

Contains audit details

---

`updateId` string

The unique identifier assigned to the transaction when it was last updated – this should be used when adding book costs

---

request.description:
This command will allow you to retrieve all linked stock transactions for the product transfer in question.

Within the user interface, our flow for our advisors is:

- Get and display all product transfers
- If you click into one of the product transfers you then see all the stock transfers
- If the stock transfers are pending, you are able to update the book value (see the next request)
    

Fields you might find on different transaction types returned by this endpoint:

This command returns the stock transfer transactions of the product transfer under the given `linkId`.

#### Attributes

---

`id` alphanumerical string

The unique identifier of the stock transfer transaction

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

The unique identifier of the node attached to the client object

The unique identifier of the investment account

The three letter ISO currency code

`auditDetails` array

request.description:
This command returns the product transfer object of all transfers processed on the platform.

The endpoint can be filtered by different parameters to allow you to build specific workflows to monitor transfers within your application.

A Joint GIA transfer can be distinguished from an individual GIA transfer by the presence of the `primaryClientId` property.

#### Attributes

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the `Product Transfer`

---

`firmId` string

The unique identifier of your firm

---

`primaryClientId` string

If account is a joint GIA, `primaryClientId` is required, the `primaryClientId` can be either clients that are linked to the GIA, it does not need to be the client assigned to lead client.

---

`accountId` string

The unique identifier of the investment account

---

`transactionType` string

The type of transaction - this will be set to `Product Transfer`

---

`transactionSubType` string

The sub-type of the transaction - this will be set to `Cash` for cash transfers or `In Specie` for in-specie transfers

---

`movementType` string

The movement of cash or assets - this will be set to `In`

---

`transferAccountAddress` array

Contains details of the address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.flatNumber` array

The flat number of the client held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.buildingName` string

The building name of the client held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.buildingNumber` string

The building number of the client held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.address1` string

The first line of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.address2` string

The second line of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.country` string

The country of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`transferAccountAddress.postCode` alphanumerical string

The post code of the client's address held by the ceding provider

---

`previousProvider` alphanumerical string

The unique code for the ceding provider as stored in Seccl's system

---

`previousProviderRef` alphanumerical string

The account reference of the account held by the ceding provider

---

`transferValue` float

The estimated value of the transfer as entered by the user instructing it

---

`status` string

The transaction status of the transfer

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `Completed` | All linked `Cash` and `Stock` transactions are complete |
| `Pending` | Instruction created |
| `Placed` | Instruction successfully sent to the transfer provider – this is an automated flow and happens instantly |
| `Deleted` | Instruction deleted |

---

`transferStatus` string

This can be used to show the progress of the transfer in your application

| **Enum value** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| `With Previous Provider` | Instruction sent to ceding provider and awaiting for them to accept |
| `Onboarding Assets` | Instruction accepted by ceding provider and re-registration requests sent for stock transfers - this only applies to in-specie transfers |
| `Completed` | Transfer completed - all stock and cash settled |
| `Rejected` | Instruction rejected by ceding provider |

---

`linkId` string

The unique identifier of transactions in the group

---

`transactionDate` numerical string

The date the transaction was instructed

---

`nodeId` numerical string

The unique identifier of the node attached to the client

---

`createdDate` numerical string

The date and time the transaction was instructed

---

`statusChanges` array

Contains details of the each time the `transferStatus` is updated

---

`wrapperType` string

The wrapper type of the account

---

`clientName` string

The name of the client who has been nominated as the lead of the destination account.

---

`clientId` string

The unique identifier of the client who has been nominated as the lead of the destination account.

---

`actionRequired` boolean

Indicates whether book costs need to be added

This will have a value of `true` when there are any`Stock Transfers In` (either `transactionSubType` `External` or `Migration`) linked to the Product Transfer by a linkId, that meet both of the following criteria:

- The `bookValue` is `0.00`
    
- The `autoSetBookValue` is either `false` or `null`
    

In all other scenarios this will have a value of `false`

---

`estimatedValue` float

The estimated value based on the valuation provided by the ceding provider

---

item.description:
This section contains requests that can be used to build a transfers workbench in your application – whether it's for your operational team, platform users, or the end investor. This includes:

- Retrieving all product transfers
- Selecting a product transfer and viewing the linked cash or stock transfers
- Updating the book costs of stock holdings included in the transfer
    

The Seccl transfers workbench aims to provide greater transparency of inflight cash and in-specie transfers instructed from other platforms (the ceding provider) to your platform.

The status updates can be made available in your application to allow clients or platform users to monitor the progress of the product transfer from initial instruction through to completion.

There are seven possible `transferStatus` for transfers

1. `With Previous Provider:`Transfer _**IN**_ request has been sent to ceding provider and is awaiting acceptance and an account valuation (what assets or cash the account holds)
    
2. `Onboarding Assets:`Transfer _**IN**_ request accepted by ceding provider and re-registration of assets and/or cash is in progress
    
3. `Pending`: Transfer _**OUT**_ has been sent to receiving provider and is waiting for settlement
    
4. `Awaiting sell down`: Sell and transfer out has been made, sell orders have been created but awaiting settlement.
    
5. `Completed:`All stock and cash transfers have `Completed` and been allocated to the investment account
6. `Rejected:`Transfer _**IN**_ request has been rejected
    
7. `Deleted`: Transfer _**OUT**_ request has been cancelled
    

#### **Understanding the operational and technical flow**

There are three types of transfer objects:

1. `Product Transfer:`An object that represents the transfer instruction
2. `Stock Transfer:`An object that represents individual stock lines within the transfer (one per asset)
3. `Cash Transfer:`An object that represents the individual cash line within the transfer
    

A `Product Transfer` can be made up of a single `Cash Transfer` transaction, a single `Stock Transfer` transaction and `Cash Transfer` transaction, or several `Stock Transfer` transactions and a single `Cash Transfer` transaction.

The transfers workbench also has functionality to allow the client or platform user to update the book costs of assets transferred via an in-specie transfer.

#### **Endpoints**

``` json
/portfoliotransaction
/portfoliotransaction/producttransfer
/upload/bookvalue/

 ```

item.name: Create a manual transfer in

request.description:
### Retrieve Available Ceding Providers This command returns a list of available ceding providers from: - Origo - ATG - Seccl’s "Golden List" of manual ceding providers Manual ceding providers can be identified by checking the following fields: - `transferProviders.${wrapperType}.manualCash` = `true` (for cash transfers), or - `transferProviders.${wrapperType}.manualInSpecie` = `true` (for in-specie transfers) By default the search will include all providers whether manual or non manual. For further filtering the query parameter `supportsManuals` can be used to retrieve only manual ceding providers or only non manual ceding providers. The **signature type** of each provider is available in: - `transferProviders.${wrapperType}.signatureType` **Note:** The list of ceding providers varies depending on the `wrapperType` and whether the transfer is _cash_ or _in-specie_. ### Optional Query Parameters You can narrow your results by using the following query parameters: | Parameter | Description | | --- | --- | | `transferWrapperType` | The account’s wrapper type | | `productTransferType` | Type of product transfer: `"Cash"` or `"In Specie"` | | `name` | Fuzzy match filter based on the provider’s name | | `status` | Filters by the status of the ceding provider record | | `id` | The unique identifier of a specific ceding provider | | `supportsManuals` | Used to show only manual or non manual ceding providers:
`True` (To show only manual ceding providers) or `False` (To show only non manual ceding providers) | --- --- #### Attributes `id` string The unique identifier of the ceding provider --- `firmId` string The unique identifier of your firm --- `name` string The name of the ceding provider --- `status` string The status of the ceding provider --- `partyType` string --- `externalIds` array Contains details of the ceding provider's external Ids in Origo and/or ATG --- `externalIds.idType` string The system that the identifier relates to | **Enum value** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | `Origo Provider ID` | The ceding provider identifier in Origo | | `ATG Reference` | The ceding provider identifier in ATG | --- `externalIds.value` string The ceding provider's identifier in the external system --- `companyType` string The type of company. This will be set to `Platform` --- `auditDetails` array Contains audit details of the object --- `transferProviders` array Contains details of what the ceding provider can facilitate for each system. If this does not exist for a given masterparty object, then it is not available to request a transfer from electronically - please contact Seccl. --- `transferProviders.providerReference` string The ceding provider's identifier in the external system --- `transferProviders.transferProviderName` string The external transfer system that the information contained in the array relates to | **Enum value** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | `ATG` | Altus Transfers Gateway. This includes both electronic transfers and manual ceding providers from Seccl’s “Golden List,” as these are processed through ATG internally. | | `Origo` | Origo Transfers System | --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}` array Contains details of what type of transfers can be supported for that `wrapperType` – for ATG transfers, this will include `PENSION`, `GIA`, `ISA`, and `JISA`; and for Origo transfers, this will include `PENSION` only --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.cashSupported` boolean Indicates whether cash transfers are supported --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.inSpecieSupported` boolean Indicates whether in-specie transfers are supported --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.manualCash` boolean Indicates whether manual cash transfers are supported. Manual cash transfers are not supported if it is undefined / false --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.manualInSpecie` boolean Indicates whether manual in specie transfers are supported. Manual in specie transfers are not supported if it is undefined / false --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.signatureType` string The type of documents to provide for a manual transfer | **Enum value** | **Description** | | --- | --- | | `Wet` | The supporting document needs to be sent via post to Seccl | | `Scanned` | The supporting document needs to be uploaded to our system in prior to the creation of product transfer | | `Electronic` | The supporting document needs to be uploaded to our system in prior to the creation of product transfer | --- `transferProviders.{{wrapperType}}.accountReferenceHint` string This can be used to indicate what the ceding provider account reference should look like ---

### Endpoint Description

This endpoint allows users to create a record for a file upload associated with a specific firm. It is designed to facilitate the integration of external file sources into the platform.

### Request

- **Method**: POST
    
- **URL**: `{{apiRoute}}/filestore/manualtransferin`
    

#### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and should include the following parameter:

- **firmId** (string): The unique identifier for the firm to which the files will be transferred. This parameter is required to associate the transfer with the correct firm.
    

**Example Request Body:**

``` json
{
  "firmId": "{{firmId}}"
}

 ```

### Response

The response body will contain a `data` object with the following fields:

- **id** (string): The identifier for the refreshed file upload.
    
- **url** (string): The URL where the file can be accessed.
    
- **fields** (object): Contains additional fields related to the file upload, including:
    
    - **Content-Type** (string): The MIME type of the file.
        
    - **bucket** (string): The storage bucket where the file is located.
        
    - **X-Amz-Algorithm** (string): The algorithm used for the request.
        
    - **X-Amz-Credential** (string): The credentials for the request.
        
    - **X-Amz-Date** (string): The date of the request.
        
    - **X-Amz-Security-Token** (string): The security token for the request.
        
    - **key** (string): The key for accessing the file.
        
    - **Policy** (string): The policy associated with the file upload.
        
    - **X-Amz-Signature** (string): The signature for the request.
        

These properties should be used to securely upload the file to AWS, as demonstrated in **Create File upload (upload file).**

[https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-UsingHTTPPOST.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-UsingHTTPPOST.html)

Example response body:

``` json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "",
    "url": "",
    "fields": {
      "Content-Type": "",
      "bucket": "",
      "X-Amz-Algorithm": "",
      "X-Amz-Credential": "",
      "X-Amz-Date": "",
      "X-Amz-Security-Token": "",
      "key": "",
      "Policy": "",
      "X-Amz-Signature": ""
    }
  }
}

 ```

## File Upload Endpoint

This endpoint allows users to upload files to a specified storage bucket. The request must be made using the HTTP POST method and includes a set of form-data parameters that provide necessary authentication and metadata for the upload process.

{{environment}} must be one of these values:

- `staging` (To access the staging environment)
    
- `prod` (To access the production environment
    

Note that this is an API call direct to AWS and not a SECCL.

[https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-UsingHTTPPOST.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-UsingHTTPPOST.html)

### Request Parameters

- **Content-Type** (text): Specifies the media type of the resource being uploaded.
    
- **bucket** (text): The name of the storage bucket where the file will be uploaded.
    
- **X-Amz-Algorithm** (text): The algorithm used for signing the request.
    
- **X-Amz-Credential** (text): The credentials used for authentication.
    
- **X-Amz-Date** (text): The date and time when the request was made.
    
- **X-Amz-Security-Token** (text): A token used for temporary security credentials.
    
- **key** (text): The key under which the file will be stored in the bucket.
    
- **Policy** (text): The policy that defines the conditions for the upload.
    
- **X-Amz-Signature** (text): The signature that validates the request.
    
- **file** (file): The actual file to be uploaded.
    

### Expected Outcome

Upon successful execution of the request, the server will respond with a status code of **204 No Content**, indicating that the file was uploaded successfully without returning any additional content.

## Portfolio Transaction Group API

This endpoint allows users to create a new portfolio transaction group (in this example a manual product transfer in) by submitting transaction details associated with a specific firm and account.

### HTTP Method

`POST`

### Endpoint

`{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransactiongroup`

### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and include the following parameters:

- **firmId** (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction.
    
- **accountId** (string): The identifier for the account related to the transaction.
    
- **transactions** (array): An array of transaction objects, each containing:
    
    - **firmId** (string): The identifier for the firm related to the transaction.
        
    - **transactionType** (string): The type of transaction (e.g., "Product Transfer").
        
    - **transactionSubType** (string): The subtype of the transaction (e.g., "Cash").
        
    - **movementType** (string): Indicates the direction of the transaction (e.g., "In").
        
    - **accountId** (string): The identifier for the account involved in the transaction.
        
    - **previousProvider** (string): The identifier for the previous provider. - the masterparty.
        
    - **previousProviderAccountType** (string): Indicates the ceding (sending) account type. Only valid for ISA/JISA transfers. Defaults to `Stocks and Shares` if omitted for an ISA/JISA transfer.
        
        | previousProviderAccountType value | Description |
        | --- | --- |
        | `Cash` | The ceding account is a Cash ISA/JISA. Requires the masterparty to have `cedingCashSupported: true` on the relevant wrapper. |
        | `Stocks and Shares` | The ceding account is a Stocks and Shares ISA/JISA. Requires the masterparty to have `cedingStocksAndSharesSupported: true` on the relevant wrapper. |
        | _(omitted)_ | Defaults to `Stocks and Shares` for ISA/JISA transfers. Not accepted on non-ISA/JISA transfers. |
        
    - **uploadedFileDetailsId** (string): The identifier for the uploaded file details. This is only required by manual transfers with an electronic / scanned supporting document needed
        
    - **previousProviderRef** (string): A reference for the previous provider.
        
    - **transferAccountAddress** (object): An object containing the address details for the transfer account:
        
        - **flatNumber** (string): The flat number of the address.
            
        - **buildingNumber** (string): The building number of the address.
            
        - **address1** (string): The first line of the address.
            
        - **address2** (string): The second line of the address.
            
        - **country** (string): The country code (e.g., "GB").
            
        - **postCode** (string): The postal code.
            
    - **isPensionTransfer** (boolean): Indicates whether the transaction is a pension transfer.
        

### Expected Response

The API will return a JSON response including the transaction group ID.

This will initiate the malware scanning of the associated file upload. If the file is found to be malware free, it will be available for download.

item.description:
## Manual Transfer In: File Upload Process

This section explains how to use our file upload functionality—direct to S3 with integrated malware scanning—to support the creation of a **manual transfer-in request**.

### What is a Manual Transfer?

A _manual transfer_ occurs when the ceding scheme requires supporting documentation (e.g., signed discharge forms) to accompany the transfer request. Whether a transfer is considered manual, and what signature requirements are accepted, is determined by the **masterparty**—Seccl’s concept of a ceding scheme.

Seccl maintains a “Golden List” of manual ceding schemes, categorized by their accepted **signature type**:

---

### Signature Types

#### 1\. **Electronic Signature**

- These ceding schemes accept digitally signed documents (e.g., via DocuSign).
    
- The signature must include metadata such as the signatory’s email, IP address, and timestamp.
    
- Once completed, the signed document is distributed as a read-only PDF and provided alongside the transfer in request.
    
- **Important:** Only one PDF document per transfer-in instruction is currently accepted.
    

#### 2\. **Scanned Signature**

- These schemes accept a **physical signature** that is **scanned and submitted electronically**.
    
- **Important:** Only one PDF document per transfer-in instruction is currently accepted.
    

#### 3\. **Wet Signature**

- These schemes only accept **original physical documents with a hand-written signature**.
    
- Documents must be sent **by post** to Seccl’s Bath office.
    
- **Note:** No file upload is required for wet-signature transfers.
    

---

## API Workflow: Manual Transfer In - high level

To initiate a manual transfer via API, follow these steps (examples of each call are shown subsequently):

### 1\. `GET` Available Ceding Providers

- Check the signature type for each ceding provider.
    
- If the signature type is **wet**, no file upload is required.
    
- If the type is **scanned** or **electronic**, you will need to upload a document (see steps 2–4).
    

---

### 2\. `POST` to Get File Upload URL

- This request creates a file record in our system and returns:
    
    - A **pre-signed S3 URL** (valid for 5 minutes)
        
    - Required form-data fields for the upload (`uploadFields`)
        
- Note: The URL allows uploads only via the `POST` method.
    

---

### 3\. `POST` to Upload the File

- Use the pre-signed S3 URL and form-data fields to upload the document directly to AWS S3.
    
- **Important:** This is a direct AWS API call—not a Seccl endpoint.
    
- On success, you will receive an on success, you will receive a 204 response code.
    

---

### 4\. `POST` to `portfoliotransactiongroup` to Create Transfer

- Submit the transfer-in request, including the `uploadedFileDetailsId`.
    

---

## Appendix

You may **re-upload a file** (before submitting the transfer) by calling:

`{{apiRoute}}/filestore/manualtransferin/refresh`

This allows you to replace a previously uploaded file if needed, as long as the portfolio transaction group has not yet been created.

request.description:
## Request Cancellation Endpoint

This endpoint allows users to request the cancellation of a specific portfolio transaction (transfer in) identified by its unique ID. The request is sent via an HTTP PUT method to the specified URL.

### Request URL

```
PUT {{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/action/requestCancellation/{{apiTestFirm}}/{transactionId}

 ```

- `{{apiRoute}}`: Base URL for the API.
    
- `{{apiTestFirm}}`: Identifier for the firm associated with the transaction.
    
- `{transactionId}`: The unique ID of the portfolio transaction to be canceled (e.g., `00008F19P`).
    

### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and includes the following parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string | The unique identifier of the portfolio transaction to be canceled. |
| firmId | string | The identifier for the firm associated with the transaction. |

**Example Request Body:**

``` json
{
  "id": "00008F19P",
  "firmId": "{{apiTestFirm}}"
}

 ```

### Response Structure

Upon successfully processing the request, the API will return a 200 response code if successful, and an error code (with details in the response body) if not.

### Transfer status

- Upon success the transferStatus of the product transfer will move to `Pending cancellation`
    
- When the Seccl operations team have confirmed the transfer cancelation with the ceding scheme they will confirm the cancellation in the Seccl system and the transferStatus will move to `Cancelled`
