### Update Firm Transfer History

This endpoint allows users to update the transfer history of a transaction (product transfer in). It is used to add a, "code" (`Client action complete`) and a "note" (free text field) to the transfer signalling that a client action has been completed - which is then used in our chasing strategy for the transfer.

#### Request

- **Method**: PUT
    
- **Endpoint**: `{{apiRoute}}/portfoliotransaction/action/firmTransferHistoryUpdate/{{apiTestFirm}}/{id}`
    

#### Request Body

The request body must be in JSON format and should include the following parameters:

- **id** (string): The unique identifier for the transfer record that is being updated.
    
- **firmId** (string): The identifier for the firm associated with the transfer record.
    
- **createdByFirm** (string): The identifier for the firm that created the transfer record.
    
- **updateNote** (string): A note describing the update being made to the transfer record.
    
- **effectiveFrom** (string, date): The date from which the update will take effect, formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
    

**Example Request Body**:

``` json
{
  "id": "00008BM7P",
  "firmId": "{{apiTestFirm}}",
  "createdByFirm": "{{apiTestFirm}}",
  "updateNote": "My Update Note",
  "effectiveFrom": "2025-01-01"

]

 ```

item.description:
The transferUpdateEvents array on the the product transfer history object can have enties added to it by seccl operations, the seccl system, and end firm users.

This section describes how an end firm user can add to it.

Transfers describe the process of moving the cash and stock of a client from one platform (or [ceding provider](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/c/ceding-company.asp#:~:text=A%20ceding%20company%20is%20an,against%20undesired%20exposure%20to%20losses.)) to another platform. Assets can be transferred [in-specie](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/in_specie.asp), or as cash.

Currently, the below set of endpoints only allow self serve of

1. cash transfers in
    
2. in-specie transfers in
    
3. cash transfers out
    

If your client wants to do in-specie transfers out, Seccl will likely have been contacted by the other provider, and will contact your firm with the request.

In this section, we will cover:

- The product transfer in object
    
- The product transfer out object
    
- Creating a transfer in request
    
- Creating a transfer out request
    
- Updating book costs of assets for an in-specie transfer
    
- Creating a manual cash transfer expectation
    
- Monitoring in-flight transfers using the transfers workbench
    

Seccl has a direct integration with two external systems for transfers in:

- **Altus Transfers Gateway (ATG):** This facilitates the transfer of GIA, ISA, JISA, SIPP/pension assets as in-specie or cash
    
- **Origo Transfers System (Origo):** This facilitates the transfer of pension assets as cash only
    

Where a ceding provider isn't set up on ATG or Origo, the transfer can be facilitated manually.

Transfers out are currently facilitated manually as well.

#### **Pre-requisites**

Before submitting a transfer instruction, the client must have viewed and accepted the platform terms, and the product terms and declarations of the relevant wrapper. The investment account must also be at `Active` status.

#### **Endpoints**

``` json
/ portfoliotransactiongroup
/ portfoliotransaction
/ masterparty/platform
/ masterparty/transferoutprovider
/ portfoliotransaction/producttransfer

 ```

item.description:
This section shows you how to:

- Check the cash position of an investment account
- Instruct a single withdrawal from uninvested cash
- Instruct a single withdrawal with auto-disinvest
- Instruct a sell and withdraw transaction group
    

### Validation

When using the `/portfoliotransactiongroup` endpoint to submit transaction groups, there are two types of validation error responses you can expect to observe, these are split between:

1. API response errors
    1. These are responses directly from the API after you send a request
2. Exception notifications
    1. Asynchronous handling of errors that cannot be handled by the API response

#### API response errors

These occur when the API can immediately validate the request. You can expect to find errors related to:

- The request format is not valid
- Cannot find the given accountId
- There is insufficient cash for the single withdrawal and no disinvestment has been instructed
    

#### Exception notifications

These occur when the system needs to validate the transactions asynchronously, such as when submitting a group of transactions. This applies whether submitting one or many transactions in a group - the validation of each transaction is processed asynchronously.

You can find further information on viewing and managing exceptions in the **Platform Management / Notifications** section.

You can expect to find exceptions related to:

- Transaction types not recognised
- There is insufficient cash when the withdrawal is triggered after some other transactions completing (e.g. linked sell orders)

item.description:
Recurring withdrawals allow investors to take income from their investment accounts. A single investment account can have multiple recurring withdrawals, which can be instructed on any day. The value configured for auto-disinvest will apply to all recurring withdrawals on the account.

Where a recurring withdrawal is set up with auto-disinvest, the disinvestments will occur five working days before the payment date (unless extended selldown is enabled, see below). This means that any instruction will need to be requested six working days before the payment date if the client wishes to receive the cash that month.

This flow shows you how to:

- Create an investment account with a recurring withdrawal
    
- Update an investment account with a recurring withdrawal
    

### Extended selldown enabled firms:

Some markets can be slow to sell down (for example during international market closures), so firms can opt into extended selldown. When enabled, the selldown for a recurring auto-disinvest withdrawal starts 10 working days before the payment date instead of 5, and the payment out is held until the payment date so the client is still paid on their chosen day. Use the Next Payment Date endpoint to work out the next payment date.

item.description:
Seccl provides a pension through Gaudi.

To move a Gaudi accumulation pension into drawdown and request income from that pension, you can follow the below steps:

User downloads and completes the drawdown request form

1.  User emails the drawdown request form to [sipp@gaudiltd.co.uk](mailto:sipp@gaudiltd.co.uk)
    1.  Client product status should be updated to `drawdownRequested`
2.  Gaudi responds with a Benefit Agreement Letter
3.  User confirms that the details are correct
4.  Gaudi responds with a Benefit Confirmation Letter
5.  Gaudi processes payroll and sends Seccl the transaction details
6.  Seccl uploads the transaction details
    1.  Client product status is automatically updated to `drawdownConfirmed`
7.  Client payslip is available in the message hub  
    

**Please note: to update the client's income instruction, the above steps need to be followed.**

To transfer a drawdown pension to Gaudi pension, you can follow these steps:

1.  User creates a pension account
2.  User indicates drawdown pension – the client product status should be updated to `drawdownRequested`
3.  User instructs the transfer
4.  When the transfer completes, Seccl updates the client product status to `drawdownConfirmed`
    

If the client wants to take income from their pension once the transfer has completed, they will need to download and email Gaudi the completed drawdown request form.

item.name: Next Payment Date
item.description:
You can use this endpoint to determine the date at which you can next expect to receive a recurring payment given the current date, the day of the month on which your recurring payment to occur and the payment type. Depending on these parameters, the next payment date could be this month, next month or the month after that.

### Extended selldown enabled firms:

For firms with extended selldown enabled, `Recurring Auto-Disinvest Withdrawal` uses a 10-weekday processing period instead of 5, counting Monday to Friday with UK bank holidays as working days. This endpoint applies that automatically, so treat its response as the source of truth.

#### **Endpoints**

``` json
/ nextPaymentDate/{{firmId}}

 ```

### Query parameters

#### Attributes

---

`currentDate` string (optional)

Date string (ISO 8601 format) indicating the date from which to calculate the next payment date. If omitted, the calculation starts from the next day, as the current day's run may already have taken place.

---

`dayOfMonth` string (required)

An integer numeric string between 1 and 28 (inclusive) indicating the day of the month you wish to set up a recurring payment.

---

`paymentType` enum value (required)

The type of payment. Different payment types require different processing times and consequently may affect which month you can next expect payment.

| **Enum value** | **Processing Period** |
| --- | --- |
| `Recurring Auto-Disinvest Withdrawal` | 5\* |
| `Recurring Direct Debit Payment In` | 3 |
| `Recurring Payment In` | 3 |
| `Recurring Withdrawal` | 3 |
| `Regular Crystallisation` | 6 |

\* For firms with extended selldown enabled this is 10 weekdays, not 5 (see *Extended selldown enabled firms* above).

This section shows you how to:

- Instruct a single withdrawal from uninvested cash
- Instruct a single withdrawal with auto-disinvest
- Create a recurring withdrawal on an investment account
- Take income from a Gaudi pension
- List withdrawals
    

Withdrawals are processed using [BACS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BACS). It takes between three and five working days from the point of instruction to land in the client's bank account.

The money is paid out to the bank details held on the client record. Where bank details are stored on the investment account, for example in the case of a third-party product, withdrawals are paid out to those bank details.

When a withdrawal is instructed:

- The `uninvestedCash` value decreases by the withdrawal amount
- The `cash` value in the positions array remains unchanged until the withdrawal completes
    

Where a withdrawal is instructed with auto-disinvest:

- The withdrawal transaction is created at a status of `Waiting` and the sells are created with a status of `Pending`
- When the sells move to `Completed`, the withdrawal transaction status updates to `Pending` and is processed
    

**Please note: where a withdrawal is instructed within 90 days of an update to the bank details held on the client record, it is held at** **`Checking`** **status. For more information, please refer to the Suspicious Activity section.**

#### **Endpoints**

```
/ portfoliotransactiongroup
/ portfoliotransaction
/ account

```

The internal cash movement object
item.description:
The inter-account cash movement `portfoliotransaction` object is used to instruct a cash movement between two accounts in a client portfolio.

This is a singular transaction that describes the movement from the `accountId` to the `destinationAccountId`.

When using the `GET /portfolioTransaction` endpoint, you will not find the internal cash transfer if you query for all transactions on the destination account ID.

For example:

- Internal cash transfer is instructed to move cash from `accountA` to `accountB`
    
    - Transaction created with ID `ict1`
        
    - A negative cash movement is recorded on `accountA`
        
    - A positive cash movement is recorded on `accountB`
        
- `GET /portfolioTransaction/{firmId}?accountId=accountA`
    
    - This will return the `ict1` transaction
        
- `GET /portfolioTransaction/{firmId}?accountId=accountB`
    
    - This will **NOT** return the `ict1` transaction (because the `accountId` is `accountA`, not `accountB`)
        

Instead, you should query for `?destinationAccount=accountB`. Generally we recommend you make two calls to retrieve transactions for each account and merge the results:

1. `GET /portfolioTransaction/{firmId}?accountId={{accountId}}`
    
2. `GET /portfolioTransaction/{firmId}?destinationAccount={{accountId}}`
    

Alternatively, to find the specific movements on a given account, use the Postings endpoints in the **Balances and valuations / Cash and stock postings** folder.

---

`id` string

The unique identifier of the transaction

`firmId` string  
The unique identifier for the firm

The unique identifier for the client’s investment account where the cash is transferring from

The unique identifier for the client's investment account where the cash is transferring to

`movementType` string  
Whether the cash is travelling in or out of the investment account – this will be set to `Out`

`currency` string  
Three-letter ISO code for the currency paid in or out of the account – this will be set to `GBP`

The status of the transaction

item.description:
Inter-account cash transfers allow the user to move cash from one investment account to another in the same client portfolio. The transaction will take place immediately, and this creates a single transaction out of the specified account.

We allow inter-account transfers between the following investment accounts:

- GIA to GIA
    
- GIA to ISA
    
- GIA to SIPP
    
- GIA to JISA
    
- ISA to ISA
    
- SIPP to SIPP
    
- SSAS to SSAS
    

This section shows you how to:

- Instruct a cash movement and keep as cash
    
- Instruct a cash movement and invest to model
    
- Instruct a cash movement and invest to a recurring order allocation
    
- Instruct a cash movement and invest to an asset
    

### Validation

When using the `/portfoliotransactiongroup` endpoint to submit transaction groups, there are two types of validation error responses you can expect to observe, these are split between:

1. API response errors
    
    1. These are responses directly from the API after you send a request
        
2. Exception notifications
    
    1. Asynchronous handling of errors that cannot be handled by the API response
        

#### API response errors

These occur when the API can immediately validate the request. You can expect to find errors related to:

- The request format is not valid
    
- Cannot find the given accountId
    
- There is insufficient cash in the ceding account for the transfer and no disinvestment has been instructed
    

#### Exception notifications

These occur when the system needs to validate the transactions asynchronously, such as when submitting a group of transactions. This applies whether submitting one or many transactions in a group - the validation of each transaction is processed asynchronously.

You can find further information on viewing and managing exceptions in the **Platform Management / Notifications** section.

You can expect to find exceptions related to:

- Transaction types not recognised

item.name: Node Switching

request.description:
You can create a node switch request via the API

This request begins the process of moving clients to a new designated node.

This request will move the client, accounts and clientProducts to a new node.

##### Requirements

To be able to instruct node switches, users must have access to the current node clients are members of, and the target node clients are to be moved to.

In addition, users instructing node switch requests must have the `Node Switch` scope.

Clients cannot be moved to a new node if:

- Clients have accounts invested in assets not available to the target node.
    
- Clients that have jointly owned accounts, or JISA accounts, must have all clients listed in within the node switch request.
    
- The client belongs to a client fee group and all members of the group are not included in the request.
    
- Client is of the corporate or trust type or the client is a stakeholder of a corporate or trust client
    

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clients` | string\[\] | Yes | List of client IDs to be updated. |
| `sourceNode` | string | Yes | The node clients are currently |
| `targetNode` | string | Yes | The node where clients should be moved. |

#### Example Request

```
PATCH /v1/client/node/SECCI
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "clients": ["client-101", "client-102"],
  "sourceNode": "1",
  "targetNode": "2"
}

 ```

#### Example Response (202 OK)

```
{
  batchId: "5f4553af-d001-47a0-b30f-eb75e1be8a01"
}

 ```

You can create a node switch request via the API

This request allows retrival of the status of a processing node switch request.

This request will output the status of the overall node switch request instructed.

##### Requirements

In addition to required params, users accessing node switch request status must have the applicable access scope.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `firmId` | string | Yes | Unique identifier of the firm. |
| `batchId` | uuid | Yes | The ID returned from instructing a node switch request |

#### Example Request

```
GET /v1/client/node/SECCI/batchId HTTP/1.1

 ```

#### Example Response (200 OK)

```
{
   batchId: uuid, 
   status: 'pending'
}

 ```

item.description:
Node switching enables you to migrate clients between nodes in your system without manual intervention from our support team.

When you switch a client to a new node, we perform a complete migration of all their data to ensure continuity:

- Client
    
- Accounts
    
- Client Products
    
- Messages
    
- Illustrations
    
- Portfolio positions
    
- Portfolio groups
    
- Portfolio transactions
    
- Valuation snapshots

response.name: Create a trade illustration

item.description:
A trade illustration is a summary of the cost and charges the investor can expect to pay based on the amount invested.

You can generate a trade illustration for a single trade or group of trades using the below request. This will calculate the accumulated charges and growth over the specified period.

## Platform fee structures

The trade illustration uses the `accountId` to look up the account's client(s) and determine the platform charge. If the client has been assigned a platform fee structure (`client.feeStructures.platformFeeId`), the illustration uses that structure's tiered rates for the platform charge in place of the node charge.

The behaviour is automatic — there is no request body field to set.

> **Note**: Only **platform** fee structures flow into trade illustrations. **Adviser** fee structures are not applied here.

#### Error responses

`400` Fee structure with id {id} for firm ({firmId}) not found  
The platform fee structure ID stored on the client record does not match any existing fee structure.

item.description: This section will show you how to retrieve client illustrations.

Our illustration tool makes it easy for your users to produce a simple, personalised illustration. Product illustrations can be generated for GIAs, ISAs and both accumulation and drawdown pensions.

You can create illustrations for new or existing clients. The new client flow can be found under **Client onboarding.**

The length of an illustration is dependent on your client's wrapper type:

- For **GIAs and ISAs**, the length of the illustration is based on the number of periods or "months"
    
- For **accumulation pensions**, the length of the illustration is based on the client's date of retirement, minus the current date. If the date of retirement is in the past then the length of the illustration will be 10 years (120 months)
    
- For **drawdown pensions,** the length of the illustration is based on the age the client turns 100 minus the current age of the client
    

This section covers:

- How to create an illustration for a GIA or ISA
    
- How to create an illustration for a accumulation pension
    
- How to create an illustration for a drawdown pension
    
- How to generate the illustration PDF
    
- How to download the illustration PDF
    
- How to generate product illustrations

## Fee structures in product illustrations

Product illustrations support both **platform** and **adviser** fee structures. They can be supplied directly in the request body, or — for the platform fee — resolved automatically from the client record.

### Platform fee structure

The platform charge for the illustration is resolved in this order (first found wins):

1. `platformFeeStructureId` in the request body (top-level) — overrides everything else
2. `client.feeStructures.platformFeeId` on the client referenced by `clientInfo.id`
3. Standard platform charge configured on the client's node

When a platform fee structure is resolved (from either source), its tiered rates replace the node's platform charge in the calculation.

For **joint GIAs**, when no `platformFeeStructureId` is supplied in the request, the lead client's structure is used (the client supplied in `clientInfo`, not in `additionalClientsInfo`).

#### Supplying a platform fee structure in the request

Add the field at the top level of the request body:

``` json
{
  "platformFeeStructureId": "{{platformFeeStructureId}}",
  "clientInfo": { ... },
  "fees": { ... }
}
```

### Adviser fee structure

To apply an adviser fee structure, supply its ID inside the `fees` block:

``` json
{
  "fees": {
    "adviserFeeStructureId": "{{adviserFeeStructureId}}"
  }
}
```

When `fees.adviserFeeStructureId` is supplied, the server fetches the fee structure and uses its tiered rates as the ongoing adviser charge. Any `fees.adviserCharge` (flat rate) sent in the same request is ignored — the resolved structure takes precedence.

The resolved tiers are surfaced on the illustration response at `firmCharges.adviserCharge[0]` so downstream renderers (such as the illustration PDF) can display the tier breakdown.

> **Note**: Adviser fee structures via the request body are supported on **product illustrations only**. They are not currently applied to trade illustrations.

#### Error responses

`400` Fee structure with id {id} for firm ({firmId}) not found  
The platform or adviser fee structure ID supplied (or resolved from the client record) cannot be found.

item.description:
Every time a trade is completed, you are required to show clients a contract note for that trade. You can obtain the contract notes from our API and display those in your client's message hub.

Contract note generation after a trade is dependent on your application receiving two webhook notifications at the same time:

*   A reconciled payment changing from `waiting` to `completed` status
*   An order expectation changing from `pending` to `completed` status
    

At this point, the `transactionId` for the order is used to generate a contract note using the above `POST` request. Similarly, the **position** of the account is updated to show the completed order by retrieving the account summary.

The result is a successful trading experience for the client, and a detailed PDF in their message hub. For more information on webhooks, check out the **Outgoing webhooks** section.

item.description:
Valuation statements are generated by Seccl on a quarterly and annual basis. This is a regulatory requirement and can be found under [Periodic reporting](https://www.handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/COBS/16/3.html) in the FCA handbook.

- Quarterly statements are generated on the **10th of the first month of the new quarter** for the previous **calendar** quarter
    
- Annual valuation statements reflect the valuation statement of the **past financial year** and are generated on **the 10th of the following month (10th May)**
    

### Eligibility

Quarterly and annual statements are generated by making a bulk request to generate all statements for a firm. Before issuing statemetns, however, the system will look through the clients and generate a statement for every eligible client, i.e. clients who have a non-zero valuation during the period or any transactions during the period. (Note that by default this check is not done for ad-hoc statements.

## Ad-hoc valuation statements

You (as the firm) can request ad-hoc valuation statements via the API. A client may request specific time-framed valuation statement for events such as mortgages.

Ad hoc statements will be generated for clients, regardless of eligibility (see Eligibility above). To override this behaviour, you may supply the `forceEligibilityCheck` to only generate an ad-hoc statement, if the client meets eligibility requirements.

Covers activity during the period specified by the user supplying a 'to' and 'from' date. To product the most up-to-date statement, the 'to' date should be set to yesterday's date. For example, if this report is being run on the 3rd of March, you should select the 2nd of March as the 'to' date to ensure an accurate valuation is produced.

- "nodeId": The node ID of the account.
    
- "name": The name of the account.
    
- "currency": The currency of the account.
    
- "accountType": The type of account.
    
- "clientId": The ID of the client associated with the account.
    
- "status": The status of the account.
    
- "wrapperDetail": An object containing details about the wrapper, including "wrapperType".
    

### Response

The response will be in JSON format and will include a "data" object. The content of the "data" object will vary based on the success or failure of the request.

The webhook will be sent with the following headers:

```
webhook-id: A unique identifier for this specific event message. Use this as an idempotency key to prevent processing the same event multiple times.
webhook-timestamp: A Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the request was sent. You should check that this timestamp is recent to prevent replay attacks.

 ```

The current payloads are defined in the subfolders and will initially be thin events. This means that core fields will be sent and an array listing the properties updated.. When an account is created, all core fields will be returned. When an account is updated, the core fields and a list of updated fields will be returned.

We are open to extension and enrichment to the payloads of the webhooks. Please contact your account manager if you wish to raise potential extensions.

item.name: Webhook best practices
item.description:
This section of documentation outlines our recommendations for building a webhook handler to receive notifications from Seccl. This list is not exhaustive and you should strongly consider all security, performance and resilience aspects that accompany building an endpoint to receive requests. This section will be updated as our recommendations evolve.

## Idempotency

Our webhook service provides "at least once" delivery due to the distributed nature of the system. In rare cases, you may receive duplicate webhook payloads. Each webhook includes a unique `webhook-id` in the request header that remains consistent across retries of the same event but changes for new events.

To handle potential duplicates, you should consider storing received `webhook-id` values and checking against these before processing. This allows you to identify and skip webhooks you've already handled.

## Resiliency

Our system expects acknowledgement of receipt within 30 seconds, after which it will retry delivery.

To avoid blocking this acknowledgement while processing potentially time-consuming logic, many implementations decouple the receipt and processing steps. For example, you could acknowledge receipt immediately and queue the payload for asynchronous processing using a message queue or similar mechanism. This approach allows you to process webhooks at whatever rate works best for your infrastructure without risking delivery timeouts.

## **Verify the sender**

We strongly recommend verifying the signature included with each webhook to confirm the request originated from Seccl. For implementation details, see the step-by-step guide in the `Webhook payload` section.

## **IP allowlist**

All webhook notifications originate from a single, consistent IP address. If your security requirements include IP-based filtering, you can configure your firewall or endpoint to accept requests only from this address. Please contact us for the specific IP details. Note that this only applies in our production environment and the IP address may differ in staging.

## New Webhooks Implementation

**Important:** This section of documentation describes our new, advanced webhooks system for account-related events. This is a separate implementation from our existing webhooks offering and provides enhanced functionality and reliability.

If you're currently using our existing webhooks, they will continue to function as expected. We will be migrating existing webhooks to this new pattern in due course, and we'll provide advance notice and guidance when that transition begins. Documentation for the existing webhook types can be found under the 'Outgoing webhooks' section.

## Standard Webhooks Specification

To ensure a secure, reliable, and consistent experience for all developers, our new webhooks follow the [Standard Webhooks specification](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/). This means you can count on a predictable structure and robust security features including:

- Standardised payload formats
    
- Built-in signature verification
    
- Consistent retry behavior
    
- Industry-standard best practices
    

---

## Webhook secret

In accordance to the specification, secrets should be prefixed with `whsec_` and then the base64 encoding of the secret. This will then be decoded and used as the signing key for the HMAC signature.

We do allow plaintext secrets. Any secrets not prefixed with `whsec_` will be handled as a raw string for signing.

---

## Payload Structure

When an event is triggered, we'll send an HTTP `POST` request to your endpoint with a JSON payload in the request body.

The payload will always contain a standard structure:

- **`type`**: A string identifying the event, with parts separated by periods (e.g., `account.created`).
    
- **`timestamp`**: An ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the event originally occurred.
    
- **`data`**: A JSON object containing the specific information related to the event.
    

### Example Payload

``` json
{
  "type": "account.created.v1",
  "timestamp": "2025-10-10T12:54:51.344Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "A123456",
    "some": "fields",
    "when": "created"
  }
}

 ```

---

## Verifying Webhook Signatures

To ensure security, you **must verify the signature of every webhook** you receive. This confirms that the request was sent by our platform and that its payload has not been tampered with during transit.

We include three custom headers in every webhook request:

- **`webhook-id`**: A unique identifier for this specific event message. Use this as an **idempotency key** to prevent processing the same event multiple times.
    
- **`webhook-timestamp`**: A Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the request was sent. You should check that this timestamp is recent to prevent [replay attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replay_attack).
    
- **`webhook-signature`**: Webhook signature.
    

### How to Verify a Signature

1. **Prepare the Signed Content**: Create a string by concatenating the `webhook-id`, the `webhook-timestamp`, and the **raw, unmodified request body**, separated by a period (`.`).
    
    - **Format**: `$webhook-id.$webhook-timestamp.$request-body`
        
    - **Example**: `msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W.1674087231."{"type":"account.created.v1",...}"`
        
    - 🚨 **Important**: It's crucial to use the raw request body, not a parsed and re-serialized version of the JSON, as even a minor change (like removing a space) will invalidate the signature.
        
2. **Calculate the Expected Signature**: Using your unique webhook signing secret (found in your webhook configuration for that type), calculate an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the string you created in step 1.
    
3. **Compare Signatures**: Iterate through the signatures provided in the `webhook-signature` header. For each signature, compare it against your calculated signature from step 2.
    
    - Use a **constant-time string comparison** function to prevent timing attacks.
        
    - If any of the provided signatures match your calculated signature, the webhook is valid.
        

---

## Delivery and Retries

For a webhook delivery to be considered **successful**, your endpoint must respond with a `2xx` HTTP status code (e.g., `200` or `204`) within **30 seconds**.

Any other response—including a non-`2xx` status code, a timeout, or a connection error—is considered a **failure**.

- **Retry Schedule**: If a delivery fails, we will automatically retry sending the webhook for non-200 status codes 429 and 5xx. We will retry sending up to 14 times across a 47 hour period.
    
- **Disabling Endpoints**: If an endpoint consistently fails, we will notify you and may eventually disable it. Returning a `410 Gone` status code will cause us to disable the endpoint immediately.

item.name: Enhanced transaction webhook data
item.description:
## Overview

When a transaction is created or updated, a webhook notification is sent to the configured endpoints if webhooks are enabled for the firm. The webhook body contains information about the transaction, including its status, type, and other relevant details.

---

## Webhook Body Structure

### Required Fields

These fields are always included in the webhook body:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accountId` | String | The ID of the account associated with the transaction |
| `amount` | Number | The transaction amount |
| `assetId` | String | The ID of the asset involved in the transaction |
| `currency` | String | The currency code for the transaction |
| `executedAmount` | Number | The amount that was executed |
| `executedQuantity` | Number | The quantity that was executed |
| `externalReference` | String | External reference identifier |
| `isin` | String | The ISIN (International Securities Identification Number) of the security |
| `linkId` | String | An ID linking related transactions |
| `movementType` | String | The direction of the movement (e.g., "In", "Out") |
| `quantity` | Number | The quantity involved in the transaction |
| `transactionSubType` | String | The subtype of the transaction (e.g., "Deposit", "Withdrawal") |
| `transferStatus` | String | The status of the transfer |

### Optional Fields

The following fields are included if available:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `externalReference` | String | An external reference associated with the transaction, if provided |
| `accountId` | String | The ID of the account associated with the transaction |
| `amount` | Number | The transaction amount |
| `assetId` | String | The ID of the asset involved in the transaction |
| `currency` | String | The currency code for the transaction |
| `executedAmount` | Number | The amount that was executed |
| `executedQuantity` | Number | The quantity that was executed |
| `externalReference` | String | External reference identifier |
| `isin` | String | The ISIN (International Securities Identification Number) of the security |
| `linkId` | String | An ID linking related transactions |
| `movementType` | String | The direction of the movement (e.g., "In", "Out") |
| `quantity` | Number | The quantity involved in the transaction |
| `transactionSubType` | String | The subtype of the transaction (e.g., "Deposit", "Withdrawal") |
| `transferStatus` | String | The status of the transfer |
| `transferUpdateEvents` | Array of Product Transfer Events | An array of product transfer events. These will show the history of events on a product transfer transaction |

---

### Types

#### Product Transfer Event

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createdByFirm` | String | The ID of the account associated with the transaction |
| `historyType` | String Enum | The type of update. Can be either 'INFO' or 'CLIENT_ACTION' |
| `updateCode` | String | A common string used to give an appropriate high level reason for the update |
| `effectiveFrom` | Date | A date from which the update is effective from |
| `createdAt` | Date | A date at which the update was added to the transaction |
| `updateNote` | String (Optional) | A string used to give a more in depth explanation on the update |

---

## Example Webhook Payload

_Shows all possible fields_

``` json
{
  "creationDate": "2023-09-12T15:30:45.123Z",
  "externalMessageType": "PortfolioTransaction",
  "externalSystem": "SecclWebhook",
  "firmId": "firm123",
  "transactionId": "tx456",
  "transactionStatus": "Pending",
  "transactionType": "Payment",
  "type": "Send",
  "accountId": "acc789",
  "amount": 900,
  "currency": "GBP",
  "externalReference": "client-ref-789",
  "movementType": "Out",
  "transactionSubType": "Withdrawal",
  "linkId": "link123"
}

 ```

---

## Important Notes

1. Only fields with defined values will be included in the webhook payload.
    
2. The ISIN is derived from either `transaction.information.originalIsin` or `transaction.isin`
    
3. Webhook notifications are only sent if the firm has the appropriate webhook service enabled.
    
4. For transactions with a status of `"Checking"`, only the webhook notification is triggered and no further processing occurs.
    

---

## Use Cases

Webhooks are triggered in various scenarios, including:

- When a new transaction is created
    
- When a transaction's status changes
    
- When a transaction is deleted
    

This allows integration systems to stay in sync with the transaction lifecycle and respond accordingly.

You can use the below PATCH request to [https://pfolio-api-staging.seccl.tech/webhook/config/position/.](https://pfolio-api-staging.seccl.tech/webhook/config/position/.) This will set up your position webhook URL and secret:

The format of the data posted by the position webhook will be as follows:

{

 ```

Once you receive one of these data POSTs, you can then use the ID to query the relevant position and process.

To validate the message, we will include a header field called `webhook-signature`. The data will be a hash of the body data sent above. This will be a HMAC SHA256 hash.

The exception webhook fires upon a notification being created.

You can use the below PATCH request to [https://pfolio-api-staging.seccl.tech/webhook/config/exception/.](https://pfolio-api-staging.seccl.tech/webhook/config/exception/.) This will set up your exception webhook URL and secret:

    "secret": "your-associated-secret"
}

 ```

The format of the data posted by the client webhook upon client creation will be as follows:

``` json
{
  "events": [
                {
                    "id": "000000LDJR", // the id of the notification
                    "firmId": "SECCI",
                    "notification": "{{notification}}" // the notification
            ]
}

 ```

The `notification` property will contain the entire entity that has been created.

To validate the message, we will include a header field called `webhook-signature`. The data will be a hash of the body data sent above. This will be a HMAC SHA256 hash.

The transfer rejection webhook is fired upon a transfer being rejected

You can use the below PATCH request to [https://pfolio-api-staging.seccl.tech/webhook/config/transfer/.](https://pfolio-api-staging.seccl.tech/webhook/config/transfer/.) This will set up your transfer webhook URL and secret:

``` json
{
    "url": "your-webhook.url",
    "secret": "your-associated-secret"
}

 ```

The format of the data posted by the transfer webhook upon transfer being rejected will be as follows:

``` json
{
  "events": [{
       "version": 1,
       "reason": "Rejected",
       "updateDate": "2025-05-20T09:17:50.138+00:00",
       "transactionId": "0000NHF7R",
       "transferStatus": "Rejected",
       "accountId": "0352GDH",
       "firmId": "SECCI",
       "rejectionCode": "Active scheme member",
       "rejectionNote": "Ceding scheme confirmed that this member is still active with them.",
       "externalIds": [
           {"externalTransferId": "856696"},
           {"transferReference": "ATI000856696"}
       ]
   }]
}

 ```

The `externalIds` array contains any external and client set references added to the transfer on creation and during processing. `externalTransferId` and `transferReference` are names reserved by the system and should not be used when creating a transfer.

To validate the message, we will include a header field called `webhook-signature`. The data will be a hash of the body data sent above. This will be a HMAC SHA256 hash.

item.description:
Webhooks allow us to notify you when certain events happen, such as:

- **Transaction:** Receive a webhook when a transaction has been created, or when it has changed status (such as pending to complete)
    
- **Position:** Receive a webhook when a position has been updated
    
- **Client:** Receive a webhook when a client has been created or updated
    
- **Exception:** Receive a webhook when a notification is generated, indicating an asynchronous error exception
    
- **Message:** Receive a webhook when a message is generated for a client
    
- **Transfer:** Receive a webhook when a transfer is rejected, notifying the reason
    
- **Account:** Receive a webhook when an account is created or updated
    

To update a webhook configuration you must have the `readWrite` access under the "Firm Management" scope.

Note that our Account Webhooks are new and improved! Please head to this section of the docs to read about how we've made delivery better, along with some comments on best practices for receiving webhooks from us.
